en: Book I · Leaving home to seek the way
zh: 第一卷 · 弃家求道

en: Mist lies on the great river. At the stern of the raft a white-haired ferryman stands, his pole set in the water, in no haste to push—he is listening.
zh: 大河上起着薄雾。筏尾立着一个白发的撑船人，篙子插在水里，却不急着推——他在听。

en: In the sound of the water there is everything: the cry of market-goers, cattle stepping into the shallows, a child's night-wailing far away, and the breath a boy let out at last, after standing the whole night through, when day broke. A thousand voices mingle, and at the end they become one sound, low and steady, as if the earth itself were humming.
zh: 水声里什么都有：赶集人的吆喝，牛蹄踏进浅滩，远处婴儿的夜啼，还有一个少年站了整整一夜、天亮时才吐出来的那口气。千百种声音搅在一处，末了并成一个又低又稳的音，像大地自己在哼。

en: What the ferryman hears is his own life. And that life must be told from far off—from two thousand five hundred years ago, from a Brahmin courtyard upstream on this same river.
zh: 撑船人听见的，是他自己的一辈子。而这一辈子，要从很远的地方讲起——从两千五百年前，从这条河上游的一座婆罗门院子讲起。

en: In that courtyard the shadow of the fig tree moved each day from the east wall to the west. The boy who grew there could recite every scripture, and at the river he could complete the whole rite of bathing and sacrifice. The elders said he would be a priest among priests.
zh: 那院子里的无花果树影，每天从东墙挪到西墙。院里长大的少年会背诵所有的经文，会在河边做完整套沐浴与献祭。长者们说，他将来会是祭司中的祭司。

en: Only he himself was unquiet: in the scriptures, in the offerings, in his father's speech, he could not find the Self he sought.
zh: 只有他自己不安：经文里、供奉里、父亲的言语里，都没有他要找的那个「我」。

en: One evening in the rains, three Samanas passed the village gate. Dust showed their lean shoulder-blades; their eyes were unnaturally bright. They left not a word behind.
zh: 一个雨季的黄昏，三个沙门走过村口。尘土里露出他们瘦削的肩胛，眼睛亮得反常，一句话也没有留下。

en: That night the boy stood before his father's door, and did not move. He stood the whole night through. At daybreak his father let him go.
zh: 那天夜里，少年站到父亲的门前，一动不动。他站了整整一夜，天亮时父亲让他走。

en: Book II · Samsara
zh: 第二卷 · 尘世轮回

en: Three years in the forest of the Samanas taught him fasting, the bearing of pain, and how to send himself out of the body. Hunger could only press that Self smaller; it never dissolved it.
zh: 苦修林里的三年，他学会了斋戒、忍痛、把自己从身体里放出去。可饥饿只能把那个「我」压小，从来没有把它化开。

en: With his companion he went to Jetavana to hear the Perfect One teach. When it was done he bowed to that man, and left alone—doctrine can be given; awakening cannot.
zh: 他和同伴一起去祇园精舍听那位圆满者说法。听完，他向那人行礼，然后独自离开——道理可以传授，觉悟不能。

en: Beyond the river lay a great city: silks, spices, dice, a courtesan's garden, and a merchant house still growing. First he learned to write and keep accounts; then wine, and love.
zh: 过河之后是一座繁华大城：绸缎、香料、骰子、名妓的园子，和一个正在扩张的商号。他先学会了写字算账，再学会了饮酒与情爱。

en: Twenty years passed. He had a house, servants, a room of fine clothes—and new cares: fear of defeat, of age, of losing what he had. Year by year the face in the mirror grew softer.
zh: 二十年过去，他有了宅第、仆人和一屋子华服，也有了新的心事：怕输、怕老、怕失去。镜子里的脸一年年软下去。

en: One morning he left the house and the ledgers and walked toward the river. Only at the water did he find that the voice in his breast had been silent a long time.
zh: 一个清晨，他丢下宅子与账簿往河边走。走到水边才发现，胸口那个声音已经很久没有响过了。

en: Book III · The river made whole
zh: 第三卷 · 河水圆融

en: He came back to the ferry that had once carried him across. The ferryman Vasudeva was still there. He knew him, and asked nothing more.
zh: 他回到当年渡他过河的渡口。那位船夫维稣德瓦还在，认出了他，也没有多问一句。

en: He poled with the ferryman, braided rope, mended oars, and learned to listen to the water. Year by year the river said more: it was at the source, at the crossing, and at the sea's mouth, all at once, and never in haste.
zh: 他跟着船夫撑船、编绳、修桨，学着听水声。河水一年比一年说得多：它同时在源头、在渡口、在入海口，从不着急。

en: Many years later the city's courtesan Kamala came to the ferry with a child, and was bitten by a snake on the bank. She died in the hut. The child remained.
zh: 许多年后，城里的名妓伽摩拉带着一个孩子来渡河，在岸边被蛇咬了。她死在草舍里，孩子留了下来。

en: The boy hated the river, and hated this father who had appeared so suddenly. He would not pole; he would not eat coarse food. One night he took the money and fled toward the city.
zh: 那孩子恨这条河，也恨这个忽然出现的父亲。他不肯撑船，不肯吃粗饭，某个夜里带着钱往城里逃了。

en: Halfway in the chase, Siddhartha saw a face in the water—his father's face, and his own. He turned back to the ferry.
zh: 追到半路，悉达多在水面上看见一张脸——那是他父亲的脸，也是他自己的。他掉头回了渡口。

en: Epilogue · The ferry
zh: 尾声 · 渡口

en: The ferryman Vasudeva put the oar into his hands, walked into the woods, and did not come back.
zh: 船夫维稣德瓦把桨交给他，走进林子里，再没有回来。

en: He kept the ferry alone, and carried people across. Some went to market, some to a burial, some only to look once upon a daughter; the river asked nothing.
zh: 他一个人守着渡口，替人渡河。有人赶集，有人奔丧，有人只是过河去看一眼女儿；河水一句也不多问。

en: Many years passed. An old friend with white hair, Govinda, came to the ferry. He had sought a lifetime and was still seeking; at first he did not know the man at the pole.
zh: 很多年过去，一位白发的老友侨文达来到渡口。他找了一辈子，仍然在找，起先并没有认出撑船的人是谁。

en: Siddhartha bade him look down at the water. Upon it rose a thousand thousand faces: child, old man, fish, the dying, the newborn, flowing away together and flowing back.
zh: 悉达多让他低头看水面。水面上浮起千万张脸：孩子、老人、鱼、垂死的人、初生的人，一起流过去，又一起流回来。

en: The old friend kissed his brow. Tears fell on the boards of the boat, and he himself could not say why.
zh: 老友吻了他的额头，泪水落在船板上，自己也说不清是为什么。

en: “He smiled, no different from a thousand thousand others.”
zh: 「他微笑着，与千万人一般无二。」

en: The next day people still stepped on and off at the ferry. The groove worn by the rope in the post was a little deeper.
zh: 第二天渡口照旧有人上船、下船。木桩上被缆绳磨出的凹痕又深了一点。

en: The city on the bank went on trading; in the forest of the Samanas men still fasted; at Jetavana they still taught; the river still went toward the sea.
zh: 岸上的城市继续做生意，苦修林里继续有人斋戒，祇园里继续有人说法，河水继续往海里去。

zh: （改编自赫尔曼·黑塞《悉达多》。）

en: Book I Gate · Two paths
zh: 第一卷闸 · 两条路

en: Two boys grew under the same banyan; from there the roads divided.
zh: 同一棵榕树下长大的两个少年，从此走上了两条路。

en: The Brahmin prayer-syllable of “perfection,” murmured as if the heart were an arrow aimed at Brahman, is:
zh: 婆罗门祷文的音节「圆满」，默念它时如以心为箭指向梵天，其音为：

en: After three years in the forest, the elder who was hypnotised into bowing and blessing the two young men as they left is
zh: 林中度日三年，两个年轻人告别时被催眠得鞠躬祝福的长者是

en: After the teaching at Jetavana, the one who put on the yellow robe and entered the order is
zh: 祇园听法之后，披上黄衣、皈依僧团的是

en: The holy one to whose face Siddhartha said that doctrine cannot give awakening, and who at parting warned, “Beware of too much cleverness,” is
zh: 被悉达多当面指出「教义无法传达证悟」、临别赠言「提防你过分的聪明」的圣者是

en: The dialogue in which the two friends, divided in what they held true, at last went their separate ways is:
zh: 两位朋友由于理念不同，最终分道扬镳的那段对话剧情是：

en: Book II Gate · Awakening
zh: 第二卷闸 · 醒来

en: Twenty years were one dream of the world. What woke him was not another person, but a bird and a single syllable.
zh: 二十年尘世一梦，叫醒他的不是别人，是一只鸟和一个字。

en: The one who taught him the art of love, who at last set the little bird free from the golden cage and closed her gate to guests, is:
zh: 教他情爱之艺、最后放走金笼小鸟、闭门谢客的人是：

en: The rich merchant of the great city who tested his reading and writing, took him into trade, and could not sleep for gain and loss, is:
zh: 考校他读写、带他做生意、总为盈亏睡不着觉的大城富商是：

en: The gambling pieces with which, in his years of sinking, he staked fortunes to spend his contempt for money, are:
zh: 他沉沦岁月里一掷千金、借以发泄对金钱轻蔑的赌具是：

en: The creature that lay stiff and dead in the golden cage in his dream, and after which he woke and cast everything aside, is that:
zh: 梦中僵死在金笼里、让他惊醒后抛下一切的是那只：

en: In that instant by the river, the ancient syllable that called him back from the edge of death is:
zh: 河边那一瞬，把他从死亡边缘唤回的古老音节是：

en: The tale in which he died once by the river and lived again is called:
zh: 他在河边死过一回、又活过来的故事，叫作：

en: Book III Gate · The river
zh: 第三卷闸 · 河流

en: The one who learned from the river at last heard, among a thousand voices, the one.
zh: 向河水学习的人，终于听见了万千声音里的那一个。

en: The old ferryman who taught him to listen to the river, and at last walked into the woods and into oneness, is 〔 〕.
zh: 教他倾听河水、最后步入林中融入圆融的老船夫是〔 〕。

en: The child who stole the ferry-money from the two-coloured basket, broke the oar, and fled alone back to the city is 〔 〕.
zh: 偷走双色小篮里的船费、折断船桨、独自逃回大城的孩子是〔 〕。

en: When all voices became one, the word the river sang at last is 〔 〕.
zh: 万音归一，河水最终唱出的那个字是〔 〕。

en: The old monk who came to the ferry to be taught, kissed his friend's brow, and then saw all forms flowing, is 〔 〕.
zh: 在渡口求教、吻过老友前额之后看见万相流转的老僧是〔 〕。

en: The tale of two old men listening to the river side by side, when a thousand voices became the sound of perfection, is called “ ”.
zh: 两个老人并肩听河、万千声音汇成圆满之音的故事，叫作《 》。

en: The one this story follows. Son of a Brahmin noble of ancient India, handsome and keen of mind, he left home to seek peace of the heart, and his life rose and fell more than once.
zh: 本故事的主角。古印度婆罗门贵族之子，英俊聪慧，为求心灵安宁离家求道，一生几经沉浮。

en: Son of a Brahmin
zh: 婆罗门之子

en: Birth
zh: 出身

zh: 古印度最高种姓——婆罗门，世代掌管祭祀与诵读经典的祭司贵族

zh: 背得出全部经文，献祭时替父亲执礼，长者们说他将来是祭司中的祭司

en: He had everything and could not be glad: he doubted that bathing, sacrifice, and scripture could give the heart true peace
zh: 拥有一切却无法快乐：他怀疑沐浴、祭祀与经典给不了内心真正的安宁

en: Sickness of the heart

en: The richer he grew, the more he feared losing, age, and death; at night he dreamed of money, and waking to the mirror found a stranger's face
zh: 越有钱越怕输、怕老、怕死；夜里会梦见金钱，醒来照镜子只见一张陌生的脸

en: The wound

en: The day the son fled, he pursued as far as the garden gate at the city's edge, stood a long time, and at last knew he could not bring him back
zh: 儿子逃走那天，他一路追到城边的园门口，站了很久，终于明白追不回来

en: Among the river's thousand voices he heard at last the sound of perfection, and was reconciled with the whole world
zh: 在河水的万千声音里，他终于听见那个圆满之音，与整个世界和解

en: Nature

en: Art
zh: 本事

en: She treated love as a craft that could be taught, knowing some thirty or forty ways; a pupil paid according to custom
zh: 她把情爱当作一门可以传授的技艺，熟知三四十种花样，学生须按规矩付学费

en: The eye that sees
zh: 眼力

en: Through the curtain of her palanquin she glanced once at a barely clothed Samana, and judged him worth the making
zh: 隔着轿帘看一眼衣不蔽体的沙门，就断定这个人值得培养

en: In her heart
zh: 心底

en: She herself admitted she did not know how to love; those who can love are ordinary people, and that is their secret
zh: 她自己也承认不懂得爱人；能够爱的是平凡人，那是平凡人的秘密

en: The loved thing in the cage
zh: 笼中爱物

en: item
zh: item

en: The way she lived
zh: 营生之道

en: concept
zh: concept

en: The last pilgrimage
zh: 最后的朝圣

en: Later years
zh: 晚年

en: She closed the garden gate, dismissed her guests, gave the garden beyond the city to the order, and set out with her son
zh: 闭了园门，遣散门客，把城外的花园献给僧团，带着儿子上路

en: The one she went to see
zh: 朝觐的对象

en: person
zh: person

en: Where the ashes lie
zh: 骨灰安处

en: place
zh: place

en: Cause of death
zh: 死因

en: A black snake in the grass by the road bit her; she reached the ferry and could not rise again
zh: 路边草丛里一条黑蛇咬中了她，走到渡口便再也起不来了

en: Last words
zh: 最后一句

en: She said she had meant to look once upon that holy one, and had found only the lover of former days, and that this too was well
zh: 她说本想去看那位圣者一眼，结果只找到旧日的情人，觉得这也一样好

en: The richest merchant of the great city, a friend of Kamala. Shrewd and anxious, he made trade his life.
zh: 大城最富有的商人，伽摩拉的朋友。精明而焦虑，把生意当作性命。

en: The rich merchant
zh: 富商

en: Appearance
zh: 相貌

en: Hair gone grey, a shrewd and guarded look, a fleshy mouth, a walk that made a wind
zh: 斑白头发，精明而颇有城府的眼神，肉感的嘴唇，走起路来带风

en: Temper
zh: 脾气

en: A single shipment could keep him sleepless three nights; each year a new line marked his brow; he made trade his life
zh: 为一批货三夜合不上眼，额上一年添一道皱纹，把生意当作性命

en: Sickness of the heart
zh: 心病

en: What he never understood, all his life, was the man beside him who held everything in his hands and took none of it in earnest
zh: 他一辈子想不通的事，是身边有个人什么都握在手里，又什么都不当真

en: Who brought him
zh: 引荐人

en: person
zh: person

en: House
zh: 宅第

en: place
zh: place

en: Ferryman at the crossing in the woods. An ordinary man who could not read, yet he knew best the art of listening—he had learned everything from the river.
zh: 林中渡口的船夫。不识字的普通人，却最懂得倾听的艺术——他从河水那里学会了一切。

en: Ferryman on the river
zh: 河上的船夫

en: Appearance
zh: 相貌

en: An ageing ferryman, his face lined with fine smiling wrinkles, few of speech; when he smiled his eyes shone
zh: 上了年纪的摆渡人，满脸细细的笑纹，话极少，笑起来眼睛发亮

en: Hut for travellers
zh: 歇客的小屋

en: place
zh: place

en: The craft that carries men
zh: 渡人之具

en: item
zh: item

en: How he received guests
zh: 待客

en: He would share bread, water, and mangoes with a traveller who had nothing, and did not press for the ferry-fee
zh: 肯把面包、水和芒果分给身无分文的过客，也不催着要船钱

en: A strange saying
zh: 一句怪话

en: He said the river had taught him: water flows out and returns; who ferries a man today will be repaid in time
zh: 他说这条河教过他：水流来流去终会回转，今日渡人，来日自有报答

en: Ferryman
zh: 船夫

en: The ferry
zh: 渡口

en: place
zh: place

en: Apprentice
zh: 徒弟

en: person
zh: person

en: Art
zh: 本事

en: To carry men across, and to hear them speak; among a thousand travellers, only four or five could hear the river talking
zh: 渡人过河，听人倾诉；千万过客里，只有四五个能听见河水说话

en: Unlettered
zh: 不识字

en: He had never read a scripture, and could speak no great doctrine, yet he had lived every word of it
zh: 他一辈子没读过经，说不出一句大道理，却把每一句道理都活了出来

en: The dead wife
zh: 亡妻

en: His wife had died of illness many years before, and was burned on the mound beside the ferry; thereafter he kept the river alone
zh: 妻子许多年前病故，火化在渡口旁的土丘上；此后他一个人守着这条河

en: The listener
zh: 倾听者

en: What taught him
zh: 师承

en: His teacher was the river: it taught him to listen, and that time does not exist in the world
zh: 他的老师是那条河：河水教他倾听，教他世上并不存在时间

en: The sound of perfection
zh: 圆满之音

en: concept
zh: concept

en: What he left at parting
zh: 临别所授

en: item
zh: item

en: How he taught
zh: 教法

en: He never spoke doctrine; he only brought a man to the water and sat with him—what is spoken is leftover rice; what is tasted is the meal
zh: 他从不讲道理，只把人带到水边一起坐着——讲出来的是剩饭，尝到的才是饭

en: Farewell
zh: 告别

en: When his friend had heard the sound of perfection, he walked into the woods and into the oneness of all things
zh: 等老友听见了圆满之音，他便步入林中，融入万物的圆融统一

en: Son of Kamala and Siddhartha, eight years old. Raised in wealth and indulged by his mother, proud and rebellious.
zh: 伽摩拉与悉达多的儿子，八岁。在富贵中被母亲惯大，骄纵而叛逆。

en: The spoiled child
zh: 惯坏的孩子

en: Mother
zh: 母亲

en: person
zh: person

en: What he took when he fled
zh: 逃走时带走的

en: item
zh: item

en: Origins
zh: 来历

en: Eight years old, raised in a house of the great city, used to fine food and a soft bed, a servant running at the lift of a hand
zh: 八岁，在大城的宅子里长大，吃惯美食软床，一抬手就有仆人跑来

en: Temper
zh: 脾气

en: He would not work, he offended his elders, he smashed the rice bowl, and took his father's patience for the most hateful of devices
zh: 拒绝做工，冒犯长辈，摔碎米饭碗，把父亲的宽容当成最可恨的手段

en: Where he went
zh: 去向

en: He broke the oar, rowed across, and went toward the city; thereafter no one spoke of where he was
zh: 他折断船桨，划船过了河，往大城去了；此后再没有人提起他的下落

en: Siddhartha's father, an honoured Brahmin priest. His bearing was calm and noble; he loved his son deeply, and could not keep him.
zh: 悉达多的父亲，可敬的婆罗门祭司。举止从容高贵，深爱儿子却留不住他。

en: Brahmin priest
zh: 婆罗门祭司

en: Station
zh: 身份

en: concept
zh: concept

en: Dwelling
zh: 居所

en: place
zh: place

en: The man he was
zh: 为人

en: His bearing was calm and noble; he never raised his voice; the whole town believed his life lacked nothing
zh: 举止从容高贵，说话从不高声；全城的人都以为他此生再无缺憾

en: That night
zh: 那一夜

en: Three times in the night he rose and saw his son still standing outside the door; at daybreak he said: Go, go into the woods
zh: 他半夜三次起身，看见儿子还站在门外；天亮时他说：去吧，去林子里

en: The eldest Samana in the forest of austerities, nearly sixty and still without Nirvana. Severe, quick to anger.
zh: 苦修林中最年长的沙门，近六十岁仍未证得涅槃。严厉、易怒。

en: Elder of the forest
zh: 丛林长老

en: Place of practice
zh: 修行地

en: place
zh: place

en: The austerity of a lifetime
zh: 一生守持的苦行

en: concept
zh: concept

en: Age
zh: 年纪

en: Nearly sixty, he had practised in the woods a lifetime, and still had not arrived where he meant to go
zh: 年近六十，在林中修了一辈子，仍旧没有抵达他要去的那个地方

en: How it ended
zh: 结局

en: When two disciples would leave, he raged; one of them held his eyes, and he bowed instead and blessed them
zh: 两个弟子要走，他大发雷霆；被其中一个盯住眼睛，反倒躬身为他们祝福

en: The house where Siddhartha was born and grew. Courtyard, hall of scripture, and the sacrificial fire—a Brahmin priest's dwelling.
zh: 悉达多出生与长大的家。庭院、经堂与祭火，婆罗门祭司的宅第。

en: Stone steps on the riverbank at the town's edge. Brahmins bathe here each day, praying to be washed of sin.
zh: 城边的河岸石阶。婆罗门每天在此沐浴净身，祈求洗清罪孽。

en: The bathing place by the river
zh: 河畔的沐浴场

en: Caste of those who bathe
zh: 沐浴者的种姓

en: concept
zh: concept

en: Use
zh: 用途

en: The high caste bathe here each day, reciting prayers, asking to be washed of sin
zh: 高种姓每天在此沐浴净身，念诵祷词，祈求洗清罪孽

en: An old matter
zh: 一件旧事

en: In boyhood he came each day and completed the whole office, until one day he doubted that water washed anything away
zh: 少年时他每天来做完整套功课，直到有一天怀疑水洗不掉什么

en: The great banyan beyond the town. Two boys often sat in its shade to meditate, murmuring the syllable Om.
zh: 城外的大榕树。两个少年常在树荫下打坐冥想，默念「唵」字真言。

en: The banyan outside town
zh: 城外的榕树

en: The friend who swore beneath the tree
zh: 树下立誓的朋友

en: person
zh: person

en: Appearance
zh: 样子

en: The great banyan beyond the town, its aerial roots hanging to the ground; under its shade it was cool the year round
zh: 城外那棵大榕树，气根一直垂到地上，树荫底下常年凉快

en: What happened here
zh: 发生过什么

en: Two boys often sat here and murmured the holy sound; here too one of them said that he would go
zh: 两个少年常在这里打坐默念圣音；也是在这里，其中一个说出了要走

en: The jungle where the Samanas dwelt. Here the ascetics tempered themselves with hunger, the sun, and thorns.
zh: 沙门们栖身的丛林。在这里，苦行者以饥饿、暴晒与荆棘磨炼自己。

en: The great city where the Buddha stayed and taught. Every house was willing to fill a monk's bowl with food.
zh: 佛陀驻锡讲法的大城。城里家家都愿意给僧侣的钵盂盛满饭食。

en: Jetavana—the grove monastery a rich merchant bought and gave to the Buddha. Monks gathered there like a little town.
zh: 祇树给孤独园——富商买下献给佛陀的园林精舍。僧侣云集，像一个小市镇。

en: Jetavana
zh: 祇园

en: Dedicated to whom
zh: 献给谁

en: person
zh: person

en: The city around it
zh: 所在大城

en: place
zh: place

en: How it came to be
zh: 由来

en: A wealthy elder bought the whole grove and gave it to the holy one he followed, and to the order
zh: 一位富有的长者买下整片园林，献给他所信奉的圣者与僧团

en: The look of the place
zh: 光景

en: Deep shade, monks as numerous as cloud, like a little town: some sat silent in stillness, some argued fiercely
zh: 园里浓荫蔽日、僧侣如云，像一座小市镇：有人默坐入定，有人激烈论辩

en: The ferryman's little hut by the river. Travellers may sleep there; inside are bread, water, and mangoes.
zh: 船夫的河边小草屋。过客可以借宿，屋里有面包、水和芒果。

en: The prosperous city where Siddhartha sank for many years. Shops, gaming, feasts—the playground of the world.
zh: 悉达多沉沦多年的繁华大城。商铺、赌局、宴饮——尘世的游乐场。

en: Kamala's garden villa beyond the city. Trees and flowers in plenty; deep in the pavilion hung a little golden cage.
zh: 伽摩拉城外的园林别墅。花木葱茏，亭子深处挂着一只小小的金笼。

en: The courtesan's garden
zh: 名妓的园林

en: The look of the place
zh: 光景

en: A garden villa beyond the city, trees and flowers in plenty; deep in the pavilion hung a little golden cage
zh: 城外的园林别墅，花木葱茏，亭子深处挂着一只小小的金笼

en: Before the gate
zh: 门前

en: By the road outside the garden a Samana grey with dust once stood a long time, only to see clearly the one in the palanquin
zh: 园门外的路边，一个满身尘土的沙门曾站了很久，只为看清轿中的人

en: The living thing in the garden
zh: 园中灵物

en: item
zh: item

en: To whom, in the end, the garden was given
zh: 最终，花园献给了谁

en: concept
zh: concept

en: Kamaswami's great house. Carpets, counting-room, and storehouses; money flowed in and out here.
zh: 湿瓦弥的豪宅。地毯、账房与仓库，金钱从这里流进流出。

en: Stone steps on the city's watercourse. Barber-helpers tout for custom here; at night small boats rest.
zh: 大城边河道的石阶。理发帮工在此招揽客人，夜里有小船栖身。

en: A coconut palm at the river's bend. Someone once looked down into the water here, with death only a line away.
zh: 大河转弯处的一棵椰子树。有人曾在这里俯视水波，与死只隔一线。

en: The ferry where Vasudeva plied. A boat, a hut, forest on both banks; here the river sings day and night.
zh: 维稣德瓦摆渡的渡口。一条船、一间草舍、两岸的森林，河在这里日夜歌唱。

en: The ferry
zh: 渡口

en: The old ferryman
zh: 老船夫

en: person
zh: person

en: What lies across
zh: 对岸的去处

en: place
zh: place

en: Form
zh: 形貌

en: A boat, a hut, forest on both banks without end; here the river sings day and night
zh: 一条船、一间草舍、两岸望不到头的森林，河水在这里日夜歌唱

en: Those who come and go
zh: 来往的人

en: Those going to market, to a burial, fleeing debt, on pilgrimage—all must board here; the river asks nothing
zh: 赶集的、奔丧的、逃债的、朝圣的都要在此上船，河水一句也不多问

en: The burning-ground by the water near the ferry. The ferryman's dead wife was burned here; later she too came to rest here.
zh: 渡口附近临水的火化场。船夫的亡妻在此火化，后来她也归寂于此。

en: The rare songbird Kamala kept in a little golden cage. It sang each morning, like her spring that would not age.
zh: 伽摩拉养在小小金笼里的珍稀歌鸟。它每天清晨歌唱，像她不老的春天。

en: The caged bird
zh: 笼中鸟

en: The keeper's dwelling
zh: 饲主的居处

en: place
zh: place

en: Who dreamed of it
zh: 谁梦到了它

en: person
zh: person

en: Habit
zh: 习性

en: Each morning it sang sweetly; its mistress took it for her spring that would not grow old
zh: 每天清晨婉转歌唱，主人拿它当作自己不会老去的春天

en: The dream
zh: 那个梦

en: In the dream it lay stiff on the floor of the cage and was thrown into the road—in that same instant the dreamer's heart was wrung
zh: 梦里它僵直地躺在笼底，被扔到路上——同一刻，做梦的人心像被绞住

en: Dice of the gaming table. In the years of sinking, the anxiety of a great stake was the only heartbeat he still felt.
zh: 赌局上的骰子。沉沦岁月里，一掷千金的焦虑是他唯一还感觉得到的心跳。

en: The gambling pieces
zh: 赌具

en: How it was played
zh: 玩法

en: Great sums on a throw; thousands won, thousands lost again in a breath; even the country villa was staked
zh: 一掷千金，赢了成千上万，转手又输掉成千上万，连乡下别墅也押上去

en: Why he gambled
zh: 为什么赌

en: He did not love money; only the anxiety of a stake not yet decided could make him feel he was still alive
zh: 他并不爱钱；只有赌金悬而未决的那种焦虑，能让他觉得自己还活着

en: The one lost in it
zh: 沉迷者

en: person
zh: person

en: The master who watched him stake everything
zh: 看他豪赌的东家

en: person
zh: person

en: The wooden boat and bamboo raft at the crossing. To carry men over the river is the ferryman's living, and the bridge between the banks.
zh: 渡口的木船竹筏。载人过河，是船夫的营生，也是两岸之间的桥。

en: The boat that carries men
zh: 渡人之舟

en: Master
zh: 主人

en: person
zh: person

en: The pole
zh: 撑船之具

en: item
zh: item

en: Form
zh: 形制

en: Wooden boat and bamboo raft, carrying men across—the ferryman's living, and the only bridge between the banks
zh: 木船与竹筏，载人过河，是船夫的营生，也是两岸之间唯一的桥

en: An old story
zh: 一桩旧事

en: Years ago it carried a young Samana who had nothing; the ferryman took no money from him
zh: 许多年前它载过一个身无分文的年轻沙门，船夫没有收他的钱

en: The long oar of the ferry, its handle worn bright. After the child fled, it was not seen again.
zh: 摇渡船的长桨，桨柄被磨得发亮。孩子逃走后，它再也没有出现。

en: The first decent garment the courtesan gave the young Samana. He carried it out of the garden under his arm.
zh: 名妓赠给年轻沙门的第一件体面衣服。他挟着它走出花园。

en: The yellow garment worn by the Buddha's disciples. To put it on is to leave household, wealth, and the old self.
zh: 佛陀弟子穿的黄衣。披上它，就意味着告别家庭、财富与旧我。

en: The bowl in which monks beg their food. One meal a day; even the Buddha himself entered the city with his bowl at dawn.
zh: 僧侣乞食的钵。一天只进一餐，连佛陀本人清晨也持钵入城。

en: The fan Kamala turned in her hands. When she smiled and asked a question, the eye-spots on the leaf flashed.
zh: 伽摩拉手中把玩的羽扇。她笑着提问时，扇面的眼斑一闪一闪。

en: Peacock fan
zh: 孔雀羽扇

en: The garden of her who held the fan
zh: 执扇者的园林

en: place
zh: place

en: Appearance
zh: 样子

en: The leaf was set with the eye-spots of peacock plumes, flashing as it moved, like many eyes blinking at once
zh: 扇面缀着孔雀翎的眼斑，一晃一闪，像许多只眼睛同时眨

en: Use
zh: 用处

en: When she smiled and asked, she half hid her mouth with it; only those who answered well saw her smile
zh: 她笑着提问时用它半掩住嘴，答得好的人才看得见她的笑

en: A little basket of two colours, woven of bark, where the two ferrymen kept the ferry-money. Later it vanished with the child.
zh: 树皮编的双色小篮，两位船夫存船费的地方。后来随孩子失踪。

en: Highest of the castes of ancient India: hereditary priests and scholars, keepers of sacrifice and scripture, who held themselves nearest the gods.
zh: 古印度种姓中最高的一级：世袭的祭司与学者，掌管祭祀与经典，自认最近神明。

en: The priestly caste
zh: 祭司阶层

en: Scriptures
zh: 经典

en: concept
zh: concept

en: A priest of the caste
zh: 族中的一位祭司

en: person
zh: person

en: Daily offices
zh: 日课

en: Bathing at daybreak, sacrifice and recitation at morning and evening; the hours of a day were all cut by prayer
zh: 天亮沐浴净身，晨昏献祭诵经，一天的时辰全由祷词分成段落

en: Transmission
zh: 传承

en: Father taught son, son taught grandson; a Brahmin child, from the first memory, could speak the most sacred syllable
zh: 父亲教儿子，儿子教孙子；婆罗门的孩子记事起就会念最神圣的那个音节

en: Wandering ascetics who had left the household. Naked and hungry, they sought release by extreme austerity, despised and revered by the world.
zh: 离弃家庭的游方苦行者。赤身忍饥，以极端苦行寻求解脱，被世人既鄙夷又敬畏。

en: The ascetics
zh: 苦行者

en: Place of practice
zh: 修行地

en: place
zh: place

en: The true Self they sought
zh: 要寻的真我

en: concept
zh: concept

en: Practice
zh: 功课

en: Fasting, the bearing of pain, the sun, sitting still; driving the self out of the body again and again, and watching it return
zh: 斋戒、忍痛、暴晒、静坐；把自我一次次赶出身体，再看它一次次回来

en: Three arts
zh: 三件本事

en: To think, to wait, to fast—later, in the city, these three were worth more than a boat of goods
zh: 会思想、会等待、会斋戒——这三样后来在城里比一船货物还值钱

en: The “true Self” in Brahmin teaching: the undying essence in the depth of each person, one with the spirit of the world.
zh: 婆罗门教义中的「真我」：每个人内心深处永恒不灭的本质，与宇宙之灵合一。

en: The true Self
zh: 真我

en: The book that names it
zh: 记载之典

en: concept
zh: concept

en: Where they bathed and prayed
zh: 沐浴祈祷之处

en: place
zh: place

en: Meaning
zh: 意思

en: The undying essence in the depth of each person; it is said to have been, from the first, one with the spirit of the world
zh: 每个人内心深处永恒不灭的本质，据说与宇宙之灵原本就是一个

en: The difficulty
zh: 难处

en: Scripture says it is in the heart, yet no one can point to where; the harder one hunts, the more one loses oneself
zh: 经文说它就在心里，谁也指不出它在哪儿；越是拼命去找，越是把自己弄丢

en: The most sacred syllable, the word that begins and ends Brahmin prayer, meaning “perfection.” To murmur it is as if the heart were an arrow aimed at Brahman.
zh: 最神圣的音节，婆罗门祷文的起止之字，意为「圆满」。默念它时，如以心为箭指向梵天。

en: The sound of perfection
zh: 圆满之音

en: Who murmured it
zh: 默念者

en: person
zh: person

en: The place that saved him
zh: 救命之地

en: place
zh: place

en: Meaning
zh: 含义

en: The word that begins and ends Brahmin prayer, meaning “perfection”; a child could speak it from the first memory
zh: 婆罗门祷文的起止之字，意思是「圆满」，孩子记事起就会念

en: The river's answer
zh: 河水的答案

en: In the instant of despair by the river, it was this syllable, long asleep, that woke him—and the thousand voices of the river, at last, became this one word
zh: 在河边绝望的刹那，正是这个沉睡多年的音节把他唤醒——万千河声，最终也汇成这一个字

en: Life turning between birth and death, like a wheel that does not stop. Those not yet awake suffer craving and pain again and again in Samsara.
zh: 生命在生死之间循环流转，如车轮不停。未证悟的人在轮回中反复经历渴望与痛苦。

en: The wheel of life
zh: 生命之轮

en: Meaning
zh: 含义

en: Life turning between birth and death, like a wheel that does not stop; craving follows pain, pain follows craving
zh: 生命在生死之间循环流转，如车轮不停；渴望接着痛苦，痛苦接着渴望

en: How it looked in the city
zh: 城里的样子

en: Feasts, gaming, buying and selling, love—the days turned and turned, and a man still thought he was walking forward
zh: 宴饮、赌局、买卖、情爱，日子转过一圈又一圈，人还当自己在往前走

en: What turns the wheel
zh: 转动的燃料

en: What keeps the wheel turning is craving: the thing wanted, once in the hand, and a new wanting grows at once
zh: 推着轮子不停转的是渴望：想要的东西一到手，新的想要立刻又长出来

en: How one is freed
zh: 如何解脱

en: concept
zh: concept

en: The meaning is quenching: the still realm beyond birth and death. The aim of the Buddha's teaching, the farther shore of the sea of pain.
zh: 熄灭之意：超越生死轮回的寂静境界。佛陀教义的目标，苦海的对岸。

en: The farther shore
zh: 彼岸

en: The cycle it stills
zh: 所止息的流转

en: concept
zh: concept

en: The elder who sought it and did not arrive
zh: 求它不得的长者

en: person
zh: person

en: Meaning
zh: 意思

en: The meaning is quenching: the still realm beyond the turning of birth and death, the aim the Buddha's teaching points toward
zh: 熄灭之意：超越生死流转的寂静境界，是佛陀教义所指的目标

en: The difficulty
zh: 难处

en: Austerity, fasting, hypnosis cannot reach it; some practise a lifetime and still stand on this shore
zh: 苦行、斋戒、催眠都到不了那里；有人修了一辈子，仍旧站在此岸

en: The company of wandering monks who followed the Buddha: yellow robes, the alms bowl, the precepts, travelling the four directions.
zh: 追随佛陀的游方僧人群体：披黄衣、持钵乞食、守戒云游四方。

en: One of the three arts of the Samanas: to bear hunger in order to master desire, and so not be driven by hunger.
zh: 沙门三大技艺之一：忍饥挨饿以降伏欲望，因此不被饥饿驱赶。

en: The high courtesan of ancient India: a woman of means and art, choosing her own companions, known for song, dance, and the art of love.
zh: 古印度的高级艺妓：有财有艺、自主择偶的独立女性，以歌舞与情爱之艺闻名。

en: The way of the courtesan
zh: 名妓之道

en: Standing
zh: 地位

en: Not a woman to be bought, but an independent person with land, with guests, who chose her lovers herself
zh: 不是可以买卖的女子，而是有田产、有门客、自己挑选情人的独立人物

en: Custom
zh: 规矩

en: One who came to learn must first have decent clothes, shoes, and money; a pupil brought the fee according to custom
zh: 求教的人须先有像样的衣裳、鞋子和钱，学生要按规矩把学费送到

en: One who stood for it
zh: 代表人物

en: person
zh: person

en: The first gift she gave him
zh: 她给他的第一份礼物

en: item
zh: item

en: The sacred scriptures handed down among the Brahmins, source of sacrifice and wisdom, including the Upanishads.
zh: 婆罗门世代传承的神圣经典，祭祀与智慧的源泉，含《奥义书》。

en: Son of a Brahmin
zh: 婆罗门之子

en: In ancient India, two thousand five hundred years ago, people divided society into ranks called caste, fixed from birth for a lifetime. Highest of them was the {{e_poluomen|ब्राह्मण}}—hereditary priestly nobles, keepers of sacrifice and scripture, who held themselves nearest the gods. In a house planted with mango trees, where the scent of the sacrificial fire hung all year, there lived a Brahmin's son.
zh: 两千五百年前的古印度，人们把社会分成好几个等级，叫作「种姓」，一出生就定下终身。最高的一等是{{e_poluomen|婆罗门}}——世代相传的祭司贵族，掌管祭祀、诵读经典，自认最接近神明。在这座种满芒果树、终年飘着祭火香气的宅第里，就住着一位婆罗门之子。

en: [[NPC1]] had a high brow and a look like a king's. He grew among his mother's songs, and at the riverbank learned the pious bath—Brahmins bathe each day, praying to be washed of sin; early he joined the talk of scholars and argued the {{e_feituo|वेद}}—the sacred scriptures handed down among the Brahmins, source of sacrifice and wisdom. At every rite his bearing was perfect and graceful; at every debate his speech was keener than other men's.
zh: [[NPC1]]有着高高的前额和王者般的眼神。他在母亲的歌声中嬉戏长大，在河岸边学会虔诚的沐浴——婆罗门每天都要沐浴净身，祈求洗清罪孽；他又早早加入学者们的谈话，与人辩论{{e_feituo|吠陀经典}}——那是婆罗门世代传承的神圣经典，祭祀与智慧的源泉。每逢祭礼，他举止完美优雅；每逢辩论，他言辞锋利过人。

en: All people loved him. Young women of the town felt a stirring when they saw him; his friend {{e_qiaowenda|गोविन्द}} honoured him above anyone, and was willing to be his shadow, following wherever he went. He could make all people glad—yet he himself was not glad. When the smoke of sacrifice rose, bewilderment and unrest rose with it; from the glittering stars of night, from the flowing river, unquiet thoughts came upon him without cease. A seed of unrest had long been buried quietly in his heart.
zh: 所有的人都热爱他。城里年轻的女子见了他，心里泛起阵阵涟漪；他的好友{{e_qiaowenda|侨文达}}敬他胜过任何人，甘愿做他的影子，他走到哪里，就跟到哪里。他能使所有的人喜悦——可是，他自己并不快乐。祭祀的烟火升起时，迷惑与躁动也跟着升起；从夜晚闪烁的群星、从流动的河水，不安宁的思绪不断向他袭来。一颗不安宁的种子，早已在他心里悄悄埋下。

en: {{e_fuqin|पिता}} was the town's most honoured priest, in white robe and sacred thread, his bearing calm and noble. He poured all his heart into this son, watching him sit, rise, and walk, filled with joy, and said to whoever would hear—
zh: {{e_fuqin|父亲}}是城中德高望重的祭司，白袍圣线，举止从容而高贵。他把全部心血倾注在这个儿子身上，看着他落坐、起立、行走，心中充满喜悦，逢人便说——

en: My son is keen of mind, and hungry for knowledge. One day he will be a great scholar, a priest, a prince among Brahmins. My whole life will shine because of him.
zh: 我的儿子聪慧，又渴求知识。将来，他会成为一位伟大的学者、一位祭司、婆罗门中的王子。我这一生，都会因他而有光彩。

en: When he said this, his eyes were full of hope. His mother, watching him greet her, would always lift her chest with pride; the teachers kept their finest verses for him, hoping he would soon take the key of the sacrificial fire. But they did not know: in the son's gaze upon that fire there was no contentment, only a thirst that deepened day by day. Neither the glory of this house, nor the future all men envied, could hold a heart already stirring to leave.
zh: 说这话时，他眼里满是期许。母亲看他向自己问安，总会骄傲地挺起胸脯；师长们把最精粹的句子留给他，盼他早日接过祭火的钥匙。可他们都不知道，儿子望着祭火的眼神里，没有满足，只有一天比一天更深的渴。这座宅第的荣光、这份人人称羡的前程，都留不住那颗已经蠢蠢欲动的心。

en: The most promising young man in the city; his father is a priest.
zh: 全城最被看好的年轻人，他的父亲是祭司。

en: No one knows his family name, yet everyone calls him “the Brahmin's son”—the name in the lexicon that most resembles the hero.
zh: 他姓什么没人知道，但人人都叫他「婆罗门之子」——词条库里最像主角的那个名字。

en: The Vessel Unfilled
zh: 容器未满

en: My father and my teachers have been very kind to me. They poured their finest wisdom, drop by drop, into the vessel I held ready, as one pours water into a jar. In the scripture hall of the {{e_poluomenzhai|ब्राह्मण-गृह}}, I read the {{e_feituo|वेद}}—the sacred books our Brahmins have handed down from age to age—volume after volume, and debated scholar after scholar. Yet my vessel was not filled, my mind was not satisfied, my soul was not at peace.
zh: 父亲和师长们待我极好。他们把自己最优秀的智慧，一点一点灌进我等待着的容器，像往罐子里注水。在{{e_poluomenzhai|婆罗门宅邸}}的经堂里，我把{{e_feituo|吠陀经典}}——我们婆罗门世代相传的神圣经典——读了一卷又一卷，与学者们辩论了一场又一场。可是，我的容器没有盛满，我的智力没有满足，我的灵魂没有安宁。

en: Pious bathing is a good thing, yet it is only water—it can wash the dust from the body, not the unrest from the heart. The rites of offering to the gods are very beautiful; but is that all there is? Why must my father, who has done no wrong, bathe himself anew each day, trying to wash his sins away? Why do even the most learned elders have hunger written in their eyes? Does the spring not lie within a man himself? To whom else should one offer sacrifice, whom else revere, if not to that?
zh: 虔诚的沐浴是善，可那只是水——洗得掉身上的尘土，洗不掉心里的烦恼。向诸神献祭的仪式极美，可那就是一切吗？为什么毫无过错的父亲，每天还要沐浴一新，试图洗清自己的罪孽？为什么最渊博的长者，眼里也写满了饥渴？难道源泉不在人的内心吗？除了向它，人们还应当向谁献祭、向谁尊崇呢？

en: The scriptures say that in the depths of every person there is an undying “true Self,” called {{e_atman|आत्मन्}}, one with the spirit of the universe. The wise know everything of the world—creation, speech, food, the stars—but if they do not know this one thing that matters, of what use is all that knowledge?
zh: 经典里说，每个人内心深处都有一个永恒不灭的「真我」，叫作{{e_atman|阿特曼}}，它与宇宙之灵合一。智者们懂得世界的一切——创生、语言、饮食、星辰——可如果他们不知道这唯一重要的事，那些知识再多，又有什么用？

en: I must find the spring within myself. A man must possess it—everything else is only detour and error. No one can point this path for me: not my father, not my teachers, not the sacred verses. This is my care, my thirst, my sorrow.
zh: 我必须找到自己内心的源泉。人必须拥有它——其他的一切，不过是弯路与错误。没有人能替我指明这条路：父亲不能，师长不能，神圣的诗篇也不能。这就是我的心事，我的渴求，我的悲哀。

en: He is the most learned in this house, and the least content.
zh: 他是这个家里最博学、也最不满足的人。

en: The pride of every Brahmin in the city—the son who left home to seek the way.
zh: 全城婆罗门的骄傲——那个离家求道的儿子。

en: I Will Follow You
zh: 我跟你走

en: Evening, under the {{e_rongshu|नगर के बाहर बरगद}}, two youths had just risen from meditation. By day three {{e_shamen|श्रमण}} had passed through the city—ascetics who had left their homes to wander, almost naked, their shoulders grey with dust and streaked with blood, yet about them a stillness that would spare nothing. [[NPC2]] had just silently recited the sacred syllable {{e_om|ॐ}}—the ancients said: Om is the bow, the heart the arrow, and the target of the arrow is Brahman. In that moment the arrow in his own heart had left the string.
zh: 傍晚，{{e_rongshu|城外榕树}}下，两个少年刚打完坐。白天，城里曾路过三个{{e_shamen|沙门}}——离弃家庭、四处游方的苦行者，几乎全身赤裸，肩上满是尘灰和血迹，周身却透着一股不惜一切的宁静。[[NPC2]]刚默念过神圣音节{{e_om|唵}}——古人说：唵为弓，心为箭，箭矢的靶子在梵天。此刻，他心里的箭也离了弦。

en: Friend, tomorrow morning I shall join the Samanas and become an ascetic.
zh: 朋友，明天早晨，我要加入沙门的行列，去做一名苦行者。

en: What are you saying? Samanas? Those naked men who passed through the city today?
zh: 你说什么？沙门？就是白天路过城里、那些赤身裸体的人？

en: Just so. They have nothing, and yet they seem to lack nothing. I want to be as they are—to peel desire away layer by layer, and see what is left at the last.
zh: 正是。他们一无所有，却好像什么都不缺。我要像他们一样，把渴望一层一层剥掉，看看最后剩下什么。

en: But—will your father allow it? You are the son he is proudest of, the most promising young man in the city!
zh: 可……可你的父亲会允许吗？你是他最骄傲的儿子，是全城最被看好的年轻人啊！

en: We need not waste words. At dawn tomorrow I begin the life of a Samana. Let us speak of it no more.
zh: 我们不用浪费口舌。明日破晓，我就开始沙门的生活。不要再讨论了。

en: Why? Tell me why! Learning, fame, the love of the teachers—things other men cannot obtain though they beg for them—you have them all. What else is there to seek?
zh: 为什么？你告诉我为什么！学问、名声、师长们的喜爱，别人求都求不来，你全有了，还要去找什么？

en: Peace. Sacrifice, scripture, debate—I have tried them all, and the thirst in my heart grows deeper day by day. The vessel is full of water; the heart remains empty. Better to go into hardship than to wither here slowly—either I find that spring, or I die upon the road that seeks it.
zh: 找安宁。祭祀、经典、辩论，我都试遍了，心里的渴一天比一天深。容器装满了水，心却一直是空的。与其在这里慢慢枯萎，不如到苦里去——要么找到那眼源泉，要么死在找它的路上。

en: Then will you come back?
zh: 那你会回来吗？

en: I do not know. Perhaps I will return if I find it; perhaps I will be on the road all my life.
zh: 不知道。也许找到了就回来，也许一辈子在路上。

en: You will take no dry provisions? Not even a garment against the cold?
zh: 你连干粮都不带？连一件御寒的衣服都不带？

en: A Samana wants nothing. Sleep, my friend. When the sun rises tomorrow, do not see me off.
zh: 沙门什么都不要。睡吧，朋友。明天太阳升起的时候，不要送我。

en: At dawn the next day, [[NPC2]] left the still-sleeping town alone. At the last hut on the edge of the city, a crouched figure slipped from the shadows and silently followed him. The night before, when that announcement was first heard, this face had gone pale as a dried banana skin.
zh: 第二天黎明，[[NPC2]]独自离开还在沉睡的城邑。走到城边最后一间小屋时，一个蜷曲的身影从阴影里闪出来，默默跟上了他。昨夜刚听到那句宣布时，这张脸曾白得像一张晒干的香蕉皮。

en: I have come. Do not send me back. Wherever you go, I will go—as your companion, as your servant, as your shadow.
zh: 我来了。你别赶我回去。你走到哪里，我就跟到哪里——做你的伙伴，做你的仆人，做你的影子。

en: You have come.
zh: 你来了。

en: I did not sleep all night. I have decided: your path is my path. If you are to become a saint, I will watch you become one.
zh: 我一整夜没睡。我想好了：你的路，就是我的路。你要成圣，我就看着你成圣。

en: Fool. Each man has his own path; no one can walk another's. Still—come.
zh: 傻瓜。路是各人的，谁也替谁走不了。不过——来吧。

en: One announced that he would go; one followed, his face pale.
zh: 一个是宣布要走的人，一个是脸色苍白跟上来的人。

en: The companion who always lagged a step behind, following him as one follows a god.
zh: 那个总落后一步、把他当神明一样跟从的伙伴。

en: Standing Until Dawn
zh: 站到天明

en: The night grew deep; the stars beyond the little window moved in silence. [[NPC1]] entered the room of the most honoured old priest in the house and stood silently behind him. He had come to ask a tremendous thing: to leave home and become a {{e_shamen|श्रमण}}—a wandering ascetic who forsakes his family and goes naked into hardship. The old man felt the presence at his back.
zh: 夜深了，小窗外的星星默默移动。[[NPC1]]走进家中最受敬重的那位老祭司的房间，默默站在他的身后。他要请求一件天大的事：离开家，去做一名{{e_shamen|沙门}}——离弃家庭、赤身苦行的游方修道者。老人感觉到了身后的存在。

en: Is it you? Then speak your mind.
zh: 是你吗？那么，说出你的想法。

en: With your leave, I have come to tell you: I wish to leave your house tomorrow, to join the ranks of the ascetics and become a Samana. I am certain you will not oppose it.
zh: 蒙您的允许，我特来告诉您：我希望明天离开您的家，加入苦修者的行列，成为一名沙门。我深信，您是不会反对的。

en: The old man was silent a long while. Beyond the little window the night sky turned. The son stood with his arms crossed upon his breast, motionless; the old man sat motionless upon the mat. At last—
zh: 老人沉默了许久。小窗外的夜空星移斗转。儿子双臂交叉在胸前，默默地站立，一动也不动；老人默默地坐在地席上，一动也不动。终于——

en: It would be unseemly for us to speak in heat and anger. Yet there is displeasure in my heart. I do not wish to hear this request from you again.
zh: 说出激烈和恼怒的言辞，对我们是不体面的。但我的心中确有不悦。我不愿再听到你提出这样的请求。

en: Why do you still wait?
zh: 你为何还在等待？

en: You know why.
zh: 您知道原因。

en: The old man left the room in vexation and returned to his bed. An hour passed; he could not sleep. He rose and paced, and through the little window he saw the young man standing with folded arms, his pale robe faintly gleaming in the dark. Another hour passed; the moon climbed the sky. He rose again and saw the moonlight like water upon the young man's bare ankles. His heart filled with anger and anxiety, with fear and grief—the one he had raised for half a lifetime was defying him in a way he had never seen.
zh: 老人懊恼地走出房间，回到自己的床上。一个小时过去了，他无法入眠，起身踱步，透过那扇小窗，看见年轻人叉手站立，淡色的长袍在夜幕中微微闪光。又一个小时过去了，月亮升上天宇，他再次起身，看见月华如水，映着年轻人赤裸的脚踝。他的心中充满怒气和焦虑，充满恐惧与忧伤——他教养了半生的人，正在用一种他从未见过的方式反抗他。

en: In the last hour before dawn the old man entered the little room once more. The young man still stood there, tall and strange.
zh: 黎明前的最后一个小时，老人再一次走进那间小屋。年轻人仍旧站在那里，显得高大而陌生。

en: Why do you wait?
zh: 你为何等待？

en: You know why.
zh: 您知道原因。

en: Will you stand like this until dawn, until noon, until night?
zh: 你要这样站着，等到天明，等到中午，等到夜晚吗？

en: I shall stand and wait.
zh: 我将站立和等待。

en: You will grow tired.
zh: 你会累的。

en: I will not grow tired.
zh: 我不会累。

en: You will fall asleep.
zh: 你会睡着的。

en: I will not fall asleep.
zh: 我不会睡着。

en: You will die.
zh: 你会死的。

en: I will not die.
zh: 我不会死的。

en: Then you would rather die than obey?
zh: 那么，你宁死也不愿服从吗？

en: I have always obeyed you.
zh: 我一向服从您。

en: Then will you give up your purpose?
zh: 那么，你要放弃你的打算？

en: I will do what you require of me.
zh: 我会做您所要求的事情。

en: The first light of day entered the room. The old man saw the young man's knees tremble a little—yet there was no tremor in his face, and his gaze was fixed on the distance. At last the old man understood: this son could no longer remain in the house; he had already left. He stretched out his hand and laid it gently on the young man's shoulder.
zh: 第一抹天光投进室内。老人看见年轻人的双膝微微战栗了一下——可他的脸上没有战栗，目光注视着远方。老人终于明白：这个儿子再也不能留在家中，他已然离开了。老人伸出手，轻轻抚上年轻人的肩膀。

en: Go, then, into the forest, and be a Samana. If you find the bliss of heaven in the woods, come back and teach it to me; if you meet with disillusion, return to me still, and we shall offer to the gods together. Now go and kiss your mother farewell, and tell her where you are going.
zh: 去吧，到林中去，做一名沙门。如果你在林中寻得天堂之乐，回来教给我；如果你遭遇幻灭，仍回到我身边，我们再一同向诸神献祭。现在，去吻别你的母亲，告诉她你的去向。

en: With that, the old man's hand slid from the young man's shoulder. He turned and went out toward the {{e_muyuhepan|नदी का स्नान-घाट}}—the stone steps on the riverbank at the city's edge, where he bathed each morning, praying to wash his sins away. Today he walked more slowly than usual. In the room the young man tried to take a step; his body swayed—he had stood in that one place the whole night through.
zh: 说罢，老人的手从年轻人的肩上滑落。他转身出门，往{{e_muyuhepan|河畔沐浴场}}走去——那是城边河岸的石阶，他每天清晨都在那里沐浴净身，祈求洗清罪孽。今天，他走得比往常更慢。屋里，年轻人试图迈步，身体摇晃了一下——他已经在原地，站了整整一夜。

en: One old, one young, facing each other through a little window until dawn.
zh: 一老一少，隔着一扇小窗对峙到天亮。

en: The one who, at the last, laid his hand on his son's shoulder.
zh: 最后把手放上儿子肩膀的人。

en: I Will Not Tire
zh: 我不会累

en: My knees are trembling; I can feel it. I have stood half the night; my legs no longer seem my own. Starlight lies on my shoulders, and dew has made the robe ice-cold. But my heart does not tremble. Three times he came from the little window to look at me, each time thinking I would sit down, would give in. I will not. Each time he went back inside, his footsteps were heavier than before.
zh: 膝盖在战栗，我感觉得到。站了半夜，双腿早就不像自己的了，星光落满肩头，露水把衣袍打得冰凉。可我的心没有战栗。他从小窗里出来看了我三次，每一次都以为我会坐下、会放弃。我不会的。他回屋时的脚步声，一次比一次沉重。

en: I am not defying him. There is no son under heaven who would wish his father to rise three times in a night, sleepless. But if I give back half a step now, I must stay, and walk the road he has laid for me—to become a {{e_poluomen|ब्राह्मण}}. That is the highest caste of ancient India, a hereditary priesthood: honourable, noble, respected by all.
zh: 我不是在反抗他。天底下没有哪个儿子，愿意让父亲一夜起身三次、一夜难眠。可我若现在退后半步，就得留下来，走他为我铺好的路——做一名{{e_poluomen|婆罗门}}。那是古印度最高的种姓，世代相传的祭司贵族：体面、尊贵、人人敬重。

en: And then? A lifetime of sacrifice, bathing, reciting scripture—and another lifetime of thirst. He has everything—learning, virtue, fame—but has he ever been content? Each day he bathes, trying to wash away an unrest that will not wash; each day he offers sacrifice, trying to reach a heaven he cannot reach. I will not become another him: learned, respectable, never satisfied.
zh: 然后呢？用一生去献祭、沐浴、诵经，再用一生去渴望。他什么都有了——学问、德行、名声——可他满足过吗？每天沐浴，想洗掉洗不掉的烦恼；每天献祭，想够到够不到的天堂。我不要成为另一个他：渊博、体面、永不满足。

en: The scriptures say there is in a man's heart an undying “true Self,” called {{e_atman|आत्मन्}}, one with the spirit of the universe. It is not in the smoke of the sacrificial fire, nor in the letters of a prayer, but only in the depths of a man himself. I will go and find it, even if it takes a lifetime.
zh: 经典里说，人心里有一个永恒不灭的「真我」，叫作{{e_atman|阿特曼}}，与宇宙之灵合一。它不在祭火的烟里，不在祷文的字里，只在人自己的内心深处。我要去找它，哪怕找上一辈子。

en: Dawn is near; the stars are fading one by one. Legs, you may tremble; heart, you may not. I will stand until dawn, until noon, until night—until he himself gives me leave to go.
zh: 天快亮了，星星一颗颗淡下去。腿，你可以战栗；心，你不许。我会站到天明，站到中午，站到夜晚——站到他亲口放行为止。

en: The one standing in that little window.
zh: 那扇小窗里站着的人。

en: The Brahmin's son.
zh: 婆罗门之子。

en: Eagle and Jackal
zh: 化鹰化豺

en: The years in the forest were counted in hunger. [[NPC1]] took one meal a day, and never cooked it; then he fasted fourteen days, and once again twenty-eight. The {{e_shamen|श्रमण}} called this art {{e_zhaijie|उपवास}}—to starve desire into submission; starve long enough, and desire faints away. His cheeks grew lean; strange dreams shone in his sunken eyes; long nails grew upon his fingers.
zh: 林中的岁月，是用饥饿来计算的。[[NPC1]]一天只进一餐，而且从不烹调；随后他禁食十四天，又一次禁食二十八天。{{e_shamen|沙门}}把这门功夫叫作{{e_zhaijie|斋戒}}——忍饥挨饿以降伏欲望，饿得久了，欲望便昏厥过去。他的两颊日渐消瘦，凹陷的大眼睛里映着奇异的幻梦，手指生出长长的指甲。

en: He stood in silence under the fierce sun until he no longer felt pain or thirst; he stood in the rain, water running over his stiff, cold shoulders and legs, until sensation was wholly extinguished; he lay among thorns, blood dripping, wounds festering, and still he did not move, until the sting itself ceased. He practised also to lessen the breath and slow the heartbeat, until the heart beat so faintly it almost vanished. Passing through towns he saw merchants at trade, princes at the hunt, lovers meeting, and found it all not worth a glance—the world was full of suffering; life was pain.
zh: 他默默伫立在暴烈的日光下，直到不再感到痛苦和干渴；他伫立在雨中，雨水流过僵冷的肩膀和双腿，直到感觉完全寂灭；他匍伏在荆棘丛里，鲜血滴落，伤口溃烂，他仍僵卧不动，直到刺痛停息。他还修习减省呼吸、减缓心跳，直到心跳极缓，几乎消失。经过市镇时，他看见商人经商、王孙行猎、恋人相会，只觉得一切都不值一顾——世界充满苦痛，生命即苦。

en: The elder taught them self-mastery and meditation. {{e_laoshamen|सबसे वृद्ध श्रमण}} was nearly sixty, dust in his tangled hair, his temper like thunder in the woods.
zh: 长老教他们自制与冥想。{{e_laoshamen|老沙门}}年近六十，纠结的长发上沾着尘灰，脾气像林中的炸雷。

en: Straighten your backs! If you cannot even govern your breath, how will you govern your heart? Pain is your teacher—endure it; do not hide! Whoever hides is not fit to be a Samana!
zh: 都把背挺直！连呼吸都管不住，还谈什么管住自己的心？苦是你们的老师——忍住，不许躲！谁躲，谁就不配做沙门！

en: In meditation the soul of [[NPC1]] flew from his body. A grey eagle swept over the bamboo; he became that eagle, flying over forest and mountain, hunting fish, enduring an eagle's hunger, speaking an eagle's tongue, dying an eagle's death. A dead jackal lay on the sand; his soul slipped into that carcass, lay there swelling, stinking, rotting, torn by hyenas, pecked by vultures, becoming remnant and dust, dissolving into the air. He killed his senses, wiped out his memory, fled into a thousand forms of the world—he was animal, corpse, rock, wood, water.
zh: 冥想中，[[NPC1]]的灵魂飞出躯壳。一只苍鹰掠过竹林，他化作那只鹰，飞越森林和山峦，猎食鱼类，忍受鹰的饥饿，说鹰的语言，经历鹰的死亡。沙滩上躺着一只死豺，他的灵魂溜进那具尸身，躺在那里肿胀、发臭、腐烂，被鬣狗肢解，被兀鹰啄食，化为残骸与尘土，融进大气。他扼杀自己的感官，除灭自己的记忆，逃进世上万千形态——他是动物，是尸体，是岩石，是木，是水。

en: Yet each time he woke again in sunlight or moonlight, became himself again, felt again the restlessness of desire—no matter how far he fled, he always came back to himself. The elders praised him as the harshest in practice, the swiftest to learn, their proudest disciple. But in this young man's heart a quiet doubt of it all was taking root.
zh: 可每一次，他都在日光下、月华中再度清醒，再度成为自己，再度感到渴望的躁动——无论逃得多远，最后总会回到自己。长老们称赞他修得最狠、学得最快，是最得意的弟子。可是这个年轻人的心里，正在暗暗怀疑这一切的意义。

en: The young man who practised most harshly and learned the fastest.
zh: 修得最狠、学得最快的那个年轻人。

en: The elder's proudest disciple—yet in his heart he is already doubting it all.
zh: 长老最得意的弟子——可他心里正在怀疑这一切。

en: Anesthetic
zh: 麻醉剂

en: Three years. In the {{e_kuxiulin|श्रमणों का वन}} I have learned every art of the Samanas: meditation, the governing of breath, {{e_zhaijie|उपवास}}—starving for so long that desire faints. My cheeks have hollowed; my nails are long and cracked; passers-by step aside when they see me. The elders praise me as the harshest in practice, the swiftest to learn; they say I shall one day become a saint. But today I must admit something to myself.
zh: 三年了。在{{e_kuxiulin|苦修林}}里，我把沙门的技艺学了个遍：冥想、调息、{{e_zhaijie|斋戒}}——长时间忍饥挨饿，直到欲望昏厥。我的两颊凹了下去，指甲长而干裂，路人见了都要绕着走。长老们夸我修得最狠、学得最快，说我有朝一日会成圣。可今天，我要对自己承认一件事。

en: What is meditation? What is the rejection of the body? Strip it bare, and it is only flight from the self, a brief escape from the suffering of life, a temporary anesthetic. A cowherd sits in a tavern, drinks a few bowls of rice wine, and sinks into sleep—he is performing the same flight: no longer feeling the self, no longer feeling the pain of life. The place he reaches with one bowl of wine, we reach by starving a month, sitting a month.
zh: 什么是冥想？什么是对肉体的弃绝？说穿了，那不过是逃离自我，是对生命苦难的短暂逃避，是一副暂时的麻醉剂。一个牧牛人坐在小酒馆里，喝几碗米酒，昏然睡去——他做的是同样的逃离：不再感觉到自我，不再感觉到生命的苦。他一碗酒就到得了的地方，我们要饿上一个月、打坐一个月。

en: Of course, when the drinker wakes, everything is as it was; he has gained nothing. And I? A thousand times I have fled the self, dwelt in nothingness, dwelt in the body of a grey eagle and a dead jackal, and each time I have been led back to myself, to feel again the restlessness of desire. Three years, and I am still as an infant in the womb, wisdom as far off as ever.
zh: 当然，酒徒醒来，一切照旧，什么也没得到。可我呢？我千万次逃离自我，住进虚无，住进苍鹰和死豺的身体，每一次却又被领回自己，重新感到渴望的躁动。三年了，我仍如母腹中的婴儿，离智慧遥遥无期。

en: Perhaps {{e_atman|आत्मन्}}—that undying true Self in the heart of man—does not lie on the road of flight at all. Intoxicate the self a hundred times; when you wake, it is still sitting there waiting. Perhaps I have been using an anesthetic to treat a sickness that only wakefulness can cure. This medicine I will take no more; this hiding I will play no more.
zh: 也许{{e_atman|阿特曼}}——人们心中那个永恒不灭的真我——根本不在逃离的路上。把自我灌醉一百次，醒来时它还是坐在原地等我。也许我一直在用麻醉剂，治一种只有清醒才治得好的病。这副药，我不想再吃了；这场躲藏，我不想再玩了。

en: The one who has begun to find asceticism a “conjurer's trick.”
zh: 开始觉得苦修是「鬼把戏」的人。

en: The Samana who made a parable of rice wine.
zh: 那个拿米酒打比方的沙门。

en: The Rising Spiral
zh: 上升的螺旋

en: On the road out of the forest to beg food, the two young men walked one behind the other. [[NPC2]] spoke suddenly.
zh: 出林乞食的路上，两个年轻人一前一后走着。[[NPC2]]忽然开口。

en: Tell me, are we on the right path? Are we growing in wisdom, drawing nearer to salvation? Or are we—only going in circles?
zh: 你说，我们是否走在正道上？我们在增进智慧、趋于得救吗？还是说——我们只是在兜圈子？

en: Why do you think that again? We have learned much, and we are still learning. We are not going in circles; we are going upward—the path of the way is a rising spiral, and we have already climbed many steps. The elder often praises you; he says you will one day be a great Samana.
zh: 你怎么又这样想？我们已经学会了很多，而且还在学。我们没有兜圈子，我们在向上——道之路是一个上升的螺旋，我们已经攀登了许多级台阶。长老常夸你，说你将来会成为一位伟大的沙门。

en: Our venerable elder—how old is he this year?
zh: 我们可敬的长老，今年多大年纪？

en: About sixty, I suppose. Why?
zh: 大约六十岁了吧。怎么了？

en: He is sixty, and he has still not attained {{e_niepan|निर्वाण}}—that still realm beyond birth and death, where all unrest is extinguished, the end of our practice. He will practise until seventy, until eighty, and still not reach it. You and I will grow old the same way, fasting and meditating the same way, and fall equally short. I do not think a single Samana among them all will attain Nirvana. We have found a little comfort, learned a few conjurer's tricks, and deceived ourselves, that is all.
zh: 他六十岁了，仍未证得{{e_niepan|涅槃}}——超越生死、熄灭一切烦恼的寂静境界，我们修行的终点。他会修到七十岁、八十岁，还是够不着。你我也将一样老去，一样斋戒、冥想，一样够不着。我看，所有沙门中不会有一个人证得涅槃。我们只找到一点安慰，只学会一些鬼把戏，骗骗自己罢了。

en: Do not say such terrible things! So many scholars, so many devout ascetics, so many who have given themselves to the inner life—can it be that not one of them has found the right path?
zh: 别说出这么可怕的话！这么多学者，这么多虔诚的苦行者，这么多献身内心生活的人，难道竟没有一人能找到正道吗？

en: Year after year I sought instruction from the wise among the Brahmins, from the sacred {{e_feituo|वेद}}—the scriptures handed down through our generations, called the wellspring of sacrifice and wisdom. It has taken me so long to understand: a man cannot obtain the one thing that matters by learning. In the essence of all things there is a secret that cannot be called “knowledge”—and knowledge, perhaps, is its greatest enemy.
zh: 年复一年，我求教于婆罗门的智者，求教于神圣的{{e_feituo|吠陀经典}}——我们世代相传的经典，人称祭祀与智慧的源泉。可我耗费了这么久才明白：一个人无法通过学习得到那唯一重要的事。万物的本质里，有一种不能叫「学识」的秘密——而学识，也许正是它最大的敌人。

en: Your words frighten me. If it is as you say, and knowledge is of no use, then what meaning have our devout prayers? Where does the holiness of practice stand? What in this world is still worth treasuring and revering?
zh: 你的话让我害怕。如果真像你说的，学识毫无用处，那我们虔诚的祈祷有什么意义？修行的圣洁又置于何地？这世上还有什么值得珍惜和崇敬？

en: I do not know, my friend. I know only that my thirst has not lessened by a fraction. Before long I shall leave this Samana path.
zh: 我不知道，朋友。我只知道，我的渴望没有减少半分。不久之后，我就要离开这条沙门之路了。

en: Leave? And what of us? Did we not say we would walk together until the day of liberation?
zh: 离开？那我们呢？我们不是说好，要一起走到解脱的那天吗？

en: The path I must walk myself now. Forgive me.
zh: 路，要我自己去走了。抱歉。

en: [[NPC1]] stopped on the road, raised his hands, and let them fall again, powerless. He looked at the figure ahead—always half a step faster than he—and for the first time a panic rose in him: this man, he could scarcely keep up with him any longer.
zh: [[NPC1]]在路上停住脚，举起双手，又无力地垂下。他望着前方那个背影——总是比他快半步的背影——心里第一次生出一种恐慌：这个人，他快跟不住了。

en: One still believes in this path; one no longer does.
zh: 一个还信这条路，一个已经不信了。

en: The doubter is always the one walking half a step ahead.
zh: 质疑者总是那个走在前面半步的人。

en: Rumour and Hypnosis
zh: 传闻与催眠

en: When the two young men had almost completed three years with the Samanas, rumours poured into this jungle from every side: a sage of the Sakya clan had appeared. It was said he had conquered the world's sufferings and forever stilled the wheel of rebirth—men call the ceaseless turning of life between birth and death {{e_lunhui|संसार}}, a wheel that never stops; and he had passed beyond it, reached {{e_niepan|निर्वाण}}, that still farther shore where all unrest is extinguished. They called him “the Enlightened One”—a man who had awakened.
zh: 两个年轻人跟着沙门修行快满三年的时候，种种传闻从四面八方涌进这片丛林：一位释迦族的智者出现了。据说他已征服世间的众苦，永远止息了再生之轮——人们把生命在生死之间不停流转叫作{{e_lunhui|轮回}}，像车轮一样转个没完；而他超脱了它，抵达了{{e_niepan|涅槃}}，那熄灭一切烦恼的寂静彼岸。人们称他为「觉者」——一个觉悟了的人。

en: Rumour grew wings. Some praised him for wisdom beyond compare, for remembering his former lives, for having subdued demons; others mocked him as a fraud, saying he scorned sacrifice, lived in luxury, and was unlearned. The city talked; the forest talked. Every piece of news was laden with doubt and with hope—in this weary world a warm promise seemed to have appeared, and young men everywhere pricked up their ears. Many believed without question, many doubted, and many set out at once to seek this sage [[NPC1]].
zh: 传闻像长了翅膀。有人赞美他具足无比的智慧，能忆起自己的前生，曾降服魔鬼；也有人嘲讽他是个骗子，说他鄙弃献祭、奢侈度日、不学无术。城里在议论，林中也在议论。每一条消息都载满疑惑，也载满希望——这令人厌倦的世间，仿佛出现了一种温暖的许诺，各地的青年人都竖起了耳朵。许多人深信不疑，许多人心存疑惑，还有许多人立刻上路，去寻找这位智者[[NPC1]]。

en: The elder of the jungle had no love for these rumours. He had heard that this “Enlightened One” had once been an ascetic too, then turned toward worldly pleasure, and he scorned him the more.
zh: 丛林里的长老对这些传闻决无好感。他听说那位「觉者」从前也是苦修者，后来却投向了尘俗的享乐，便越发不屑。

en: Absurd! A man who threw off austerity halfway and went over to pleasure—and he is fit to speak of “awakening”? Whoever mentions him again shall starve three extra days! I have practised a lifetime, and I have never heard of liberation dropping from the sky!
zh: 荒唐！一个半路扔掉苦行、投向享乐的人，也配谈「觉」？谁再提他，谁就多饿三天！我修了一辈子，还没听说过天上会掉下解脱来！

en: But the more the rumours were forbidden, the louder they grew. At last one day the two young men came together before the elder and asked leave to quit the jungle, to hear with their own ears the teaching of that Enlightened One.
zh: 可是传闻越禁越响。终于有一天，两个年轻人一起来到长老面前，请求离开丛林，去亲耳听听那位觉者的教义。

en: What? Both of you leaving? Ungrateful creatures! I taught you the arts one by one, and this is how you repay me? Get out! Get out now!
zh: 什么？两个都要走？忘恩负义的东西！我把技艺一样一样教给你们，你们就这样报答我？滚！现在就滚！

en: [[NPC4]] started in alarm and stepped back again and again. [[NPC3]] leaned to his companion's ear and said softly—
zh: [[NPC4]]大惊失色，连连后退。[[NPC3]]却凑到同伴耳边，轻声说——

en: Do not be afraid. Now I will let this old man see what I have learned from him.
zh: 别怕。现在，我要让这位老人看看，我从他这儿学到了什么。

en: With that he approached the elder, stood still, and fixed his whole attention on the old man's eyes. With his look he seized the old man, hypnotised him, conquered his will, and silently commanded him to obey. The old man fell suddenly silent, his gaze froze, his arms hung powerless; all that fire could not issue a spark—this art of capturing the soul was what the old man himself had taught, year after year.
zh: 说罢，他走近长老，站定，专注一意，注视着老人的眼睛。他用自己的神情攫住老人，将他催眠，征服他的意志，暗暗命令他听从摆布。老人忽然沉默，目光凝滞，双臂无力地垂下，满腔的火气发不出一点——这门摄魂的本事，正是老人自己一年一年教出来的。

en: Then the old man bowed again and again to the two young men, blessed them, and stammered a few words of safe journey. They thanked him, bowed in return, and set out empty-handed.
zh: 接着，那老人竟频频向两个年轻人鞠躬，为他们祝福，结结巴巴地说了几句旅途平安之类的话。两个年轻人谢过他，鞠躬还礼，空着双手上路了。

en: I can scarcely believe my eyes… To hypnotise an elder—that is the hardest thing of all! Truly, if you stayed, you would soon learn to walk on water!
zh: 我简直不敢相信自己的眼睛……催眠一位长老，这是最难最难的事！说真话，你要是留下来，很快就能学会在水面上行走了！

en: I have no mind to walk on water. Let those who have grown old and rotten be content with such arts.
zh: 我可没有心思在水面行走。让那些老朽的人，为这种技艺心满意足吧。

en: The morning mist thinned; two figures took the road toward the great city. The man of the rumours was still far away, yet both of them felt they had already heard his voice.
zh: 晨雾散开，两条身影走上通往大城的路。那个传闻中的人还在很远的地方，可他们俩都觉得，自己已经听见了他的声音。

en: Of the four “people,” one is not there at all; he lives only in rumour.
zh: 四个「人」里有一个根本不在场，他只活在传闻里。

en: The old man who bowed and blessed once his eyes were held, and the disciple who held them.
zh: 被盯住眼睛就鞠躬祝福的老人，和盯人的那个弟子。

en: The Teaching at Jetavana
zh: 祇园听法

en: Asking the way as they went, the two young ascetics entered {{e_sheweicheng|श्रावस्ती}}. The one walking in front was named {{e_xidaduo|सिद्धार्थ}}. The Enlightened One—people called him “the Buddha,” meaning “the awakened one”—was a household name in this city; every house was willing to fill a monk's {{e_boyu|भिक्षा-पात्र}} with food. The two stood silently begging at the first door, and the master of the house at once gave them food.
zh: 一路打听，两个年轻的苦行者走进了{{e_sheweicheng|舍卫城}}。走在前面的那个，名叫{{e_xidaduo|悉达多}}。那位觉者——人们称他「佛陀」，意思是「觉悟了的人」——的大名，在这座城里家喻户晓，家家都愿意把僧侣的{{e_boyu|乞食钵盂}}盛满饭食。两人在第一家的门前默默站立乞食，主人立刻把食物施与他们。

en: Kind woman, please tell us: where does the Blessed One dwell? We are Samanas from the forest, come to pay our respects to this holy man and hear the teaching from his own mouth.
zh: 善良的妇人，请您告诉我们：世尊居住在何处？我们是从林中来的沙门，特来拜见这位圣者，聆听他亲口演说的教义。

en: Woman
zh: 妇人

en: Ah, Samanas from the forest, you have arrived at last. The Blessed One lives in the monastery outside the city—a wealthy elder bought the whole grove and offered it to him; those who come to hear the teaching may spend the night there. I often see him in a yellow robe, walking the lanes in silence, holding out his bowl at the doors, and going back with the bowl filled.
zh: 啊，林中的沙门，你们可算到了。世尊就住在城外那座精舍里——一位富有的长者买下整片园林献给他，来听法的人都可以在那里过夜。我常见他披着黄衣，默默走过街巷，在人家门前端出钵盂，再端着盛满的钵盂回去。

en: They thanked her and took their leave, and followed the stream of pilgrims to that great grove. Deep shade covered the sun; monks were as many as clouds, like a little town: some sat under trees in silent absorption, some gathered in fierce debate. They were all disciples of {{e_sengtuan|गौतम का संघ}}—the company of wandering monks who follow the Buddha, wearing the {{e_sengyi|पीली काषाय}}, keeping the precepts, taking one meal a day at noon. The two young men found a sheltered corner and rested until dawn.
zh: 两人道谢告别，随朝圣的人流来到那座大园林。园里浓荫蔽日，僧侣如云，像一个小小的市镇：或坐在树下默默入定，或聚在一起激烈论辩。他们都是{{e_sengtuan|僧团}}的弟子——追随佛陀的游方僧人群体，披着{{e_sengyi|黄色僧衣}}，守戒修行，一天只在午间进一餐。两个年轻人找到一处遮蔽的角落，歇到天明。

en: At morning [[NPC1]] went quietly out of the grove gate with his bowl to beg food. He walked among hundreds of monks dressed alike, yet Siddhartha knew him at a glance. There was no pride in the man; his peaceful look was neither joy nor sorrow, as if a mild smile rose from within—a smile no different from a child's. His face, his gait, his gaze, even each of his fingers, spoke of completeness, and gave off a stillness that nothing could destroy.
zh: 清晨，[[NPC1]]手持钵盂，静静走出园门去乞食。他走在几百个装束相同的僧侣中间，悉达多却一眼认出了他。那个人毫无骄慢之态，平和的表情既非欢喜，亦非忧伤，仿佛从内心发出温和的微笑——那微笑，与婴孩的笑并无不同。他的面容、步态、目光，乃至每一根手指，都显示着圆满，放射着一种不可摧毁的宁静。

en: He spoke not a word; merely walking so quietly, he made himself known. The two young Samanas followed at a distance, watched him enter the city, watched him return, watched him withdraw into the shade of a mango tree with food enough only to feed a bird. They decided to fast that day.
zh: 他不讲一句话，光是这样安安静静地走路，就叫人认出了他。两个年轻沙门远远跟着，看他入城，看他归来，看他带着只够喂饱一只鸟的饭食，退到芒果树荫里。两人决定，当天禁食。

en: At dusk the heat receded; those sleeping in the open gathered under the trees. That voice rose, clear and peaceful, like the motion of light, like stars in the night sky—
zh: 黄昏，暑热消退，露宿的人们聚到树下。那个声音响起来，清晰而平和，如光之运行，如夜空的星辰——

en: Life is suffering. Suffering has its origin; the origin can be extinguished; extinction has its path. I have found this path. If you walk it, you too can put an end to all pain.
zh: 生命是苦。苦有它的来处，来处可以熄灭，熄灭有它的道路。这条路我已找到。你们若循着走，也能断灭一切痛苦。

en: He spoke of “suffering, origin, cessation, and the path,” patiently, with parables, repeating it again and again. The two young men listened until late into the night; neither moved a step.
zh: 他论述「苦、集、灭、道」，耐心地用譬喻，一遍又一遍重述。两个年轻人一直听到深夜，谁也没有挪动一步。

en: He speaks not a word; merely walking, he makes himself known.
zh: 他不讲一句话，光走路就让人认出来。

en: People call him “the Blessed One.”
zh: 人们称他为「世尊」。

en: The Night of Taking Refuge
zh: 皈依之夜

en: When the teaching in the grove ended, the night was already deep. Among those sleeping in the open, many pilgrims came forward and asked to join {{e_sengtuan|गौतम का संघ}}—the company of monks who follow the Buddha, wander the four directions, and keep the precepts. {{e_qiaodamo|गौतम}} looked at them and received them one by one.
zh: 园林中的讲法结束时，夜已经深了。在园中露宿的人群里，许多朝圣者走上前去，请求加入{{e_sengtuan|佛陀僧团}}——追随佛陀、云游四方、守戒修行的僧人群体。{{e_qiaodamo|世尊}}望着他们，一一接纳。

en: You have listened to the teaching with great care. Then follow us, enter the garden of bliss, and put an end to all pain.
zh: 你们对教义听得很认真。那么，就跟从我们，进入极乐之园，断灭一切痛苦。

en: That friend who had always been shy—[[NPC1]]—suddenly pressed forward as well. His voice was tight, but there was no hesitation.
zh: 那个一向羞怯的朋友——[[NPC1]]——忽然也挤上前去。他的声音发紧，却没有犹豫。

en: I… I wish to take refuge in the Blessed One, in his teaching. Please receive me, and let me be one of the order.
zh: 我……我愿皈依世尊，皈依他的教义。请您收留我，让我做僧团的一员。

en: He was received. That night he turned, searching urgently for his friend.
zh: 他被接纳了。当晚，他转身，急切地寻找自己的朋友。

en: We have both heard the Blessed One teach. I have already taken it to heart and will practise it—will you not walk the path of salvation as well? Will you still delay, still wait?
zh: 我们都听了世尊说法。我已经信受奉行——难道你不愿意也行走于得救之路吗？你还要拖延，还要等待吗？

en: My friend, you have taken that step and chosen your own path. You have always followed me a step behind; I have often wondered whether one day you could take a step without me, on your own. Now you are a man. May you walk this path; may you find salvation!
zh: 我的朋友，你已经走出了那一步，选择了自己的路。你一直落后一步跟从我，我常常想：你是否有一天能没有我，独立走出一步？现在，你是个男子汉了。愿你沿这条路走下去，愿你得到救赎！

en: Speak, my dear friend—say that you too can only swear refuge to the Buddha!
zh: 说呀，我亲爱的朋友，说你也只能向佛陀宣誓皈依！

en: You have already heard my blessing. I say it again: may you walk this path; may you find salvation.
zh: 你已经听到我的祝福了。我再说一次：愿你沿这条路走下去，愿你得到救赎。

en: In an instant [[NPC1]] understood: his friend was about to leave him. His tears welled up.
zh: 一瞬间，[[NPC1]]明白了：他的朋友就要离开他了。他的眼泪涌了上来。

en: Do not forget: you now belong to the Buddha's order. You have given up home and parents, birth and wealth, friendship, and the wishes of the self—this was your own desire. Tomorrow I shall leave you.
zh: 别忘了，你现在已经属于佛陀的僧团。你抛弃了家庭和父母，抛弃了出身和财富，抛弃了友谊，也抛弃了自我的愿望——这正是你自己的心愿。明天，我就要离开你了。

en: The two friends walked a long time in the grove, lay down, and still could not sleep. Again and again he asked why his friend would not take refuge; the other only waved his hand and would not say. At dawn an old monk called the newly received together and distributed the {{e_sengyi|पीली काषाय}}—to put it on was to bid farewell to home, wealth, and the old self.
zh: 两个朋友在林中长久地漫步，躺下，又久久无法入眠。他再三追问朋友不肯皈依的原因，对方只是摆手，不肯说。第二天清晨，一位老僧召集新皈依的人，分发{{e_sengyi|黄色僧衣}}——披上它，就意味着告别家庭、财富与旧我。

en: [[NPC1]] embraced the friend of his youth and put on the yellow robe. From then on he stayed, and was no longer anyone's shadow.
zh: [[NPC1]]拥抱了他青年时代的朋友，披上黄衣。从此，他留了下来，不再是谁的影子。

en: This is the first time in his life he has not followed his friend.
zh: 这是他人生第一次没有跟着朋友走。

en: From now on he belongs to the Buddha's order.
zh: 从此他属于佛陀的僧团。

en: The Crack in the Teaching
zh: 论法裂缝

en: The next day the young man met the Blessed One in the grove. He greeted him with respect and gathered courage to ask for speech. The Blessed One silently consented.
zh: 第二天，年轻人在园中遇见世尊。他恭敬问安，鼓起勇气请求交谈。世尊默默首肯。

en: Rare Blessed One, yesterday I had the fortune to hear your profound teaching. My friend has taken refuge with you, and I shall continue my own seeking.
zh: 希有世尊，昨日我有幸聆听您的深妙教理。我的朋友已皈依于您，而我还将继续我的求道之旅。

en: As you wish.
zh: 随你的愿望。

en: My words may be rash, yet I would not leave without honestly telling you my thought. Will you hear a few sentences more?
zh: 我的话或许鲁莽，可我不愿没有把想法诚实告诉您就离开。您可否再听我讲几句？

en: Speak.
zh: 讲吧。

en: What I most revere in your teaching is its perfection and its clarity. You have shown this world as a complete, unbroken chain, linked by cause and effect. Never has the world been displayed so clearly: whole, unified, crystal-clear, without a gap.
zh: 您的教义最令我崇仰的，是它的完美与清晰。您指明这世界是一列圆满的、不间断的链条，由因果联缀而成。世界从未被如此清晰地展示：圆融、统一，水晶般明晰，没有任何漏洞。

en: And yet in this rounded unity there is a small crack. Your doctrine of rising above the world and obtaining salvation cannot be shown, cannot be proved—through this little gap a breach appears in the one eternal law of the world. Forgive me for raising this objection.
zh: 可是，这圆融的统一之中，有一个小小的裂缝。您超出世间、得到救赎的教理，无法展示，也无法证明——通过这小小的缺口，那唯一的永恒的世界规律，出现了一道破口。请宽恕我提出这一异议。

en: The Blessed One had listened in stillness, without moving. Then he answered in a voice kind, humble, and clear.
zh: 世尊一直静静听着，一动也不动。随后，他以善意、谦和、清亮的嗓音回答。

en: You have listened with great care, descendant of Brahmins; that is praiseworthy. But do not fall into the abyss of disputation. Words may be beautiful or ugly, clever or foolish; anyone may accept them or refuse them. My teaching is not a set of arguments; its aim is not to explain this world, but to lift one out of suffering and obtain salvation. That is all.
zh: 你听得非常认真，婆罗门的后裔，这值得称道。可是，不要陷入论辩的渊薮。言辞或优美或丑陋，或聪明或愚蠢，任何人都可以接受或拒绝。我的教义并非辩言，它的目标不是解释这个世界，而是超拔苦难、得到救赎。仅此而已。

en: Please do not be angry. I have never for a moment doubted that you have attained awakening. But you reached the goal by your own seeking, through thought, meditation, and awakening—you did not learn it from a doctrine. Therefore no one else can obtain salvation through a doctrine. The experience of the moment you awoke cannot be given to anyone in words.
zh: 请不要恼怒。我从未有一刻怀疑您已经证悟。可您是以自己独自的追寻，通过思考、冥想与觉醒抵达目标的——您不是通过教义学会它的。所以，任何人也无法通过教义得到救赎。您觉醒那一刻的体验，无法以言辞传达给任何人。

en: Your teaching holds much: how to live rightly, how to leave evil, how to still {{e_lunhui|संसार}}—the ceaseless turning of life between birth and death—and reach {{e_niepan|निर्वाण}}, that still farther shore where all unrest is extinguished. But one thing it cannot contain: the secret of your own awakening. Therefore I shall go on walking my own path—leaving all dogma and all teachers, to reach my goal.
zh: 您的教义包容了许多：如何正确地生活，如何脱离邪恶，如何止息{{e_lunhui|轮回}}——生命在生死之间不停的流转——抵达{{e_niepan|涅槃}}，那熄灭一切烦恼的寂静彼岸。可有一件事它无法包括：您本人证悟的秘密。所以我要继续走自己的路——离开一切教条与导师，抵达我的目标。

en: The Blessed One's gaze lowered; his unfathomable expression showed a complete stillness.
zh: 世尊的眼光低垂，深奥莫测的表情显出彻底的宁静。

en: I hope your reasoning is not mistaken. But tell me: you have seen my order and the brothers who have taken refuge—do you think they would do better to abandon the teaching and return to a world ruled by desire?
zh: 我希望你的推论没有弄错。可是告诉我：你已见到我的僧团和皈依的兄弟们——你是否认为，他们最好抛弃教义，回到被欲望统治的尘世中去？

en: I have never had such a thought! May they all follow your teaching. I have no right to judge another man's life; I can judge only for myself. If I too became your disciple, I fear it would remain only on the surface—I would deceive myself that I was already safe, while the self slipped into the teaching and went on growing.
zh: 我从未有过这样的念头！愿他们所有人都遵循您的教义。我无权评判他人的生活，只能为自己判断。假如我也成为您的信徒，我担心这只会停留在表面——我会骗自己已经平安，而自我却潜入教义，继续生长。

en: The Blessed One gazed at this unknown young man, with a hint of a smile, and with a gesture almost imperceptible signed him to withdraw.
zh: 世尊凝视着这个陌生的年轻人，带着一丝微笑，以几乎无法察觉的姿态，示意他退下。

en: You are clever, Samana from afar; you know how to argue with skill. My friend—beware of your own excessive cleverness.
zh: 你很聪明，远方来的沙门，你懂得如何巧妙地论说。我的朋友——提防你自己过分的聪明。

en: The Blessed One walked slowly away. That smile was engraved from then on in the depths of the young man's memory.
zh: 世尊缓步走开。那微笑，从此铭刻在年轻人的记忆深处。

en: The one who dared say to his face that “the teaching lacks a corner,” and the one of whom it was said.
zh: 敢于当面指出「教义缺了一角」的人，和被指出的人。

en: The parting gift of words was about “excessive cleverness.”
zh: 临别赠言是关于「过分的聪明」。

en: Awakening
zh: 觉醒

en: The moment I walked out of {{e_qiyuan|जेतवन}}, I left my former life behind me as well. I walked slowly, alone, and suddenly understood: I was no longer a youth. Something had been shed from me, as a snake sheds its old skin—the wish to seek teachers and listen to doctrines. Even that holiest Enlightened One I had already left.
zh: 走出{{e_qiyuan|祇园精舍}}的那一刻，我把从前的生活也留在了身后。我缓缓独行，忽然明白：我已不再是青年。某种东西从我身上蜕去了，像蛇蜕去旧皮——那是寻觅导师、聆听教义的愿望。连那位最神圣的觉者，我也已经离开。

en: What was that thing I wanted to learn from teachers, which they could not teach? The self. I had always wanted to be rid of the self, to conquer the self, yet I had never conquered it; I had only deceived it, fled from it. Of all things, what I knew least was myself.
zh: 我想从教师那里学到、他们却教不了的那件事，到底是什么？是自我。我过去一直想摆脱自我、征服自我，可我从没能征服它，只是在欺骗它、逃离它。我对万有所知最少的，恰恰是我自己。

en: Why? For one reason only: I feared the self; I was fleeing the self. I sought {{e_atman|आत्मन्}} with my whole heart—that undying true Self, one with the universe—wanting to destroy the self and find the core of all things in its ruins. And precisely because of that, I lost myself along the way.
zh: 为什么？只因为一个原因：我害怕自我，我在逃避自我。我一心追寻{{e_atman|阿特曼}}——那永恒不灭、与宇宙合一的真我——想摧毁自我，在它的废墟上找到万有的核心。而正因为如此，我一路丢失了自己。

en: From today everything is reversed: I will no longer flee myself, no longer practise any doctrine. I will learn from the self, take the self as teacher. I am no longer a priest, nor a Samana in flight; {{e_lunhui|संसार}}—that old road of birth and death—I have walked to its end.
zh: 从今天起，一切颠倒过来：我不再逃离自己，不再修习任何教义。我要向自我学习，以自我为师。我不再是祭司，也不再是逃难的沙门，{{e_lunhui|轮回}}——那生死流转的老路——我已经走到头了。

en: I lifted my eyes and looked about, as if seeing this world for the first time: there gold, there deep blue, there green. Sky, river, forest, mountain—strangely beautiful. Meaning is not behind things; it is in the things themselves. Today I have at last awakened, and been born again. I will not go home—my road is ahead.
zh: 我举目四望，仿佛初次见到这个世界：那儿是金黄，那儿是湛蓝，那儿又是碧绿。天空、河流、森林、山峦，美得出奇。意义不在事物的背后，就在事物自身。今天，我终于觉醒，又获得新生。我不回家——我的路，在前方。

en: The one who decided “no longer to flee himself.”
zh: 决定「不再逃避自己」的人。

en: The hero of this story.
zh: 这个故事的主角。

en: The I in Rumour
zh: 传闻里的我

en: Before it is light I go out with the {{e_boyu|भिक्षा-पात्र}}. I have walked the lanes of {{e_sheweicheng|श्रावस्ती}} for many years; with my eyes shut I know which flagstones are sunken. The children of the city can call my name; housewives fill the bowl with food across the threshold. Some would add another spoonful; I ask them to take it back—one meal is enough; what is extra weighs a man down so he cannot walk.
zh: 天没亮我就带着{{e_boyu|乞食钵盂}}出门。{{e_sheweicheng|舍卫城}}的巷子我走了许多年，闭着眼也知道哪一段石板是凹的。城里的孩子都叫得出我的名字，主妇们隔着门槛把饭食盛进钵里，有人还要多添一勺，我便请她收回去——一餐足够，多出来的会压着人走不动路。

en: When I hold the bowl I do not speak. Some think it is a rule. It is only this: if a man is willing to share his food with you, in that moment he already has his own answer; anything I might add would be superfluous.
zh: 托钵的时候我不说话。有人以为这是规矩。其实只是因为：一个人肯把饭分给你，那一刻他心里已经有了他自己的答案，我再讲什么都是多余的。

en: The stories about me grow year by year. Some say I remember every road I walked in former lives; some say I subdued spirits in the snow mountains; and some say I practised austerity in youth, then loved ease, a fraud who quit halfway. When such words come back to the grove, the young disciples flush with anger and want to go argue. I say: let it be. Rumour itself grows old, loses its teeth, cannot walk. What truly matters is another thing—this year the people sleeping under the trees are twice last year's number.
zh: 关于我的说法，一年比一年多。说我记得住前世走过的每一条路的有，说我在雪山里降伏过精怪的也有；还有人说我早年苦修，后来贪图安逸，是个半途而废的骗子。这些话传回园子里，年轻的弟子气得脸发红，要去与人分辩。我说：随它去。传闻自己会老，会掉牙，会走不动路。真正要紧的是另一件事——今年在树下过夜的人，比去年多了一倍。

en: That is what I worry about. Many of them have come for tales of wonder, wanting to see me take a step on water, wanting to hear me speak their names from former lives. I can only speak, again and again, of [suffering], of its origin, of the path that extinguishes it—slowly, at length, all in parables they can understand. Those who stay to hear it a second time have truly come.
zh: 这才是我担心的。他们中的许多人是奔着神通故事来的，想看我在水面上走一步，想听我说出他们前世的名字。我只能一遍一遍地讲【苦】，讲它的来处，讲熄灭它的那条路——讲得很慢，很啰嗦，全用他们听得懂的比喻。肯留下来听第二遍的，才算真的来了。

en: This morning at the city gate there were two young men out of the woods. Thin, dirty, their eyes frighteningly bright. They did not press forward with the crowd to pay respects; they only followed me at a distance, all the way to the grove gate. I know such men: they have not come to take refuge; they have come to test me. The best disciples in {{e_sengtuan|गौतम का संघ}} are often of this kind; there are exceptions too—who test, then turn away, and never come back in a lifetime.
zh: 今天早上，城门口有两个从林子里出来的年轻人。瘦，脏，眼睛亮得吓人。他们没有跟着人群挤上来行礼，只是远远跟着我，一直跟到园门口。这样的人我认得：他们不是来皈依的，是来验一验我的。{{e_sengtuan|僧团}}里最好的弟子，往往就是这样的人；也有例外——验过之后掉头走掉，一辈子不再回来。

en: That is well also. This business of seeking the way was never me leading anyone. Each man has his own path; I have only arrived a step sooner, turned back, and pointed the road to those still walking.
zh: 那也很好。求道这件事，从来不是我领着谁走。人各有各的路，我不过是先到了一步，回过头，把路指给还在走的人看。

en: This man with the alms bowl—the children of the city can call his name.
zh: 托钵的这个人，城里的孩子都叫得出他的名字。

en: What he speaks of, again and again, is suffering, and the path that extinguishes it; these years, young men from every place have set out because of him.
zh: 他一遍遍讲的是苦，以及熄灭苦的那条路；这些年来，各地的年轻人都为他上路。

en: Lay Out One More Robe
zh: 多备一件衣

en: Once the heat receded, the people in the grove gathered toward the central clearing. An elder monk, carrying newly washed and sunned {{e_sengyi|पीली काषाय}}, walked quickly to the tree.
zh: 暑气一退，园中的人就往中央空地聚。一个年长的比丘捧着新洗晒的{{e_sengyi|黄色僧衣}}，快步走到树下。

en: Elder monk
zh: 老比丘

en: Blessed One, tonight I fear there will not be room to sit. The eastern clearing is full as well, and people are still standing outside the woods. Shall I ask them to come tomorrow?
zh: 世尊，今晚怕是坐不下了。东边的空地也满了，林子外头还站着人。要不要请他们明日再来？

en: No need. Room is made by people pressing together. Go and say: those sitting near, draw in your legs a little; those sitting far, do not push forward—my voice will go to them.
zh: 不必。地方是人挤出来的。你去说一句：坐得近的把腿收一收，坐得远的不用往前挤——我的声音会走过去。

en: Elder monk
zh: 老比丘

en: And another matter. At the distribution of food today, two Samanas from the forest ate not a bite. When asked, they said it was voluntary {{e_zhaijie|उपवास}}. It looks as if they have already starved a whole day.
zh: 还有一桩。今天分饭，有两个林中来的沙门一口没吃。问他们，说是自愿{{e_zhaijie|斋戒}}。看样子，已经饿了整整一天。

en: Then let them starve. They are not being polite to us; they are settling accounts with themselves: how they endured in the woods, they must first endure here too, even where there is food, before they will sit down to listen. That mind is worth more than a bowl of rice.
zh: 那就让他们饿着。他们不是跟我们客气，是在跟自己交代：从前在林子里怎么熬，今天到了有饭的地方也得先熬过去，才肯坐下来听。这份心思，比一钵饭金贵。

en: Elder monk
zh: 老比丘

en: I do not understand. Hearing the teaching is hearing the teaching—can one take it in on an empty stomach?
zh: 我不明白。听法就听法，空着肚子听得进去吗？

en: They must first make one thing clear: what I give here is not a good meal.
zh: 他们要先弄清一件事：我这里给的，不是一顿好饭。

en: Elder monk
zh: 老比丘

en: …Then what is it you give?
zh: ……那给的是什么呢？

en: A path. Whether they walk it depends on their own legs.
zh: 一条路。走不走，取决于他们自己的腿。

en: The elder monk still wanted to ask, and swallowed the words. He looked at the dark press of heads in the clearing and suddenly sighed.
zh: 老比丘还想再问，把话咽了回去。他望着空地上黑压压的人头，忽然叹了口气。

en: Elder monk
zh: 老比丘

en: Today again someone came asking for wonders. Said he wanted to see you take a step on water; then he would believe.
zh: 今天又有人来求神通。说想看您在水面上走一步，看了就信。

en: What did you answer?
zh: 你怎么答的？

en: Elder monk
zh: 老比丘

en: I said we do not do that here. They laughed, and asked how we were any different from Samanas elsewhere.
zh: 我说这里不做这个。他们就笑，说那和别处的沙门有什么两样。

en: Well answered. I saw a few in my youth who could walk on water. They are still walking on water; they will walk that way their whole lives. Men turn without cease in birth and death; you call it {{e_lunhui|संसार}}—even with water underfoot, one is still in the wheel.
zh: 答得好。会在水上走的人，我年轻时见过几个。他们至今还在水上走，一辈子就这么走过去了。人在生死里打转不停，你们叫它{{e_lunhui|轮回}}——脚下踩着水，也一样在轮子里。

en: He stood, straightened the edge of his robe, and walked toward the clearing. After two steps he looked back.
zh: 他站起身，理了理衣角，往空地走。走出两步，又回过头。

en: Tonight lay out one more robe.
zh: 今晚多备一件衣。

en: Elder monk
zh: 老比丘

en: Someone will take refuge tonight? How do you know?
zh: 今晚有人要皈依？您怎么知道的？

en: The shy come earliest and stand last. When I entered the grove I saw one who had already been standing there a long time: he never dared come forward, yet his eyes never left this side.
zh: 羞怯的人来得最早，站得最后。我进园的时候看见一个，已经在那儿站了很久：他一直不敢往前，眼睛却一直没有离开过这边。

en: The clearing is packed with people, yet he first concerns himself with two hungry guests from the woods.
zh: 空地上坐满了人，他却先关心两个饿着肚子的林中来客。

en: One word from him—“follow us”—and that very night someone took off worldly clothes and put on the yellow robe.
zh: 他一句「跟从我们」，当晚就有人脱下俗衣、披上黄衣。

en: The Missing Corner
zh: 缺的那一角

en: This morning a young man from afar stood before me, took apart what I have spoken for decades, looked it through, and then told me: a corner is missing here.
zh: 今天早晨，一个远方来的年轻人站到我面前，把我讲了几十年的东西拆开看了一遍，然后告诉我：这里缺了一角。

en: He was not wrong. He was not the first to see it, but he was the first to say it to my face, with respect. I listened and did not move. I was like that in my youth: speaking fast and exact, thinking that if the reasoning were straightened, a man could stand straight too.
zh: 他说得不错。他不是头一个看出来的人，却是头一个当着我的面、恭恭敬敬说出来的。我听着，一动也没有动。我年轻时也这样：把话说得又快又准，以为道理捋直了，人就能站直了。

en: I did not contend with him.
