Contention is easy; these two lips of mine have not lost in forty years—but if I argued him down, he would believe me all the more, and be all the less willing to walk his own stretch of road. I answered him with one short sentence, a parting gift. He will need some thirty years of walking, I think, before he knows what that sentence meant.
zh: 我没有与他争。争是容易的，我这一双嘴皮子四十年没有输过——可我若辩赢了他，他就更信我，也就更不肯去走他自己的那一段。我只回了他一句很短的话，算作临别的赠礼。他大约要走上三十年，才知道那句话是什么意思。

en: His friend stayed; last night he put on the yellow robe, and is now one of {{e_sengtuan|गौतम का संघ}}. Some will say: the one who stayed is the duller, the one who left the cleverer. I do not see it so. The one who stayed has already finished asking his questions; the one who left must still ask them through to the end, alone. Which arrives first I do not know; I know only that both are walking.
zh: 他的朋友留下了，昨夜刚披上黄衣，如今是{{e_sengtuan|僧团}}的一员。有人会说：留下的那个笨些，走掉的那个聪明。我不这样看。留下的人已经把问题问完了，走掉的人还要一个人把问题问到底。哪一个先到，我不知道；我只知道两个人都在走。

en: What I underwent that night under the tree, I cannot say. Speech is an old cart; what it can haul is limited; yet besides this cart I have nothing else in my hands. I watched him walk out the gate of {{e_qiyuan|जेतवन}}, his step very light. What I thought was: the missing corner may be a door left open for such as him.
zh: 树下那一夜我经历了什么，我说不出来。言语是一辆旧车，能拉的东西有限；可除了这辆车，我手上再没有别的。我看着他走出{{e_qiyuan|这片园林}}的门，脚步很轻。心里想的是：缺的那一角，说不定正是给他这样的人留的门。

en: Someone said to his face that his teaching lacked a corner; he did not refute it.
zh: 有人当面说他的教义缺了一角，他没有反驳。

en: After sitting a night under the tree, he spent the rest of his life speaking of the same path.
zh: 他在树下坐了一夜之后，用余生讲同一条路。

en: The Ferryman and the River
zh: 船夫与河

en: After leaving the Buddha's grove, [[NPC1]] travelled several days alone. He had been a Samana—an ascetic who left home and lived by begging—and now he had laid even that path down; his heart felt light and bright. That evening he came to a great river: the water wide, forest on both banks as far as the eye could see, dusk spreading little by little over the surface. On the shore stood a {{e_dukoucaoshe|घाट की कुटिया}}, a small house where the ferryman rested and received guests. He asked lodging; {{e_weisudewa|वासुदेव}} agreed at once, and shared with him bread, water, and mangoes. The fire crackled; this was the first night in many years he need not sleep in the open.
zh: 离开佛陀的园林以后，[[NPC1]]独自赶了几天路。他曾是个沙门——离家苦行、靠乞食为生的修道者——如今连这条路也放下了，心里反倒又轻又亮。这天傍晚，他走到一条大河边：河面宽阔，两岸是望不到头的森林，暮色正一点点漫过水面。岸边有一间{{e_dukoucaoshe|渡口草舍}}，是摆渡人歇脚待客的小屋。他请求借宿，{{e_weisudewa|船夫}}痛快地答应了，还分给他面包、水和芒果。火堆噼啪作响，这是他多年来第一次不用在露天过夜。

en: Ferryman
zh: 船夫

en: The night is cool; sleep by the fire. Tomorrow at first light I will take you across.
zh: 夜里凉，靠着火堆睡。明天一早，我渡你过河。

en: Ferryman
zh: 船夫

en: From your dress, you come from the woods. Where are you going?
zh: 看你这身打扮，是从林中来的吧。要到哪里去？

en: To the great city ahead. I am a Samana no longer—the road from here I will walk myself.
zh: 到前面的大城去。我不再做沙门了——往后的路，我要自己走。

en: Ferryman
zh: 船夫

en: Good. The river never asks where she is going, yet she always reaches the sea.
zh: 好。河水从不问她要去哪里，可她总是到得了大海。

en: At first light the ferryman set his bamboo pole; the {{e_duchuan|नाव}}—more like a great bamboo raft—slid into midstream. The wide water held a peach-coloured dawn; the {{e_yezishu|ताड़ का तट}} receded quietly in the thin mist. He had never looked at a river so; for a moment he was lost in it.
zh: 晓色初开，船夫撑起竹篙，{{e_duchuan|渡船}}——其实更像一张大竹筏——滑进河心。宽阔的水面映着桃红色的晨光，{{e_yezishu|椰子树岸边}}在薄雾里静静后退。他从未这样看过一条河，一时出了神。

en: This is a beautiful river.
zh: 这真是一条美丽的河。

en: Ferryman
zh: 船夫

en: It is. I love it more than anything. I often listen to it murmur, or gaze at it in stillness. A man can learn a great deal from a river.
zh: 的确。我爱它胜过一切。我常常聆听它低语，或者静静凝视它。人可以从一条河学会很多东西。

en: They reached the bank. [[NPC1]] felt in his empty pocket, a little ashamed.
zh: 到岸了。[[NPC1]]摸了摸空空的口袋，有些难为情。

en: Thank you, kind man. I fear I have no ferry-money for you—I have nothing.
zh: 谢谢你，善良的人。恐怕我没有船钱给你——我一无所有。

en: Ferryman
zh: 船夫

en: I can see that, and I did not expect your money. One day you will come and repay me. That too I learned from this river: the water flows away and flows back; it always returns. A safe journey to you; may your friendship be my reward.
zh: 我看得出来，也没指望你的钱。将来有一天，你自会来报答我。这也是我从这条河上学来的：水流来流去，终会回转。祝你一路平安，愿你的友谊就是我的报偿。

en: The words were strange, yet oddly kind. [[NPC1]] smiled, said farewell, and took it for a joke. He did not yet know that he would remember this morning and this river many years later; still less what the ferryman's “repay” would mean. He knew only that everyone he met on the road was well-disposed, willing to be his friend, though they themselves were the ones who should have been thanked—in his eyes, people were like children.
zh: 这话说得真奇怪，却又莫名亲切。[[NPC1]]笑着道了别，只当是一句玩笑。他还不知道，这个清晨和这条河，他许多年后还会想起；更不知道船夫那句“报答”究竟是什么意思。他只知道，一路上遇见的人都心存善意、愿意作他的朋友，尽管他们自己本应是受感谢的一方——在他眼里，人们都像孩子。

en: The seeker who has just left the Buddha and taken the road alone, penniless.
zh: 刚离开佛陀、独自上路的求道者，身无分文。

en: The ferryman said he would come back one day to repay him—remember this river.
zh: 船夫说，他日后还会回来报答——记住这条河。

en: The Lady in the Palanquin
zh: 轿中的贵妇

en: Before he entered the city, [[NPC1]] came upon a train of menservants and maids beside a beautiful unwalled garden outside the walls: each carried a gift-box. In the middle of the procession was a splendid palanquin borne by four men, a coloured awning, a crimson cushion, gold thread on the curtains. He had lived three years in the woods by begging; never had he seen such state. He stood at the garden entrance and watched the procession approach in its splendour.
zh: 进城之前，[[NPC1]]在城外一座没有围墙的美丽园林旁，遇见一队男女仆从：每人手捧礼盒。行列中间是一顶四人抬的华美轿子，彩色的阳篷，大红的坐垫，轿帘上绣着金线。他在林中以乞讨为生三年，何曾见过这样的排场，便伫立在园林入口，看这支队伍浩浩荡荡地走近。

en: In the palanquin sat a lady, [[NPC2]]. Beneath a high coil of hair was a face both brilliant and intelligent: a small mouth, crimson, like a newly picked fig; the brows drawn cleverly into an arc; a pair of black eyes, clever and keen; the neck smooth and long. She wore a gown of bright green and gold; wide gold bracelets on her wrists; in her hand a {{e_kongqueshan|मोर-पंखा}} stirred lightly, the eye-spots on the feathers flashing.
zh: 轿中端坐着一位女主人[[NPC2]]。高高绾起的发髻下，是一张艳丽而聪慧的脸：嫣红的小嘴像一枚新摘的无花果，眉毛巧妙地描成弧形，一双黑眼睛聪明而敏锐，颈项光洁修长。她身着艳绿与金黄相间的礼服，腕上套着宽大的金镯，手里一把{{e_kongqueshan|孔雀羽扇}}轻轻摇着，扇面的眼斑一闪一闪。

en: He had never seen such beauty; his heart filled with joy. As the palanquin passed him he bowed low; when he rose he met those intelligent eyes. For an instant the beautiful woman inclined her head and smiled, then vanished with her servants into the depths of the garden. He stood where he was, greedily breathing the unknown perfume that lingered in the air, his heart beating hard—a feeling he had not known for half a lifetime.
zh: 他从未见过这样的美，心里充满喜悦。轿子从身旁经过时，他深深躬身行礼，起身时正迎上那双聪慧的眼睛。只一瞬，那美丽的女人向他颔首微笑，随即在仆从的簇拥下消失在园林深处。他站在原地，贪婪地呼吸着空气里残留的、不知名的香气，心怦怦直跳——这种感觉，他已陌生了半生。

en: Servant
zh: 仆从

en: Out of the way! What dirty Samana is this, blocking the garden gate, staring at the lady?
zh: 让开让开！哪来的脏沙门，也配挡在园子门口，盯着夫人看？

en: The servants' looks, scornful and dismissive, came at him like needles. [[NPC1]] lowered his head and for the first time examined himself with care: tangled hair full of dust, a torn loincloth barely covering him, bare feet. A shame he had never felt rose in him—in the woods he had been proud of poverty; at this garden gate he suddenly felt himself only a beggar. I cannot enter this garden like this, he thought, and could not help laughing aloud.
zh: 仆人们的目光轻蔑又不屑，像针一样扎过来。[[NPC1]]低下头，第一次认真打量自己：纠结的长发沾满尘土，一条破腰布勉强蔽体，赤着脚。一股从未有过的羞愧涌上心头——在林中，他以贫穷为荣；可在这座园子门前，他忽然觉得自己只是个乞丐。我不能像这样走进这座园林，他想着，不禁笑出了声。

en: He asked passers-by about the garden and its mistress. She was, it seemed, of these {{e_dachengjiexiang|महा नगर की गलियाँ}}, the most famous {{e_mingji|गणिका}}—that is, a woman of means and art who chooses her own lovers, famed for song, speech, and the arts of love, held in honour, not an ordinary woman of the streets. She was known also for a sure eye and a proud temper: many young men who came with rich gifts never even passed her garden gate. Besides this villa outside the walls she had a house in the city.
zh: 他向路人打听那座园子和它的女主人。原来，她是这座{{e_dachengjiexiang|大城街巷}}中最有名的{{e_mingji|名妓}}——所谓名妓，就是有财有艺、自己挑选情人的高级艺妓，以歌舞、谈吐与情爱之艺闻名，备受尊敬，并非寻常的风尘女子。她还以眼光准、脾气傲闻名：多少捧着厚礼上门的年轻人，连她的园门都进不去。除了这座城外的园林别墅，她在城里还有一座宅第。

en: Then I have entered this city under a lucky star, he thought. That one smile had lit a fire in his heart. He came into the city with a single aim; for that aim he surveyed the whole town, wandering the maze of lanes, watching shops, crowds, palanquins coming and going. This prosperous city told him everywhere: here everyone has money, and everyone loves money. For the first time in his life he had a clear “want”: he wanted fine clothes, costly shoes, a bag full of coin—wanted to walk into that garden with dignity, and see those eyes again. At the thought he himself was startled: a man who had thrown everything away had things he wanted once more.
zh: 那么，我是在一颗幸运之星的照耀下进了这座城，他想。那一个微笑，在他心里点起了一把火。他走进城来，只有一个目标；为了这个目标，他巡视了整座城邑，在迷宫般的街巷里四处游荡，看商铺、看人群、看轿子来来往往。这座繁华大城处处在告诉他：这里人人有钱，也人人爱钱。他生平第一次有了清清楚楚的“想要”：想要华美的衣服、名贵的鞋子、满袋的钱财——想要堂堂正正地走进那座园林，再见到那双眼睛。想到这里，他自己也吃了一惊：一个抛弃了一切的人，竟又有了想要的东西。

en: One in the palanquin, one outside it.
zh: 一个在轿子里，一个在轿子外。

en: The mistress of this garden; her red lips like a fresh fig.
zh: 这座园子的女主人，红唇像新鲜的无花果。

en: A Poem for a Kiss
zh: 以诗换吻

en: The next day he shaved his beard, combed his hair, smoothed on pomade, and waited at the garden entrance in the afternoon. When the palanquin returned he had a servant announce: a young Brahmin requested an audience. The servant led him silently to a pavilion in the garden; [[NPC1]] was reclining on a couch, playing with the fan in her hand.
zh: 第二天，他刮净胡须，梳好头发，抹上发膏，午后在园林入口恭候。轿子回来时，他托仆人传话：一位年轻的婆罗门求见。仆人领他默默走进园中一座凉亭，[[NPC1]]正斜倚在长椅上，玩弄着手里的羽扇。

en: It was you yesterday, waiting for me outside the garden? But yesterday you still wore a beard, your long hair full of dust; today you seem another man.
zh: 昨天站在园子外面迎候我的，就是你？可昨天你还蓄着胡须，长发上沾满灰尘，今天倒像换了个人。

en: You observe well; nothing escapes your eyes. I was a Brahmin's son; I left home to seek the way, and was a Samana for three years—now I have thrown even that path aside. The first person I met before I entered the city was you. I have come to ask you to be my friend and teacher: the arts in which you excel, I know nothing of.
zh: 你观察得很好，什么都逃不过你的眼睛。我曾是婆罗门之子，为求道离家，做过三年沙门——如今连那条路也抛下了。入城之前，我遇到的第一个人就是你。我来，是想请你作我的朋友和导师：你所擅长的技艺，我一无所知。

en: When she heard this, she laughed aloud.
zh: 她听罢，笑出声来。

en: Never has such a thing happened—a Samana from the woods coming to seek instruction from me! The young men who come here, even descendants of Brahmins, all wear fine clothes, costly shoes, hair scented, purses full of gold, and gifts worth offering. Do you understand, Samana from the woods?
zh: 从未有过这样的事——一个林中的沙门，竟来求师从于我！到我这里来的年轻人，包括婆罗门的后裔，个个穿着华丽的衣服、名贵的鞋子，头发飘香，袋中装满金钱，还带着拿得出手的礼物。你懂了吗？林中来的沙门？

en: I understand very well. How could I fail to understand words from so lovely a mouth? But I have already begun to learn from you: yesterday I shaved my beard and put on pomade. What I lack is already limited—clothes, shoes, and money, that is all.
zh: 我非常明白。从这样可爱的嘴里说出的话，我怎能不明白？可我已经开始向你学习了：昨天我就刮掉了胡子、抹上了发膏。我所缺乏的已然有限——衣服、鞋子和钱财而已。

en: Yes, and that is not enough. He must have fine clothes, costly shoes, a purse full of gold, and many gifts prepared for me.
zh: 是的，还不够。他必须有华丽的衣服、名贵的鞋子，口袋里装满钱财，还要为我准备许多礼物。

en: Then I will exchange what I have learned. I know thought, I know waiting, I know {{e_zhaijie|उपवास}}.
zh: 那么，我用我所学的来换。我会思想，我会等待，我会{{e_zhaijie|斋戒}}。

en: Fasting—the art of starving, of subduing desire; one who can fast is not driven by hunger, and can wait in quiet. These were three arts she did not understand.
zh: 斋戒——忍饥挨饿、降伏欲望的本事；会斋戒的人不被饥饿驱赶，可以安静地等待。这是她听不懂的三样技艺。

en: Nothing else?
zh: 没有别的吗？

en: Ah, yes—I can make poems as well. May I exchange a poem for a kiss?
zh: 噢，对了，我还会做诗。我可否用一首诗，换你一个吻？

en: If your poem pleases me, of course. What sort of poem?
zh: 如果你的诗让我满意，当然可以。是什么样的诗？

en: He thought a moment, then recited in a clear voice: The beautiful lady proceeds toward her garden; a dark Samana stands at the garden gate; he gazes upon that lotus, and bows himself low—better to offer sacrifice to her beauty than to the gods! She clapped loudly; the gold bracelets on her wrists rang.
zh: 他思索片刻，朗声吟道：美丽的女主人向她的园林行进，黧黑的沙门伫立在园林入口；他注目那朵莲花，深深躬下身去——与其向诸神奉献祭礼，何如献祭于美丽的她！她听了大声鼓掌，腕上的金镯玎玲作响。

en: Your poem is quite good, dark Samana. To give you a kiss for this poem, I lose nothing at all.
zh: 你的诗真不错，黧黑的沙门。为这首诗给你一个吻，我实在一无所失。

en: With her eyes she drew him near. His lips met those red lips, just like a newly picked fig—she kissed him deeply in return; in that kiss lay so rich a learning: conquest, refusal, and temptation besides. He stood motionless, like a child, astonished that this learning should be so vast and so deep.
zh: 她以目光引他走近。他的双唇吻上那恰如新摘无花果的红唇——她深深地回吻他，这一吻里竟藏着如此丰富的学问：征服、推拒，又是诱惑。他站着一动不动，像个孩子，惊讶于这学问竟如此博大精深。

en: Then a servant entered the pavilion and whispered a few words at her ear—a guest had arrived.
zh: 这时仆人进亭，在她耳畔低语了几句——有客人登门了。

en: Leave here quickly; let no one see you. I will see you again tomorrow.
zh: 你快离开这儿，别让任何人看见。我明天再见你。

en: She had a servant bring a {{e_baichangpao|श्वेत वस्त्र}} for him, led him out of the garden by a winding path, and told him to go at once, leaving no trace. He walked out of the garden with the folded robe under his arm, well satisfied—two days in the city, and he had already kissed the most beautiful woman in it.
zh: 她令仆人取来一件{{e_baichangpao|白色长袍}}送给他，又领他沿迂回的小径出园，嘱咐他尽快、不留影踪地离开。他臂下挟着叠好的长袍走出园林，心满意足——进城才两天，他已经吻过了全城最美的女人。

en: One named a price, one bargained—his counter-offer was three arts and a poem.
zh: 一个开价，一个还价——他还的价是三种本事和一首诗。

en: The one whose red lips are like a fresh fig.
zh: 红唇如新鲜无花果的人。

en: The Merchant's Interview
zh: 富商的面试

en: Introduced by the mistress of the {{e_mingjihuayuan|गणिका का उद्यान}}, [[NPC2]] called on the richest merchant in the city. Servants led him over luxurious carpets into a hall. The master of the great house, [[NPC1]], came in quickly: greying hair, shrewd and guarded eyes, sensual lips—a man who took business as his life. Before he spoke he looked the visitor over from head to foot. Host and guest greeted each other as friends.
zh: 经{{e_mingjihuayuan|名妓花园}}的女主人引荐，[[NPC2]]登门拜访城中最富有的商人。仆从引他走过豪华的地毯，来到一间厅堂。豪宅的主人[[NPC1]]快步走进来：斑白的头发，精明而颇有城府的眼神，肉感的嘴唇——一个把生意当作性命的人。主人还未开口，先把他从头到脚打量了一遍。宾主朋友式地相互问安。

en: I hear you are a Samana, a learned man. Yet you come seeking to serve a merchant—then you are in difficulties, I suppose?
zh: 我听说，你是一位沙门，一位博学的人。你却来求效力于一个商人——那么，你是陷入窘境了吧？

en: No. I have never been in difficulties. I have no property; if that is what you mean, I have nothing, of course—but I am so by choice, therefore I am not in want.
zh: 不。我从未陷入窘境。我没有任何财产，如果你指的是这个，我当然一无所有——但我是甘愿如此，所以我并不窘迫。

en: But you have nothing; how do you live? Always on other men's property?
zh: 可你一无所有，靠什么生活呢？难道一直靠他人的财产？

en: For nearly three years I have had not a coin, and never thought of the question. Besides, a merchant also lives by other men's property, does he not?
zh: 将近三年，我身无分文，从未想过这个问题。再说，商人也是依赖他人的财产生存，不是吗？

en: True. But a merchant does not take others' goods for nothing; he exchanges his own. You have nothing; what do you give? What have you learned that you can give?
zh: 说得对。但商人不白拿别人的东西，他是以自己的货物来交换。你一无所有，拿什么付出？你曾学会了哪些可以付出的东西？

en: Everyone gives what he has: the soldier gives strength, the teacher instruction, the farmer rice, the fisherman fish. As for me—I know thought, I know waiting, I know {{e_zhaijie|उपवास}}.
zh: 人人都付出他所拥有的：士兵付出体力，教师付出教诲，农民付出稻米，渔民付出鱼。至于我——我会思想，我会等待，我会{{e_zhaijie|斋戒}}。

en: Is that all? Then of what use is fasting?
zh: 就这些吗？那么，斋戒又有什么用处？

en: Of great value. When a man has nothing to eat, the wisest thing is to fast. If I could not fast, I should have to scramble today to find some work, because hunger would drive me to act. As it is, I can wait in quiet, without haste, without want, keeping hunger at a distance for a long time, mocking hunger. So fasting is of use, sir.
zh: 极有价值。一个人没东西可吃的时候，最聪明的事就是斋戒。假如我不会斋戒，今天就得慌慌张张找点活儿干，因为饥饿会驱使我行动。而事实上，我可以安静地等待，不急躁，不窘迫，长时间避开饥饿、嘲弄饥饿。所以斋戒有用，先生。

en: A sharp tongue. But in my house, skill of the mouth will not buy a meal.
zh: 好一张利嘴。可在我这里，嘴上功夫换不来饭吃。

en: Then please try the skill of my hands.
zh: 那就请您试试我手上的功夫。

en: The merchant brought a document and ordered him to read it aloud on the spot. It was a contract of sale; he looked at the page and read it through, not a word wrong. The merchant then handed him paper and brush and asked him to write a few sentences. He took up the brush, wrote, and gave it back.
zh: 商人取来一份案卷，命他当场朗读。那是一项售货契约，他目视案卷，一字不差地朗声读完。商人又递上纸笔，请他再写几句话。他提笔写罢，交还回去。

en: The merchant unfolded the paper and saw two lines: Writing, though fair, is not so fair as thought; wit, though fair, is not so fair as patience.
zh: 商人展开纸，只见上面是两行字：写作虽美，莫如沉思；机智虽美，莫如能忍。

en: Written indeed with brilliance! … We have much still to discuss. Today I invite you first as a guest, to stay in my house.
zh: 写得的确精彩！……我们还有许多事可以商讨。今天，我先邀请你作为客人，住在我家里。

en: In this interview the one being tested was unhurried; it was the examiner whose heart moved first. From then on servants brought him clothes and shoes, and attended him at the bath each day; in the rich merchant's house there were two fine meals a day, yet he took only one, and touched neither meat nor wine. He listened much and spoke little, remembering the garden mistress's counsel—not to be a servant full of servility, but an equal counterpart. The merchant had judged countless men, and for the first time met a hireling who did not take his rice-bowl as a serious matter; astonished and admiring, he gradually put important letters and papers into his hands. The servants said privately: this new guest was more like another master of the house.
zh: 这场面试里，应试的人不慌不忙，考校的人倒先动了心。从此，仆从给他送来衣服和鞋子，每日服侍他沐浴；富商家中一日两餐，丰盛精美，他却一天只进一餐，荤酒不沾。他听得多，说得极少，牢记着花园女主人的叮嘱——不作奴态十足的仆从，要作平等的对手。商人阅人无数，头一回遇见不把饭碗当回事的伙计，又惊又佩，渐渐把重要的信件与文书都交到他手上。仆人们私下议论：这位新客人，倒像是宅子的另一位主人。

en: One examines, one answers—the one answering called fasting the wisest thing.
zh: 一个考校，一个应答——应答者把斋戒说成最聪明的事。

en: The richest man in the city, and the one most given to worry.
zh: 全城最有钱、也最爱发愁的人。

en: Love and Commerce
zh: 情爱与生意

en: In those years [[NPC1]] lived a double life in the city. At the appointed hour each day he put on fine clothes and costly shoes and went to visit [[NPC3]]—a woman beautiful and clever, whose profession was love. With her he passed from a child who knew nothing of love to her proudest pupil, lover, and friend.
zh: 那几年，[[NPC1]]在城里过着一种双重的生活。每天约定的时刻，他穿上华丽的衣服、名贵的鞋子，去拜访[[NPC3]]——一位以情爱为业、美丽而聪明的女子。在她那里，他从一个对情爱一无所知的孩子，渐渐成了最得意的弟子、恋人与朋友。

en: One who cannot give pleasure will not receive it. Every gesture, every caress, every look has its own secret. After delight, one must go on admiring one another, then part with grace—so there is no satiety, and none of that terrible sense of using or being used.
zh: 不能付出快乐的人，也得不到快乐。每一个姿态、每一次抚摸、每一个眼神，都有它独特的秘密。欢好之后，要继续彼此爱慕，再得体地分开——这样才不会厌腻，也不会有玩弄或被玩弄的可怕感觉。

en: He learned quickly; every lesson pleased her. Yet only she herself vaguely felt: this man treated everything as a lesson; his heart hung in mid-air, and never truly came down.
zh: 他学得快，样样课业都令她满意。可只有她自己隐约觉得：这个人把一切都当作课业，心是悬在半空的，从不真正落下来。

en: And in business he was still more an outsider. His master [[NPC2]] was cautious and small in his cares, glad of a deal, anxious over a shipment, wrinkles gathering on his brow, sleepless at night, taking profit and loss as his life; he treated it only as a game—the rules he did his best to learn, the game itself never moved his heart. When he won, he smiled mildly; when he lost, he only smiled as well: a wretched transaction.
zh: 而在生意场上，他更是个局外人。东家[[NPC2]]谨小慎微，为一笔交易欢喜，为一批货发愁，额上添皱纹，夜里睡不着，把盈亏当作性命；他却只当游戏——规则他尽力去学，游戏本身却动不了他的心。赢了，他淡然一笑；亏了，他也只笑一笑：这笔交易真糟糕。

en: Once the master sent him to a village to buy a lot of rice. When he arrived, the rice had already been bought by another merchant. He was not angry; he simply stayed in the village: he entertained the farmers, gave the children small coins, and went to a lively wedding; a few days later he returned, well satisfied.
zh: 有一次，东家派他去一个村落收购一批稻米。他赶到时，稻子已经被另一个商人买走了。他却不恼，索性在村里住下：款待当地的农夫，给孩子们零钱，还赴了一场热闹的婚宴，几天之后，满意而归。

en: You have come back empty-handed! The rice is gone, and you stayed several days for nothing—wasting my time and my money!
zh: 你空着手回来了！稻子没了，你还白白住了好几天——浪费了我的时间和钱财！

en: Do not scold, my dear friend; scolding solves nothing. Since a loss has been suffered, let me bear it. I am very satisfied with this journey: I met many people, children sat on my knee and played, farmers showed me their fields—no one took me for a merchant.
zh: 别责骂，我亲爱的朋友，责骂解决不了任何问题。既然蒙受了损失，由我来承担好了。我这趟非常满意：认识了许多人，孩子们坐在我膝上玩耍，农夫带我参观了他们的田地——没有人把我当作商人。

en: All that is well enough. But you are in fact a merchant! Did you make this journey only for amusement?
zh: 这一切当然不错。可你实际上就是商人！难道作这番行程，只是为了玩乐吗？

en: Of course I went for amusement; why not? I made new friends, gained friendship and trust. If it had been you, seeing the business could not be done, you would have hurried back in a temper, and time and money would truly have been lost. The day you feel I have harmed your affairs, you need only say so, and I will go my own way. Until that day, let us remain good friends!
zh: 我当然是为了玩乐才去的，何乐而不为呢？我认识了新朋友，获得了友情和信任。若换成你，一看生意做不成，气急败坏地立刻赶回，时间和金钱才真的损失掉了。哪一天你觉得我坏了你的事，只需说一声，我就走自己的路。在那一天到来之前，我们还是作好朋友吧！

en: The master looked at him, angry and helpless—this hireling never feared a loss, yet success always fell into his hands of its own accord; a strange thing.
zh: 东家望着他，又气恼又无奈——这个伙计从不怕亏本，可成功总自然而然地落到他手里，真是件怪事。

en: Love and commerce turned like a wheel, round after round. Some call this cycle {{e_lunhui|संसार}}: life turning without cease between birth and death, a man trapped in the wheel, still thinking he is going forward. Even the {{e_touzi|पासे}} at the gambling table he played without a change of face, staking a fortune on a throw—money to him was only a counter in a game. No one knew how many more turns this game would take, or in which year it would end.
zh: 情爱与生意，就像车轮转了一圈又一圈。有人把这种循环叫作{{e_lunhui|轮回}}：生命在生死之间流转不息，人困在轮子里，还以为自己在往前走。连赌桌上的{{e_touzi|骰子}}，他也玩得面不改色，一掷千金——金钱于他，不过是游戏里的筹码。只是没有人知道，这场游戏还要再转多少圈，转到哪一年才是个头。

en: Three people: the one who teaches “the art of love,” the one anxious over losses, and the one anxious over neither.
zh: 三个人：教“爱的艺术”的、为亏本着急的、一个都不着急的。

en: The anxious one is the master; the unanxious one was once a Samana.
zh: 着急的那个是东家，不着急的那个曾是个沙门。

en: Death of the Songbird
zh: 歌鸟之死

en: One night, after years of sinking, [[NPC1]] and [[NPC2]] sat under a tree in the garden. Her look was grave; sadness and weariness could not be hidden in her speech. She asked him to tell again the story of {{e_qiaodamo|गौतम}}—that Enlightened One people call the Buddha; Buddha meaning “the awakened one.” How clear his eyes, how peaceful his smile, how complete his bearing—she could never hear enough.
zh: 沉沦多年后的一个夜晚，[[NPC1]]与[[NPC2]]坐在园中的一棵树下。她表情庄重，言语间藏不住哀伤与倦怠。她请他再讲一讲{{e_qiaodamo|乔答摩}}的故事——那位人称佛陀的觉者；佛陀，就是“觉悟的人”。他的眼睛如何清澈，微笑如何安详，仪态如何圆满——她总是听不够。

en: One day, perhaps before long, I too shall become a disciple of this Buddha. I will offer my garden to his order—those monks in yellow robes who wander with their bowls. I want to find consolation for the heart in his teaching.
zh: 将来有一天，也许就在不久之后，我也要作这位佛陀的信徒。我要把我的花园献给他的僧团——那些披黄衣、托钵乞食、云游四方的僧人。我想在他的教义里，找到心灵的慰藉。

en: Yet having said this, she drew him to love. That time her eyes held tears; with extreme passion she clasped him violently in her arms, as if to wring the last drop of sweetness from this impermanent joy. Never had he seen so clearly: love and death stood so near. For the first time he read the fine wrinkles at the corners of her eyes, like autumn and evening; in his own black hair there were already threads of white. He left her with a sigh, his heart full of pain and a fear he could not name.
zh: 可是说完这话，她却引诱他欢爱。那一回，她眼中含着泪，带着极度的热情，狂烈地把他紧抱在怀里，仿佛要从这无常的快乐中，榨取最后一滴甜蜜。他从未如此清晰地意识到：爱与死，竟挨得这样近。他第一次在她眼角读到细细的皱纹，像秋日与晚景；他自己乌黑的头发里，也已有了丝丝白发。他叹息着离开她，心中充满痛楚和一种说不清的恐惧。

en: That night in his own house he kept company with dancing girls and wine, and did not go to bed until after midnight. In those years he was long since not the man he had been: he had become a gambler to be feared, the {{e_touzi|पासे}} staking a fortune on a throw, spending to vent his contempt for money, then hating himself in the morning when he woke. This night he was tired and restless, his heart full of a pain hard to speak; tears were near to falling.
zh: 当夜，他在自己的住宅里以舞女和酒为伴，喝到午夜之后才上床。那几年，他早已不是从前的人：他成了令人生畏的赌徒，{{e_touzi|骰子}}一掷千金，用挥霍来发泄对金钱的轻蔑，又在醒来的清晨痛恨自己。这一夜，他疲倦而焦躁，心中充满难言的痛苦，泪水几欲夺眶。

en: Toward dawn he at last drifted into sleep and dreamed: the {{e_jinlongniao|सोने के पिंजरे का गायक पक्षी}} she kept in a small gold cage, which used to sing sweetly every morning, was silent this morning. He thought it strange, and looked close into the cage: the little bird lay stiff at the bottom, already dead. He held the dead bird in his hand a while, then threw it into the road—and in that same instant he was struck with terror, his heart wrung as by a hand, as if he had thrown away with this dead bird everything in himself that was good and of worth.
zh: 破晓时分，他终于迷迷糊糊睡去，做了一个梦：她养在一只小巧金笼里的那只{{e_jinlongniao|金笼歌鸟}}，往常每天清晨婉转歌唱，今天早晨却寂然无声。他觉得奇怪，凑近笼子往里看：小鸟僵直地躺在笼底，已经死了。他把死鸟托在手里放了一会儿，随后扔到了路上——就在同一瞬间，他大惊失色，心像被一只手狠狠绞住，仿佛他已把自己身上所有善良和有价值的东西，都随这只死鸟一起抛弃了。

en: Waking from the dream he was swallowed by a great sorrow, sick to the point of vomiting, as if he had drunk sour, spoiled wine. He loathed the scented hair, the wine on his breath, the slack skin—and loathed himself more. He felt he had wasted his life without worth, without meaning, like a survivor of shipwreck on the shore.
zh: 从梦中惊醒，他被一种巨大的悲哀吞没，恶心欲呕，像喝了酸腐的酒。他厌恶洒了香水的头发，厌恶嘴里的酒气，厌恶松弛的皮肤——更厌恶他自己。他觉得自己已经毫无价值、毫无意义地浪费了自己的生命，像海岸上一个遭了船难的幸存者。

en: He went sombrely into his own garden, shut the gate tight, and sat a whole day under a mango tree, reviewing his life from the beginning: the praise of his youth, the austerities in the woods, the morning of hearing the teaching… Had he left all those people only to become such a rich man as this? When night fell he stood, bid farewell to the mango tree, to the garden, to this city, and did not return.
zh: 他神情黯然地走进自己的花园，闭紧园门，在一棵芒果树下坐了整整一天，从头回顾一生：少年时的赞誉、林中的苦修、听法的清晨……难道他离开所有那些人，就是为了成为今天这样一个富人吗？夜幕降临，他站起身，与芒果树道别，与花园道别，与这座城市道别，一去不返。

en: When she heard he had vanished, she was not surprised—she had long foreseen this day. She went silently to the gold cage by the window, opened the little door, and lifted out the bird. The bird flew lightly away; she watched a long time as it vanished in the far sky.
zh: 她得知他失踪的消息，并不惊讶——她早就预料到会有这一天。她默默走近窗边的金笼，打开小门，捧出那只小鸟。小鸟翩然飞去，她久久目送它消失在远空。

en: The one who dreamed the caged bird had died.
zh: 梦见笼中鸟死去的人。

en: The owner of the golden cage.
zh: 金笼的主人。

en: Om at the Riverbank
zh: 岸边闻唵

en: After leaving the city, [[NPC1]] wandered into the forest, not knowing the way. He knew only one thing: he could not go back. That life he had tasted to the point of nausea—the songbird in the cage was dead, and the songbird in his heart was dead as well. He had sunk deep into {{e_lunhui|संसार}}: life turning like a wheel, desire following pain, pain following desire; and now this wheel held for him only nausea and a dead air.
zh: 离开城市之后，[[NPC1]]彷徨着走进森林，一路不辨方向。他只知道一点：再也不能回头。那种生活，他已经品味到了恶心的程度——笼中的歌鸟死了，他心里的歌鸟也死了。他深深堕进了{{e_lunhui|轮回}}：生命像车轮一样循环流转，渴望接着痛苦，痛苦接着渴望；而如今，这车轮对他只剩恶心与死气。

en: He longed eagerly for emptiness, for peace, for death. Let a bolt of lightning destroy him! Let a tiger devour him! Nothing in the world could attract him, give him pleasure, give him comfort.
zh: 他热切地希求空寂，希求安宁，希求死亡。就让一道雷电把他击毁！就让一条猛虎把他吞噬！世上再没有任何东西能吸引他，能给他快乐，能给他安慰。

en: He came to a great river in the woods. Many years before, a ferryman had taken him to this same bank of this same river—then he had been in his prime, just leaving the Buddha's city. Now he stood hesitating on the bank, so weak with weariness and hunger. Why go on? Where to? For what? Every aim had worn away; only a deep longing remained: to end this bitter, heart-sour life.
zh: 他来到林中的一条大河边。许多年以前，一位船夫曾把他渡到这同一条河的此岸——那时他正值英年，刚刚告别佛陀的城邑。此刻，他犹豫地站在岸边，疲乏与饥饿已使他非常虚弱。为什么还要前行？去往何方？为了什么？一切目标都已磨灭，只剩一种深切的渴望：结束这令人心酸的苦涩生活。

en: There was a great tree on the bank. He put his arms around the trunk and leaned, looking down at the moving water. The cold and loneliness in the water mirrored the terrible emptiness in his soul. One thought filled his heart: let go, and sink. He had come to the end of the road; only one thing was left to do—to wipe himself out, to destroy this husk of a failed life.
zh: 河岸上有一棵大树。他双臂搂住树干，俯身看着下面流动的水波。水里的冰冷和寂寥，正映照着他灵魂中可怕的空虚。一个念头充满了他的心：松开手，沉下去。他已经到了穷途末路，只剩下最后一件事可做——清除自己，摧毁这失败的生命的躯壳。

en: Let the fish in the water eat me! Eat this scoundrel, this madman—this decaying, corrupted flesh, this idle, dissipated soul!
zh: 就让水里的鱼来吃掉我！吃掉这个无赖，这个疯子——这颓废腐败的肉体，这怠惰浪荡的灵魂！

en: With a twisted look he stared at the water and saw his own face in it. He spat at the reflection; his arms loosened from the trunk, his body slid forward; he shut his eyes and threw himself toward—death.
zh: 他带着扭曲的表情瞪视水面，看见水中映出自己的脸。他向那倒影唾了一口；手臂松开树干，身体向前滑转；他闭起双眼，投向——死亡。

en: In that instant, from some distant corner of his soul, from the far past of his weary life, a sound came. The sound was only one word, one syllable. He recited it, indistinctly, without thinking: {{e_om|ॐ}}—the ancient opening and closing word of Brahmin prayer, the most sacred syllable, meaning “completeness,” which Brahmin children learn to say from the first.
zh: 就在这时，从他灵魂中某个遥远的角落，从他疲惫生活的久远往昔，传来一个声音。那声音只有一个字、一个音节。他含混地、不假思索地念诵着：{{e_om|唵}}——那是婆罗门祷文古老的起止之字，最神圣的音节，意思是“圆满”，婆罗门的孩子从小就会念。

en: In that instant the long-sleeping soul woke with a start. At once he saw how foolish his act had been: that he should be so lost, so astray, as to seek death! That he should think to buy peace by destroying the body! The shock of that word entering his heart exceeded all the torment, disillusion, and despair of these years put together. He saw clearly his wretched state, and perceived also that life cannot be destroyed.
zh: 就在这一瞬间，那久已沉睡的灵魂猛然觉醒。他立刻看清了自己的行为有多么愚蠢：他竟如此迷惘、如此失落，竟在寻求死亡！竟妄想通过毁灭肉体来换取安宁！那个字传入心中的这一刻，他所受的震动，超过这些年来所有的折磨、幻灭与绝望加在一起。他认清了自己的悲惨处境，也感知到生命的不可毁灭。

en: But it lasted only a moment. Weariness overwhelmed him; he sank down under the great tree, his head on the roots, reciting that word in a low voice as he fell into a deep sleep. The sleep was deep and without dreams; he had not slept so in a very long time.
zh: 但那只发生在刹那之间。疲劳淹没了他，他跌坐在大树下，头枕着树根，一面低声念诵着那个字，一面沉入了酣睡。这一觉深沉而无梦，他已经很久很久没有这样睡过了。

en: He had meant to drown himself in this river. In truth, that aged, weary, despairing self had already drowned in it.
zh: 他想自溺于这条河。而实际上，那个衰老、疲惫、绝望的他，已经溺在了河里。

en: He meant to destroy himself; one word saved him.
zh: 他想毁掉自己，一个字救了他。

en: That syllable Brahmin children learn to say from the first.
zh: 那个音节，婆罗门的孩子从小就会念。

en: How Beautiful the World Is
zh: 世界真美好

en: How beautiful the world has suddenly become! At morning I watch the sun rise beyond forest and mountain; at evening I watch the far sunset; at night I look up at the stars, and see the sickle moon like a little boat drifting on the dark sky. Gold, deep blue, green—this many-coloured world has been here all along: sun, moon, and stars forever shining, rivers forever running, bees forever humming. Once I took it all for empty, impermanent illusion, destined to be despised and discarded by thought. I was truly blind.
zh: 世界忽然变得这么美！清晨，我看太阳从森林和山峦那边升起；黄昏，我看远方的落日；夜晚，我仰望星辰，看镰刀似的月牙像一条小船，在黑黝黝的夜空漂游。金黄的、湛蓝的、碧绿的——这色彩缤纷的世界一直都在：日月星辰永远在照耀，江河永远在奔流，蜜蜂永远在嗡鸣。从前我却把这一切看作空虚无常的幻影，注定要被思想蔑视和抛弃。我真是瞎了眼。

en: I will no longer go to the far side of the world of appearances to chase some “reality.” I will find my place among the ten thousand things of this very life. Thought and the senses are of equal weight—behind both something ultimate is hidden. I will listen to both voices with equal care, despising neither, overvaluing neither.
zh: 我不再到现象世界的另一面去追什么“实在”了。我就在这一世万物之中，寻自己的位置。思维和感官同样重要——在两者背后，藏着某种终极的意义。我要同样专心地倾听这两种声音，不再鄙弃谁，也不再高估谁。

en: I knew long ago that my self is {{e_atman|आत्मन्}}—the undying true Self in the depths of a man—yet I never truly found it, because I always wanted to catch it in the net of thought. From now on I will only obey the voice in my own heart, without delay, without hesitation. This is the one necessary thing; everything else is meaningless.
zh: 我早知道，我的自我就是{{e_atman|阿特曼}}——人内心深处永恒不灭的真我——可我从未真正找到它，因为我总想用思想的罗网去捕捉它。从今往后，我只服从自己内心的声音，不再迟延，不再犹疑。这才是唯一必要的事，其他的一切都毫无意义。

en: It is dark. I hear the {{e_linzhongdukou|वन की नाव-घाट}} is ahead; on the bank a {{e_dukoucaoshe|घाट की कुटिया}}, the ferryman's little house for guests, with bread and water inside. Tonight I will lodge there—for the first time in many years I am no longer afraid of tomorrow.
zh: 天黑了。听说前面就是{{e_linzhongdukou|林中渡口}}，河边有一间{{e_dukoucaoshe|渡口草舍}}，是摆渡人待客的小屋，屋里有面包和水。今晚，就去那里借宿吧——许多年来，我第一次不再害怕明天。

en: The one who has just begun to see the world with “another pair of eyes.”
zh: 刚刚“换一种眼睛”看世界的人。

en: Still the same hero.
zh: 还是那个主角。

en: I Am No Longer a Beggar
zh: 我不再是乞丐

en: The first thing upon entering the city: to change my own skin. At the {{e_hebianshiji|नदी की पत्थर की सीढ़ियाँ}}—the stone stairs of the watercourse at the city's edge—I made the acquaintance of a barber's helper: first I watched him busy in the shadow of an arch, then met him praying in a temple; I told him stories of the gods, and he listened, rapt. At first light I asked him to shave my beard, comb my hair, smooth on good pomade, then bathe in the river. When the water poured over my head I felt that Samana with dusty long hair was flowing away, little by little, with the current.
zh: 进城第一件事：给自己换一张皮。我在{{e_hebianshiji|河边石级}}——大城边河道的石阶——结交了一个理发店的帮工：先是看他在拱门的阴影里忙碌，又在神庙里遇见他祈祷，我给他讲了天神的故事，他听得入了迷。天一亮，我请他刮掉胡须，梳好头发，再抹上上好的发膏，然后到河里沐浴。水从头顶浇下来的时候，我觉得那个长发沾灰的沙门，正顺着河水一点一点流走。

en: Standing before a tavern where travellers gathered, I silently held out a bowl and begged a rice cake. The cake in my hand, I was suddenly startled by myself: I was a Samana no longer; why was I still begging? A pride I had never felt seized me. I threw the cake to a dog, and stood straight, my belly empty. Perhaps tomorrow I will no longer need to beg—a man who will not beg again must first learn not to put out his hand like a beggar. From today I am no longer a beggar.
zh: 站在行客聚集的酒馆门前，我默默伸出碗，乞来一块米糕。米糕一到手，我忽然被自己吓了一跳：我已经不是沙门了，怎么还在乞讨？一股从未有过的自尊攫住了我。我把那块米糕抛给一条狗，自己腹中空空，却站得笔直。也许明天我就不再需要乞食了——一个不肯再乞讨的人，得先学会不像乞丐那样伸手。从今天起，我不再是乞丐。

en: The people here live so simply, without a single difficulty. When I was a Samana everything was hardship and unrest, and at last despair; now everything is easy, easy as learning a kiss. I need clothes, shoes, and money, that is all—small aims, too small to disturb a man's sleep.
zh: 这里的人们，生活真简单，没有一点难题。我当沙门的时候，一切都是艰难和烦恼，最终是绝望；现在一切都容易，容易得就像学一个亲吻。我需要衣服、鞋子和钱，仅此而已——这些都是小目标，小到不会搅乱一个人的睡眠。

en: These {{e_dachengjiexiang|महा नगर की गलियाँ}}, shops, feasts, gambling, men and women in an endless stream, a playground of the world—I have come. This time I have not come to look on.
zh: 这座{{e_dachengjiexiang|大城街巷}}，商铺、宴饮、赌局，男男女女川流不息，一座尘世的游乐场——我来了。这一回，我不是来旁观的。

en: The one just made new at the river, changing his own skin.
zh: 刚在河边焕然一新的那个人，正在给自己换新皮。

en: The hero of the story, still without a coin to his name.
zh: 故事的主角，这时还一文不名。

en: The Courtesan's Introduction
zh: 名妓的引荐

en: The next day he called at her house in the city. Hearing he had not eaten in two days, she had food and fruit brought, ate with him, then spoke of the business at hand.
zh: 第二天，他登门拜访她在城中的住宅。她听说他已两天没有吃饭，令人送上食物和水果，陪他进餐，然后谈起正事。

en: Things are going well. {{e_shiwami|कामस्वामी}} is expecting your visit—he is the richest merchant in the city; I have already mentioned you to him through others. Be clever, dark Samana!
zh: 事情进行得不错。{{e_shiwami|湿瓦弥}}正期待你去拜访——他是城中最富有的商人，我已经通过别人向他提过了你。聪明点，黧黑的沙门！

en: Thank you. Then how should I treat him?
zh: 谢谢你。那么，我该怎么对待他？

en: Be friendly; he has much power. But do not be too humble—I do not want you as his servant; I want you as his equal counterpart, or I shall be displeased. He is already growing old and lazy; if you please him, he will trust you greatly.
zh: 对他友善，他很有权势。但也不要过于谦逊——我不想要你作他的仆从，我要你作与他平等的对手，不然我会不高兴的。他已经开始变得衰老、懒散；只要你取悦于他，他会对你极为信赖。

en: I have noted it: be a counterpart, not a servant.
zh: 我记下了：作对手，不作仆从。

en: Eat something first. I hear you have not eaten in two days—thinking, waiting, and fasting will not fill a belly.
zh: 先吃点东西。听说你两天没吃饭了——思想、等待和斋戒，可填不饱肚子。

en: They will. One who can fast is not driven by hunger. But I will not refuse your food.
zh: 填得饱。会斋戒的人，饥饿驱赶不了他。不过你的食物，我不拒绝。

en: You are fortunate. See, door after door is opening for you. How does it happen? Have you some magic?
zh: 你很幸运。你看，一道又一道的门正为你敞开。这是怎么发生的？莫非你有魔力？

en: Yesterday I told you I can think, wait, and fast; you thought these of no use. You will understand: when a man has an aim, he is like a stone thrown into water; he finds the swiftest line to the bottom. I do nothing; I only wait, think, fast, and let myself sink—I allow nothing that disturbs the aim to enter the mind. That is what people call magic.
zh: 昨天我就说过，我会思想、等待和斋戒，你以为这些没有用。你会明白的：人有了目标，就像石子投入水中，会找到沉向水底最快的路线。我无所作为，只是等待、思考、斋戒，任凭自己沉落——我不允许任何扰乱目标的东西进入心境。这就是人们所谓的魔法。

en: Perhaps it is as you say, my friend. But if there were no me? Without my help, where would you be now?
zh: 也许的确如你所说，我的朋友。可是如果没有我呢？如果没有我的帮助，你现在会在什么地方？

en: When I first saw you at your garden gate I had already taken the first step. I resolved to learn from the most beautiful of women the secrets of love—the moment I decided, I knew it would be fulfilled. From the first look you cast at me, I knew you would help me.
zh: 在你的园林入口第一次见到你时，我已经走出了第一步。我决意师从一位最美丽的女人，学习情爱的秘密——做出决定的那一刻，我就知道必将实现。从你第一次投向我的目光里，我就知道你会帮我。

en: And if I had not wished to help you?
zh: 如果我不想帮你呢？

en: But you did wish to.
zh: 可是你确实想。

en: She listened in stillness. She liked his voice, liked his gaze—as the cleverest {{e_mingji|गणिका}} in the city, she was used to men who came with purses to seek pleasure; this was the first who spoke with her of “aims” and “magic.” At parting he kissed her, and said he hoped his gaze would always give her joy, and that good fortune would come because of her.
zh: 她静静地听着。她喜爱他的嗓音，喜爱他的目光——身为全城最聪明的{{e_mingji|名妓}}，她见惯了捧着钱袋来求欢的男人，头一回有人同她谈“目标”与“魔法”。临别，他吻她，说愿自己的目光永远使她快乐，愿好运因她而降临。

en: She pushed open door after door for him.
zh: 她替他推开一扇又一扇门。

en: Red lips, gold bracelets, a fan of feathers.
zh: 红唇、金镯、羽扇。

en: Writing, Though Fair
zh: 写作虽美

en: A strange interview. That grey-haired merchant examined me through and through: asked whether I was in want, asked how I lived, then had me read a contract and write. I took up the brush and wrote him a sentence: “Writing, though fair, is not so fair as thought; wit, though fair, is not so fair as patience.” He read it twice, his eyes bright, and at once kept me as a guest at {{e_fushangzhaidi|कामस्वामी का घर}}—that great house, carpets laid to the door, servants in flocks, money flowing in and out of the counting-room day and night. An interview that bought food, clothing, and a place to stay—not by pleading, but by a few lines.
zh: 一场奇怪的面试。那个斑白头发的商人把我考了个遍：问我窘迫不窘迫，问我靠什么活，又让我读契约、写字。我提笔写下一句话送给他：“写作虽美，莫如沉思；机智虽美，莫如能忍。”他读了两遍，眼睛发亮，当即留我作{{e_fushangzhaidi|富商宅第}}的客人——那座豪宅，地毯一直铺到门口，仆从成群，金钱日夜从账房流进流出。一场面试换来衣食与落脚之处，靠的不是哀求，是几行字。

en: In truth I gave nothing, only a few things that cannot be seen. They do business by impulse and passion: glad of a shipment, anxious over an account, wrinkles gathering on the brow, sleepless at night. I treat business as a game—the rules I learn with care, winning and losing I do not take to heart. Before long the important letters and papers were in my hands; even in urgent matters he grew used to consulting me first. He never saw through me, and often said to his friends: this Brahmin never fears a loss, yet success always falls to him—has he some magic about him?
zh: 其实我什么都没付出，只付出了几样看不见的东西。他们做生意，靠的是冲动和激情：为一批货欢喜，为一笔账发愁，额上添皱纹，夜里睡不着觉。我把生意当游戏——规则我认真学，输赢我不入心。没过多久，重要的信件和文书都交到我手上，连要紧的事，他也习惯先同我商量。他始终看不透我，常对朋友念叨：这个婆罗门从不怕亏本，成功却总落到他手里，莫非身怀魔法？

en: Thought, waiting, {{e_zhaijie|उपवास}}—these three arts are worth more than a boat of goods. One who can fast is not driven by hunger, and can sit steady at the table until the other party grows anxious first; a hungry man makes no good bargain, a hasty man strikes no good price. This the “foolish” Samanas in the woods taught me. The city people do not understand; they call it magic. In truth there is no magic in the world—to think, to wait, to fast, anyone can practise.
zh: 思考、等待、{{e_zhaijie|斋戒}}——这三样本事，比一船货物值钱。会斋戒的人不被饥饿驱赶，才能稳坐桌前，等对方先着急；饥饿的人做不成好买卖，着急的人谈不出好价钱。这是林中那些“愚蠢”的沙门教我的。城里人不懂，他们管这个叫魔法。其实世上哪有什么魔法——会思想、会等待、会斋戒，人人都能施展。

en: The one who has just passed a strange interview.
zh: 刚通过一场奇怪的面试的人。

en: The one who takes “fasting” as his capital.
zh: 把“斋戒”当本钱的人。

en: You Do Not Know True Love
zh: 你不懂得真爱

en: Another dusk. These years he often came to see her at the appointed hour; the lessons of love had long been finished, yet they still liked to talk so, at length. After delight she leaned down and gazed a long time at his face, at those eyes that had grown weary. In the gold cage by the pavilion the {{e_jinlongniao|सोने के पिंजरे का गायक पक्षी}} too had fallen quiet.
zh: 又是一个黄昏。这些年，他常在约定的时刻来看她，情爱的课业早已学完，他们却仍喜欢这样长谈。欢好之后，她俯下身，长久地注视他的面庞，注视那双已变得倦怠的眼睛。亭边的金笼里，那只{{e_jinlongniao|金笼歌鸟}}也安静了下来。

en: You are the finest of all my lovers. You are stronger than the others, quicker, and more tractable—you have mastered my arts well.
zh: 你是我所有情人当中最优秀的一个。你比别人更强壮，更敏捷，也更温驯——我的技艺，你掌握得很好。

en: You teach well, my teacher.
zh: 你教得好，我的导师。

en: Do you know how many have come to me with purses full of gold, and I have never taught them so? One day, when I am a little older, I would like to have a child with you.
zh: 你可知道，多少人捧着满袋的钱财来求我，我都没有这样教过他们。将来有一天，等我年纪再大一些，我愿意与你要一个孩子。

en: He was silent. She looked at him, then suddenly shook her head a little.
zh: 他沉默着。她望着他，忽然轻轻摇头。

en: And yet, my dear, you are still a Samana. You do not truly love me—you love no one, is that not so?
zh: 可是，亲爱的，你仍旧是一个沙门。你并不真正爱我——你不爱任何人，难道不是吗？

en: Perhaps. I am much like you—you too have no capacity for love, or how could you practise love as an art? Perhaps people like us have none.
zh: 也许是。我很像你——你也没有爱的能力，否则，你怎么会把爱作为一种技艺来从事呢？可能我们这样的人，都没有爱的能力。

en: And ordinary people? They all seem to love with great heat.
zh: 那世人呢？他们倒个个爱得轰轰烈烈。

en: Ordinary people can love—that is their secret. They are like fallen leaves, tumbling and drifting in the wind; we are like stars, moving on a set orbit, and the wind does not reach us. And precisely because of that, we cannot reach the joy that only fallen leaves have.
zh: 平凡的人们能够爱——这就是他们的秘密。他们像落叶，在风中翻滚、飘零；我们像星辰，沿着既定的轨道运行，风吹不到我们。可也正因如此，我们够不着落叶才有的那种快乐。

en: Master Star, have you ever envied the fallen leaves?
zh: 星辰先生，那你可曾羡慕过落叶？

en: I have. They fret over children, over honour, over a little gain; that anxious, sweet intensity I cannot learn.
zh: 羡慕过。他们为孩子、为荣誉、为一点利益牵肠挂肚，那种焦虑而甜美的劲头，我学不来。

en: I cannot learn it either. I can only divide love into thirty or forty arts, and teach them one by one to men.
zh: 我也学不来。我只会把爱分成三四十种技艺，一样一样教给男人们。

en: She was silent a long time. As the cleverest {{e_mingji|गणिका}} in the city, she was used to tender speeches; this was the first time anyone had spoken her inner case so plainly. Strangely, she was not angry.
zh: 她沉默了很久。身为全城最聪明的{{e_mingji|名妓}}，她听惯了缠绵的情话，头一回有人把她的底细说得这样明白。奇怪的是，她并不恼怒。

en: There you are, talking like a Samana again… But you are right. In the depths of my heart there is always a still sanctuary I can withdraw into at any time, and be myself. Very few have such a sanctuary—so, like you, I cannot learn that kind of love.
zh: 你看你，又在说沙门的话了……可你说得对。我的心底也总有一处宁静的圣地，随时可以退避进去，成为我自己。极少人有这样的圣地——所以，我和你一样，学不会那种爱。

en: At least in this moment you are my teacher, my lover, and my friend. The meaning of my present life is all here with you, not in the marketplace.
zh: 至少此刻，你是我的导师、恋人和朋友。我现时生活的意义，全在你这里，而不在生意场上。

en: She said the words “you do not know true love.”
zh: 她说出了“你不懂得真爱”。

en: The bird she keeps lives in a golden cage.
zh: 她养的鸟住在金笼里。

en: The Potter's Wheel
zh: 陶匠的旋轮

en: A potter's wheel, once started, will turn a long time, then slowly, and at last stop. The wheel of austerity in my soul, the wheel of thought, are the same: still turning, yet slower and slower, almost still. The worldliness of men seeps like damp into a dying trunk, soaking the soul heavy, weary, asleep. People call this cycle {{e_lunhui|संसार}}—the days turn round after round, and a man still thinks he is living a life.
zh: 陶匠的旋轮，一经开动会转上很久，然后渐渐缓慢，最终停息。我灵魂里的禁欲之轮、思维之轮也是这样：还在转，却越来越慢，几乎停了。尘俗像湿气钻进垂死的树干，把灵魂泡得沉重、倦怠、昏睡。人们管这种循环叫作{{e_lunhui|轮回}}——日子转了一圈又一圈，人还以为自己活在生活里。

en: I have learned to manage business, to give orders to servants; learned fine clothes, good wine, scented baths; learned also to gamble—the {{e_touzi|पासे}} thrown, thousands won, thousands lost. Only when a great stake hung undecided did I feel a little of that terrible, sweet anxiety, feel that I was still alive. I spent to vent my contempt for money, and hated myself when day came.
zh: 我学会了料理生意，对仆从发号施令；学会了华服、美酒、香汤沐浴；也学会了赌钱——{{e_touzi|骰子}}一掷，成千上万地赢，又成千上万地输。只有大笔赌金悬而未决时，我才感到一点可怕又甜美的焦虑，感到自己还活着。我用挥霍发泄对金钱的轻蔑，又在天亮时痛恨自己。

en: Ordinary people are like children. They suffer for money, for paltry pleasures and honours, and grow grey early; they grieve bitterly over a loss a Samana would only laugh at. I envy them and despise them both—envy the strength with which they can love, despise the things they love. And I smile less and less; my face has taken on the rich man's look: sombre, irritable, never satisfied. Sometimes at night I even dream of money.
zh: 世人像孩童。他们为金钱、为微不足道的享乐和荣誉受苦，华发早生；为一点沙门只会一笑置之的损失悲伤不已。我既羡慕他们，又鄙弃他们——羡慕他们爱得动的力气，鄙弃他们爱的东西。而我的笑容越来越少，脸上有了富人常有的表情：阴郁、恼怒、不知厌足。有时夜里，我竟会梦见金钱。

en: In the mirror on the bedroom wall that man grows older and uglier day by day. Sometimes I think of {{e_qiaowenda|गोविन्द}}—that friend who always used to follow behind me. He wanders now with his bowl; has he failed to know himself in a mirror? And that word {{e_om|ॐ}}, recited from childhood, that once sang aloud in my heart, now only whispers far away, almost inaudible.
zh: 卧房墙上的镜子里，那个人一天比一天衰老、丑陋。我有时会想起{{e_qiaowenda|侨文达}}——当年那个总跟在我身后的朋友。他如今托钵云游，可曾在镜子里认不出自己？还有那个从小念诵的{{e_om|唵}}字，曾在我心里高声欢唱的声音，如今只在远方轻轻私语，几乎听不见了。

en: The one who has caught “the rich man's disease.”
zh: 染上“富人的病”的人。

en: He was once a Samana.
zh: 他曾经是个沙门。

en: Unrecognised
zh: 不相识

en: Waking, he found a shaven old monk in a {{e_sengyi|पीली काषाय}} sitting before him, as if sunk in meditation. The monk had neither hair nor beard; his face was aged, yet between the brows there was an eager loyalty.
zh: 一觉醒来，他发现一位身披{{e_sengyi|黄色僧衣}}的落发老僧坐在面前，仿佛正陷入冥想。那僧人无发无须，面容老迈，眉眼间却透着一股热切与忠诚。

en: You are awake? It is not good to sleep in such a place; venomous snakes and wild beasts often come here. I am a monk of {{e_sengtuan|गौतम का संघ}}—one of those who follow the Buddha and wander with their bowls. I was travelling with companions and saw you sleeping so deeply, so I stayed to watch over you. Later I myself fell asleep; I watched very poorly, in truth.
zh: 你醒了？在这种地方睡觉可不好，这里常有毒蛇猛兽出没。我是{{e_sengtuan|佛陀僧团}}的僧人——就是追随佛陀、托钵云游的那一群。我和同伴外出游化，看见你睡得深沉，就留下来看护你。后来我自己也睡着了，实在看护得很不好。

en: Thank you for watching, Samana. The Blessed One's disciples are truly very kind.
zh: 谢谢你的守护，沙门。世尊的信徒，真是非常善良。

en: Then I will go; may you be well!
zh: 那么我走了，祝你安康！

en: The old monk bowed farewell and turned to leave. Looking at that yellow robe, he suddenly smiled and called the other's name.
zh: 老僧躬身道别，转身欲行。他望着那袭黄衣，忽然微笑着，唤出了对方的名字。

en: Wait—how do you know my name?!
zh: 等等——你怎么会知道我的名字？！

en: I know you: from the Brahmin school, from the rites of sacrifice, from the years we spent together in the Samana woods, until the moment you took refuge with the Blessed One at Jetavana—I have always known you.
zh: 我认识你：从婆罗门的学堂，从献祭的仪式，从沙门林中一同度过的岁月，直到你在祇园皈依世尊的那一刻——我一直认识你。

en: It is you! It is you! Why did I not recognise you just now? How glad I am to see you again!
zh: 是你！原来是你！我刚才为什么竟没有认出你？能再见到你，我真高兴！

en: I am very glad to see you as well. You watched over me while I slept; I thank you again—though I did not need watching.
zh: 能见到你，我也非常高兴。我睡觉时你守护了我，我再次谢谢你——尽管我并不需要守护。

en: But where are you going, old friend?
zh: 可你要去什么地方呢，老朋友？

en: Nowhere in particular. I am still on the road; I am making a journey in search of the way.
zh: 没有特别要去的地方。我仍在路途中，我在进行一次求道之旅。

en: A journey in search of the way? Forgive me—you do not look like a seeker: you wear a rich man's clothes, a gentleman's shoes; your hair is even scented. I have wandered many years, and never seen a seeker like you.
zh: 求道之旅？请你原谅——你不像个求道者：你身着富人的衣服，脚穿上流人的鞋子，头发还洒着香水。我自己云游多年，从未见过你这样的求道者。

en: You see very truly; nothing escapes your keen eyes. But the world of appearances turns without rest; clothes and the dressing of hair change all the more. I am indeed richly dressed, because I was once rich; now I am not. As for what manner of man I am now—I do not know. In that, I am as ignorant as you.
zh: 你看得很准，一切都逃不过你敏锐的眼睛。可表象的世界流转无常，衣服和发式更是变化不定。我的确衣着华贵，那是因为我曾经富有；如今不了。至于我现在是怎样一个人——我不知道。对此，我与你一样无知。

en: The old monk gazed long and doubtfully at the friend of his youth, bowed as to a man of rank, and then took to the road. He watched the yellow robe go far, smiling—he still loved this loyal, ardent friend. After this sleep, how could he not love everything in the world?
zh: 老僧犹疑地久久注视着他青年时代的朋友，像面对一位显贵般躬身行礼，然后踏上了旅程。他目送那袭黄衣远去，微笑着——他依旧爱着这个忠诚而热忱的朋友。经过了这一觉，他如何能够不去爱世上的一切呢？

en: The old monk who watched over the sleeper, and the seeker who does not look like a seeker.
zh: 守护酣睡者的老僧，和不像求道者的求道者。

en: When young, the old monk had a friend he honoured most.
zh: 老僧年轻时有个最敬爱的朋友。

en: One Third
zh: 三分之一

en: Night had fallen; the lamp in the counting-room was still lit. The master of the house, [[NPC1]], invited an old friend in the spice trade into an inner room and dismissed the servants. What he had to say concerned the lodger [[NPC2]] who had entered the house half a year before.
zh: 入夜，账房的灯还亮着。宅子的主人[[NPC1]]把做香料生意的老友请进内室，屏退了仆从。他要说的，是半年前进门的那个门客[[NPC2]]。

en: Spice merchant
zh: 香料商

en: You did not call me here to look at your new carpets. Speak: what is the worry?
zh: 把我叫来，总不是为了看你的新地毯。说吧，愁什么？

en: A man. Half a year ago that {{e_mingji|गणिका}} outside the city sent word: a Samana who could write and reckon wanted a post. I thought, of what use is a Samana? Then the man came in, in a brand-new {{e_baichangpao|श्वेत वस्त्र}}, standing straight, looked me over from head to foot first, and only then let me look at him.
zh: 愁一个人。半年前，城外那位{{e_mingji|名妓}}打发人来递话，说有个能写会算的沙门想谋个差事。我想，沙门能有什么用？结果人进了门，一身崭新的{{e_baichangpao|白色长袍}}，站得笔直，先把我从头看了一遍，才让我看他。

en: Spice merchant
zh: 香料商

en: A man who has begged, putting on airs. You kept him?
zh: 一个讨过饭的，倒摆起谱来。你留他了？

en: I did. I had him read a contract; not a word wrong. I had him write; he wrote two lines for me, and I still keep them under the paperweight on my desk. Business he learned at once: letters, accounts, dealing with people—better in every way than the old hands under me.
zh: 留了。我叫他读契约，他一字不差；叫他写字，他写了两行送我，我到今天还压在案头。生意上的事，他一学就会：信件、账目、跟人周旋，样样强过我手下那些老伙计。

en: Spice merchant
zh: 香料商

en: Then what are you worrying about?
zh: 那你还愁什么？

en: That he does not care. When he profits, he smiles; when he loses, he smiles as well, says the bargain was wretched, and sleeps just the same. I can go three nights without closing my eyes over a shipment; he sits beside me as if watching a play.
zh: 愁他不在乎。赚了，他笑一笑；蚀了，他也笑一笑，说这笔买卖真糟糕，然后照样睡得着。我为一批货能三夜合不上眼，他坐在旁边，像在看戏。

en: Spice merchant
zh: 香料商

en: Easy. Give him a third of the profit on what he handles, and let him bear a third of the loss as well. Once money touches a man, he wakes.
zh: 这好办。把他经手那部分的赢利分他三分之一，蚀本也让他担三分之一。钱一沾身，人就醒了。

en: …There is reason in that. We will do it so.
zh: ……有理。就这么办。

en: A month later the two sat in the same room again. This time the master's face was longer still.
zh: 一个月后，两人又坐在同一间屋里。这回主人的脸拉得更长。

en: Spice merchant
zh: 香料商

en: Well? Once he had a share of the profit, he took it to heart, I suppose.
zh: 如何？分了红，总该上心了吧。

en: I am the one taking it to heart. The first deal he made a profit; he turned and gave half to the porters on the quay. The second he lost; he made it up himself without a word, then went off to someone's wedding feast. I said a couple of things to him; guess what he answered.
zh: 上心的是我。头一笔他赚了，转手把一半分给码头上抬货的；第二笔蚀了，他一声不吭自己补上，掉头又去赴人家的喜宴。我说了他两句，你猜他怎么回我。

en: Spice merchant
zh: 香料商

en: What did he answer?
zh: 怎么回？

en: He said: from you I have learned what a basket of fish should sell for, what interest a loan should bring; those are your arts. But I have not learned from you how to think—that, you had better learn from me.
zh: 他说：我从你这儿学会了一篮子鱼该卖多少钱，学会了借出一笔款该收多少利息，这些是你的本事。可我没有从你这儿学会怎么思考——这一点，你最好跟我学。

en: Spice merchant
zh: 香料商

en: …He dared say that? You did not send him away?
zh: ……他真敢这么讲？你没赶他走？

en: I cannot send him. While he is here, business runs smoothly; if he goes, I fear it will not. Tell me if it is not maddening: I get up at midnight to count the books; he sleeps like a child. There are such men in this world—everything in their hands, and nothing taken as real.
zh: 赶不走。他在，生意就顺；他一走，我怕它就不顺了。你说气人不气人：我半夜爬起来数账，他睡得像个孩子。这世上竟有这样的人——什么都握在手里，又什么都不当真。

en: A master who has made his lodger's “not caring” a sickness of the heart, and the lodger who will not take it to heart no matter what.
zh: 一个把门客的「不在乎」当成心病的东家，和那个怎么也不肯上心的门客。

en: The one who worries is the grey-haired man who takes business as his life; the one spoken of came from the woods, and can think, wait, and fast.
zh: 发愁的是斑白头发、把生意当性命的那位；被议论的那个从林子里来，会思想、会等待、会斋戒。

en: At Last He Has Learned to Worry
zh: 他终于肯着急了

en: At first I was glad. At last he was willing to worry over money—that was what I had hoped for all these years. He began to chase debtors for payment, harder than I; once he could sit a whole hour with a beggar and even give him money, now he dismissed them from behind the door. I thought: good, now he looks like a man of business.
zh: 起初我是高兴的。他总算肯为钱着急了——这些年我盼的就是这个。他开始追欠债的人要账，追得比我还紧；从前他能陪一个乞丐坐上一个时辰，还倒贴钱，如今隔着门就打发了。我想：好，这才像个做买卖的。

en: Later I could not laugh. It was not that he loved money; he hated it. The {{e_touzi|पासे}} thrown, thousands staked, no joy in winning, no change in losing, and the next day he doubled the stake just the same. Fewer and fewer dared gamble against him; at last only a few strangers from elsewhere. He lost a country villa once; I redeemed it for him twice—the second price I never dared tell him.
zh: 后来我笑不出来了。他不是爱钱，他是恨钱。{{e_touzi|骰子}}一掷，成千上万地押上去，赢了不喜，输了不改，第二天照样加倍。敢跟他对赌的人越来越少，末了只剩几个外乡客。他输掉过一座乡下别墅，我替他赎回来两次——第二次的价钱，我没敢告诉他。

en: Now the {{e_dachengjiexiang|महा नगर की गलियाँ}} are talking: that gentleman wins and loses ten thousand in a night without a change of face. They take it for skill. I know it is not. A man who treats money as an enemy—money will collect its due sooner or later.
zh: 如今{{e_dachengjiexiang|大城街巷}}里都在传：那位先生一夜之间输赢万金，脸都不变一下。他们当那是本事。我知道不是。一个人把钱当仇人，钱迟早要讨回来。

en: All my life I have been careful, sleepless over a shipment, and he has laughed at me for ten years. But I have done nothing wrong: I take goods by the scale, pay by the contract, keep a whole household, and have never cheated anyone of a coin. He laughs at the wrinkles on my brow—the wrinkles I earned myself; no one bestowed them.
zh: 我这一辈子小心翼翼，为一批货睡不着觉，被他笑了十年。可我并没有做错什么：我按秤收货，按契约付钱，养活一大家子人，从没赖过谁一文。他笑我额上添皱纹——皱纹是我自己挣的，不是谁赏的。

en: Last month I went to his room and found him staring at the mirror on the wall. That face I knew, and did not quite know: hair scented, skin slackened, the little light gone from the eyes. He saw me, smiled, and said: old friend, how is business today. I could not answer a word.
zh: 上个月我去他屋里，撞见他对着墙上的镜子发呆。那张脸我认得，又不太认得：头发熏了香，脸皮松下来，眼睛里那点亮光没有了。他看见我，笑了一下，说：老朋友，今天生意怎么样。我竟一句也答不上来。

en: He had waited so long for that man to fret over money—and now that it had come, he could not be glad.
zh: 他终于等到那个人肯为钱着急，反倒高兴不起来。

en: Hair gone grey, shrewd and full of care; the counting-house lamp often burned past midnight.
zh: 斑白头发，精明多虑，账房的灯常常亮到半夜。

en: He Left No Word
zh: 他没有留下话

en: On the third morning, the steward came in with a string of keys and a ledger. The master of the house, [[NPC1]], was at his meal. He looked up—and could eat no more. The man he wanted, [[NPC2]], had not been seen for three days.
zh: 第三天清早，管家捧着一串钥匙和一本账进来。宅子的主人[[NPC1]]正在用饭，抬头看了一眼，饭就吃不下去了。他要找的那个人[[NPC2]]，已经三天不见踪影。

en: Steward
zh: 管家

en: Sir, there is still no sign of him. I have asked at the city gates, at the harbour, in every street and lane.
zh: 先生，人还是没着落。城门口的、码头上、街巷上，我都问遍了。

en: And the garden?
zh: 园子里呢？

en: Steward
zh: 管家

en: The garden gate is bolted from within; the gardener says no one has gone in for many days. A barber at the {{e_hebianshiji|नदी की पत्थर की सीढ़ियाँ}} says he saw, some days ago, a gentleman in fine clothes sitting there alone, watching the water, sitting a long while. Whether it was him, he cannot say.
zh: 园门从里头闩着，花匠说好些天没人进去。{{e_hebianshiji|河边石级}}上有个剃头的说，前些日子见过一位穿好衣裳的先生独自坐在那儿看水，坐了很久。是不是他，说不准。

en: Out of the city? Alone? How much money did he take?
zh: 往城外去了？一个人？他身上带走了多少钱？

en: Steward
zh: 管家

en: That is the strange part. Not a coin was touched. Here is the ledger—I have checked it three times. Not a discrepancy, not even last month's odd sums. His clothes, his rings, his shoes—all laid out in the room, neat as ever.
zh: 怪就怪在这里。钱一文没动。这是账，我核过三遍——分毫不差，连上个月的零头都结清了。衣裳、戒指、鞋子，全在房里摆得整整齐齐。

en: Settled? He settled the accounts before he left?
zh: 结清了？他把账结清了才走的？

en: Steward
zh: 管家

en: Yes. The last entry is the silk of the fourteenth. Even the wastage is counted in.
zh: 是。最后一笔是十四日的绸缎，连折损都算进去了。

en: …Then he was robbed. He must have been robbed. That road beyond the city has not been safe for years—go, take more men, search toward the woods! If you find nothing, search downstream; look in the river-bends as well!
zh: ……那就是遭了劫。他必是遭了劫。城外那条路多少年没干净过——去，多带几个人，往林子那边找！找不着就往下游找，河湾里也要看！

en: Steward
zh: 管家

en: Sir, permit me a word. If he was robbed, why did the robbers not come into the house for the money?
zh: 先生，容我说一句。若是遭劫，劫道的怎么不顺手进宅子拿钱？

en: The master did not answer. He opened the ledger and shut it, opened it and shut it, three times over, and at last stopped at the last line, where the pen had rested.
zh: 主人没有答话。他把那本账翻开又合上，来回翻了三遍，最后停在最末一行的落笔处。

en: These last days… did he say anything to you?
zh: 他前些日子……跟你说过什么没有？

en: Steward
zh: 管家

en: Nothing. Only once, standing under the eaves of {{e_fushangzhaidi|कामस्वामी का घर}} watching the rain, he said a strange thing.
zh: 没有。只有一回，他站在{{e_fushangzhaidi|富商宅第}}的廊下看雨，说了一句怪话。

en: What did he say?
zh: 什么话？

en: Steward
zh: 管家

en: He said: Water that flows from here will reach the sea, sooner or later. I did not understand; I thought he meant the drain in the courtyard.
zh: 他说：水从这儿流下去，早晚是要归海的。我当时没听懂，只当他在说院里的排水沟。

en: …Search. Keep searching.
zh: ……找。给我接着找。

en: They searched another half a year. The master would not accept the other explanation—that a man would lay down money, clothes, house and trade, and for what? He left that room empty a whole year, and had the bedding aired once a month. In the spring of the second year, he rented it to a stranger who sold flax.
zh: 后来又找了小半年。主人始终不肯认另一种说法——一个人把钱、衣裳、宅子、生意全撂下，凭什么？他把那间屋子空了整整一年，被褥每月晒一次。第二年春天，他才把屋子租给了一个卖亚麻的外乡人。

en: A man left without a word, and not a coin was touched—those left behind were more frightened than if the money had been lost.
zh: 一个人不告而别，钱一文没动——留下的人比丢了钱还慌。

en: The frightened one was the master who turned the ledger three times; the one who left never came back to this city.
zh: 慌的是那位把账翻了三遍的东家；走掉的那个，从此再没回过这座城。

en: My Name Is Vasudeva
zh: 我叫维稣德瓦

en: At dusk the great river was in flood. An old man in rich clothes came on foot, alone, to the ferry. His hair was wholly white; dust covered his fine robes. The ferryman wondered to himself: men dressed like this always went out in carriages or palanquins.
zh: 黄昏，大河涨水。一位衣着华贵的老人独自步行来到渡口。他头发全白了，华服上落满尘土。摇船的老人暗自惊讶：这样打扮的人，出门向来是乘车坐轿的。

en: Old man, will you ferry me to the other shore?
zh: 老丈，能否渡我到彼岸？

en: The ferryman asked him aboard the {{e_duchuan|नाव}}. The long oar dipped, and they left the bank. The guest gazed at the water, then suddenly spoke.
zh: 船夫请他登上{{e_duchuan|渡船}}，长桨一点，便离了岸。客人望着河水出神，忽然开了口。

en: You have chosen a beautiful life. To live by the river every day, to travel on it every day—it must be very beautiful.
zh: 你选择了一种美妙的生活。日日住在河边，天天行在河上，一定非常美妙。

en: It is as you say, sir—very beautiful. And yet, sir, which life, which labour, is not beautiful?
zh: 正如你所说，先生，是很美妙。可是先生，哪一种生活、哪一种活计，不美妙呢？

en: Perhaps. Still, I envy yours.
zh: 或许吧。但我羡慕你的生活。

en: Ah, you would soon tire of it. This is not a life for men in rich clothes.
zh: 哦，你很快就会失去兴味的。这不是衣着华贵的人过的日子。

en: The guest smiled. He said that today, because of these clothes, he had been questioned all along the road; he would give the fine robes to the ferryman as fare—he had not a copper on him.
zh: 客人笑了。他说，今天他已因这身衣服被人盘问了一路；他愿把华服送给船夫抵船费——他身上连一个铜板也没有。

en: You must be joking, sir.
zh: 先生一定是在开玩笑。

en: It is no joke. Many years ago you ferried a young Samana across for nothing—Samanas, those seekers who leave their homes and wander in austerity. Today, ferry him once more.
zh: 不是玩笑。许多年前，你曾免费渡过一个年轻的沙门过河——沙门，就是那些离弃家庭、四处苦行的求道人。今天，请再渡他一次。

en: The oar in the ferryman's hands slowed. He looked at the stranger a long while, carefully. Then a smile rose from the depths of his wrinkles.
zh: 船夫手里的桨慢了下来。他久久地、仔细地打量这位陌生人。忽然，皱纹深处漾开了笑。

en: I know you. More than twenty years ago you spent a night in my {{e_dukoucaoshe|घाट की कुटिया}}. You were a Samana then, and we parted as friends. I am sorry I did not keep your name.
zh: 我认出你了。二十多年前，你在我的{{e_dukoucaoshe|草舍}}里住过一夜。那时你是个沙门，我们友好地分了手。可惜，我没能记住你的名字。

en: I was a Samana then, yes.
zh: 那时，我的确是个沙门。

en: You are welcome. My name is [[NPC1]]. Be my guest today, and sleep again in that hut—and tell me why you have grown so weary of these fine clothes.
zh: 欢迎你。我叫[[NPC1]]。今天请你作我的客人，还睡那间草舍——再讲讲，你为什么这样厌倦这身华服。

en: I am weary of them, and of everything they bought me. I want to stay: give me an old garment; let me be a helper first, then an apprentice. I must learn to row.
zh: 我厌倦了它，也厌倦了它换来的一切。我想留在这儿：给我一件旧衣裳，让我先作帮手，再作学徒。我一定要学会摇船。

en: They reached midstream, where the current ran hard. The ferryman asked no more; he only worked his strong arms, rising and falling, and rowed steadily. Watching him, the guest felt a solid joy he had not known in a long time.
zh: 船到河心，水流湍急。船夫不再多问，只把强壮的臂膀一起一伏，稳稳摇桨。客人望着他，心里生出一种久违的、踏实的欢喜。

en: Ashore, the guest helped him moor the boat. In the hut there was bread, clear water, and mangoes. The sun sank; the two old men sat on a log by the river. The guest told his life: birth, study, wealth, the long fall, down to today's despair, and the waking after despair beside the river. The story lasted deep into the night.
zh: 上了岸，客人帮他把船泊好。草舍里有面包、清水和芒果。日渐西沉，两个老人坐在河边的树干上。客人讲起自己的身世：出身、求学、富贵、沉沦，一直讲到今天的绝望，和绝望之后在河边的醒来。故事一直持续到深夜。

en: The ferryman only listened—did not interrupt, did not press, did not blame, did not praise. When he heard of the tree on the bank and the syllable that saved a life, he even shut his eyes. The guest felt that every word he spoke was received and held.
zh: 船夫只是听——不打断，不追问，不责备，也不称赞。听到那棵岸边的树、那个救命的音节时，他连眼睛都闭上了。客人觉得，自己讲出的每个字，都被稳稳接住了。

en: Stay, my friend. The river has known you a long time; it is kind to you. My wife has been dead many years; I have lived alone too long. Come and share this life with me—you will not want for food or shelter.
zh: 留下吧，我的朋友。河水早已认识你，它待你很友好。我的妻子死了许多年，我一个人住得太久了。来和我一起过日子——吃住都不会缺。

en: I thank you; I accept. And I thank you for this as well: in all my wanderings I have never met a man so willing to listen.
zh: 感谢你，我接受你的邀请。还要谢谢你：这样肯听人说话的人，我走遍四方也没遇见过。

en: That night [[NPC2]] slept deeply in the hut. The river ran past the window, like a song that would not end. The old life was dead; the new one began here.
zh: 那一夜，[[NPC2]]在草舍里睡得很沉。河在窗外流，像一首唱不完的歌。旧的生活已经死了；新的生活，就从这里开始。

en: That old promise—'You will come back and repay me'—was fulfilled today.
zh: 多年前那句「你会回来报答我」，今天应验了。

en: The man who knew best how to listen—he spent his whole life rowing this river.
zh: 最会倾听的人——他一辈子都在这条河边摇船。

en: The Ferryman's Apprentice
zh: 船夫的学徒

en: Life settled at the ferry. Each day before dawn, the {{e_weisudewa|वासुदेव}} woke the new apprentice. The work was learned piece by piece: tending the {{e_duchuan|नाव}}, stopping leaks in the hull, oiling the sides; when the ferry was idle, planting rice in the fields, or gathering wood and bananas in the forest.
zh: 日子在渡口定了下来。每天天没亮，{{e_weisudewa|老船夫}}就把新学徒叫起来。活计一样一样地学：照看那条{{e_duchuan|渡船}}，补船底的缝，给船帮上新油；渡口闲下来，就下田插秧，或者进林捡柴、摘香蕉。

en: Shape the oar along the grain. Steady hands—and a steadier heart.
zh: 桨要顺着木纹削。手稳，心更要稳。

en: The apprentice did as he was told. He learned to make {{e_chuanjiang|चप्पू}}—choosing the straightest wood, planing it, polishing it, fitting the handle to the palm; he learned to weave baskets, pressing the bamboo strips dense and even. Hands that had held only pens and wine-cups soon grew calluses.
zh: 学徒照着做。他学会了做{{e_chuanjiang|船桨}}——选最直的木头，削平，磨光，桨柄要握着合手；他也学会了编篮子，把竹篾压得又密又匀。一双从前只拿过笔杆和酒杯的手，很快磨出了茧。

en: The master's words were always short: one sentence, never a second. Little by little the apprentice learned to read the water: clouds meant rain; eddies meant depth; driftwood told what had happened upstream. The master said none of this needed teaching; the river would speak, if one would listen.
zh: 师父的话从来短促，一句是一句，从不说第二遍。渐渐地，学徒学会了看水：看云，知道雨；看漩涡，知道深浅；看漂下来的浮木，知道上游发生了什么。师父说，这些都不用教，河自己会讲，只要你肯听。

en: Years ran past like the river. Slowly travellers noticed a strange thing: the smiles of the two ferrymen, old and younger, grew more and more alike—the same unfolding from a thousand fine lines, the same innocence, the same peace. Many, boarding, asked: Are you brothers? The two only looked at each other and smiled.
zh: 岁月像河水一样流过去。慢慢地，行客们看出了怪事：这一老一少两个船夫，笑容越来越像——同样从千百条细纹里漾开，同样的天真，同样的安详。许多人上了船就问：你们是亲兄弟吧？两人听了，只是相视一笑。

en: At dusk after work, the two old men sat on the log by the bank. The apprentice had been carrying a question for many days.
zh: 收工的黄昏，两个老人坐在岸边的树干上。徒弟心里揣着一个问题，已经揣了许多天。

en: Master, have you also learned this secret from the river—that time does not exist at all?
zh: 师父，你是否也从河水学到了这个秘密——世上，根本不存在时间？

en: Oh? Tell me.
zh: 哦？你说说看。

en: The river is everywhere at once. At the source, at the waterfall, at the ferry, in the sea—each place is it, and each is only 'now'. It is not a shadow of the past, nor a shadow of the future.
zh: 河水在同一时刻无处不在。它在源头，在瀑布，在渡口，在大海——每一处都是它，都只有「现在」。它不是过去的影子，也不是未来的影子。

en: My life is a river too. The boy I was, the man in his prime, the white-haired man—only three stretches drawn by illusion, not three true persons. What was is not left behind in 'the past'; death does not wait in 'the future'. The mind of the past cannot be grasped, nor the mind of the future; all is now, all is only this moment.
zh: 我的生命也是一条河。少年的我、壮年的我、白发的我，只是幻象划出来的三段，并不是真的三个人。从前种种并没有留在「过去」，死亡也不是等在「将来」。过去心不可得，未来心不可得，一切都是现在，一切只在眼前。

en: You have understood.
zh: 你懂了。

en: And another layer. I used to think men suffered in {{e_lunhui|संसार}}—birth and death turning, circle after circle, with no way out. Now I see it clearly: all sorrow, all fear, live in time. Fear is fear of 'later'; regret is regret of 'before'. If time is seen through, what suffering is left in the world?
zh: 还有一层。我以前以为，人是在{{e_lunhui|轮回}}里受苦——生死流转，一圈又一圈，没有出头之日。可如今我看清了：所有的悲伤、所有的恐惧，其实都住在时间里。怕，是怕「以后」；悔，是悔「从前」。倘若看破了时间，世上还有什么苦可受呢？

en: What you used to fear was tomorrow. And now?
zh: 你从前怕的，是明天。如今呢？

en: Now I only fear failing this moment.
zh: 如今，我只怕辜负了此刻。

en: Good.
zh: 好。

en: Master, why did you never tell me these things of your own accord?
zh: 师父，这些话，你为什么从不主动讲给我？

en: What is spoken is leftover rice; what one tastes for oneself is the meal. So I do not speak. I only sit and listen with you.
zh: 讲出来的，都是剩饭；自己尝到的，才是饭。所以我不讲，我只陪你听。

en: He grew more and more excited as he spoke. The master only smiled, nodded, touched his shoulder, and rose to weave a basket. That touch was warmer than a hundred praises.
zh: 他越说越兴奋。师父只是微笑，点头，抚了抚他的肩膀，又起身去编篮子。那一抚，比一百句夸奖都暖。

en: When night fell, master and apprentice still sat by the river, listening. It was not the sound of water—they felt it was life itself speaking. As [[NPC1]] listened, he felt the wounds of his first half of life being soothed, little by little, by that sound.
zh: 夜幕降临时，师徒俩仍坐在河边听河。那不是水声——他们觉得，那是生命本身在说话。[[NPC1]]听着听着，觉得自己前半生结下的伤，正被这水声一点一点抚平。

en: The new apprentice later asked the question about 'time'.
zh: 新上手的那个徒弟，后来问出了「时间」的问题。

en: He had once been a rich man in the great city.
zh: 他曾是大城里的富人。

en: The Snakebite
zh: 蛇咬

en: The news ran like wildfire: the Awakened One was gravely ill, and would soon leave the world. {{e_sengtuan|गौतम का संघ}}—those in yellow robes who begged with bowls and wandered in practice—hurried from all sides to his sickbed; merchants, women, and old people crowded the roads, as if to a king's coronation, or like bees drawn to a magnet. Everyone wished to see him once more. The {{e_duchuan|नाव}} at the ferry did not rest from dawn to dusk. Some said an age was ending.
zh: 消息像野火一样传开：那位觉者病重，不久就要离世了。{{e_sengtuan|朝圣的僧团}}——那些披黄衣、托钵乞食、云游修行的僧人——从四面八方赶往他的病榻；商贩、妇人、老人也蜂拥上路，像赶赴国王的加冕礼，又像被磁石吸住的蜂群。人人都想见他最后一面。渡口的{{e_duchuan|渡船}}，从早到晚没有停过。有人说，一个时代正在落幕。

en: In the crowd walked a mother and child. She wore plain clothes—she had once heard the Awakened One {{e_qiaodamo|गौतम}} teach in the great city, and had given him her garden; now, hearing he was dying, she had come on foot with the child to see him on his last journey. In her face one could still see that she had been the most beautiful woman in the city; the boy was about eight, in silk, with a handsome face, crying and fussing all the way—wanting rest, wanting food, bursting into anger or into tears.
zh: 人潮里，有一对步行的母子。母亲一身素衣——她从前在大城里听过那位觉者{{e_qiaodamo|乔答摩}}讲法，把自家的园子赠给了他；这次听说他病危，便带着孩子步行赶来，要送他最后一程。她眉眼间仍看得出，年轻时曾是全城最美的女人；孩子八岁上下，穿着丝绸衣裳，生着一张漂亮脸蛋，一路走，一路哭闹——要休息，要吃东西，动不动恼怒无礼，不然就眼泪汪汪。

en: I can't walk any more! I want to go home! What has a dying old man to do with me?
zh: 我走不动了！我要回家！一个快死的老头子，跟我有什么关系？

en: Be good, a little longer. Once we cross this river, we shall be nearly there. Mother begs you.
zh: 乖，再忍一忍。渡过这条河，就快到了。娘求你了。

en: It's your fault! We had a good home, and you had to come this far!
zh: 都怪你！好好的家不住，非要走这么远！

en: The child had been used, from infancy, to matching his will against his mother's. She had to stop and start: feed him, soothe him, then scold him. In the woods she was so weary she curled on the ground and half-closed her eyes; the child sat beside her, eating a banana with relish.
zh: 这孩子从小习惯了和母亲较量意志。她不得不走走停停：喂他，哄他，再申斥他。走进林间，她实在疲倦，蜷在地上半闭着眼歇息；孩子坐在一旁，津津有味地吃香蕉。

en: Suddenly she cried out in pain, her face gone white—a small snake was crawling out from under her.
zh: 突然，她痛楚地叫了一声，脸色煞白——一条小蛇，正从她的身下爬出来。

en: Mother! Mother, what is it?
zh: 娘！娘你怎么了！

en: Don't be afraid… help Mother up. The ferry is just ahead; we will go for help.
zh: 别怕……扶娘起来。前面就是渡口，我们去求救。

en: Mother and child stumbled forward. Thorns tore her skirt; she lost a shoe. Not far from the ferry her body gave way, and she could walk no more. The child kissed her again and again, shouting for help; she too spent her last strength, calling out, call after call.
zh: 母子俩跌跌撞撞地往前跑。她的裙摆被荆棘扯破了，鞋也掉了一只。离渡口不远，她身子一垮，再也走不动了。孩子一边连连亲吻母亲，一边扯着嗓子呼救；她也拼尽最后的气力，一声一声地喊。

en: Help! Is anyone there? Save my mother!
zh: 救命啊！有没有人啊！救救我娘！

en: The cry reached the ferry. The old ferryman came at the sound—strong in the arms, without a word he lifted the fainting woman and strode toward the hut by the river.
zh: 呼声传到渡口。摇船的老人闻声赶来——他臂膀强壮，二话不说，一把抱起昏迷的妇人，快步往河边的草舍走。

en: Don't be afraid. The house is warm. Child, come.
zh: 别怕。屋里暖和。孩子，跟上。

en: Only then did the child see the man who carried her: a vest of coarse cloth, two arms hard as boat-timber. He wanted to cry and held it in, fists clenched, running behind.
zh: 孩子这才看清抱人的老人：粗布坎肩，两条胳膊硬得像船木。他想哭，又死死忍住，攥紧小拳头跟在后面跑。

en: Inside, another old man was bent over, lighting the fire. At the sound of footsteps he raised his head—first a boy's face that seemed half-familiar, then the fainting woman in the old man's arms. The fire leapt. He knew her at a glance; and in that instant he knew who the child was.
zh: 屋里，另一个老人正弯着腰生火。听见脚步声，他抬起头——先看见一张依稀熟识的男孩的脸，随即看见老人怀里那个昏迷的妇人。火光一跳。他一眼认出了她；也就在那一瞬，他明白了那孩子是谁。

en: The garden outside the great city, many years ago, rushed before his eyes. He dared not look again, dared not think. The wood in his hands fell to the floor with a crack.
zh: 许多年前大城外的那座园子，一下子涌到眼前。他不敢再看，也不敢多想。手里的柴，啪的一声掉在地上。

en: Lay her… on my bed. Quickly.
zh: 把她……放到我的床上。快。

en: The fire burned higher, lighting four faces: the fainting mother, the child with a wet, smeared face, the old man who had carried her, and the old man at the fire, still standing, his hands faintly trembling. Outside the window the river ran on, sound after sound, knowing nothing of this, intent only on the sea.
zh: 炉火越烧越旺，映着四张脸：昏迷的母亲，哭花了脸的孩子，抱人的老人，和怔在原地、双手微微发抖的生火老人。窗外的河，还在一声一声地流，对这一切浑然不觉，只顾奔向大海。

en: Of the four, two were old men, and one was a child.
zh: 四个人里，有两个是老人、一个是孩子。

en: The mother had been the most beautiful in the city; the old man at the fire was an old acquaintance of hers.
zh: 母亲曾是全城最美的人；生火的老人与她是旧相识。

en: old
zh: old

en: Death at the Ferry
zh: 渡口死别

en: The wound was washed, yet it had already blackened, and the whole arm was swollen. After the herbs, she slowly opened her eyes. She lay on his bed; he bent over her. She thought she was still dreaming, and smiled, gazing at that face. In the doorway the child she had brought was crying, out of breath.
zh: 伤口洗净了，却已然发黑，整条手臂肿了起来。喂下草药，她慢慢睁开了眼睛。她躺在他的床上；他俯身望着她。她以为自己还在梦里，便微笑着，凝视这张脸。门口，她带来的孩子哭得上气不接下气。

en: You have grown old, my dear; your hair is white. Yet you remind me of that young Samana who once stood outside my garden—barefoot, covered in dust. You now are more like him than you were when you left the city. You have a Samana's eyes again. Ah—just now… did you still know me?
zh: 你老了，亲爱的，你的头发白了。可你让我想起当年站在我园外的那个年轻沙门——赤脚，满身尘土。现在的你，比离开大城时的你，更像他。你又有了沙门的眼睛。呵，你刚才……还认得出我吗？

en: I knew you at a glance.
zh: 我一眼就认出了你。

en: Her gaze turned to the {{e_xiaoxiduo|सिद्धार्थ का पुत्र}} beside the bed, and she signed him to come near.
zh: 她的目光转向床边那个{{e_xiaoxiduo|孩子}}，示意他靠近。

en: Look at him well. He is your son.
zh: 你看清楚他。他是你的儿子。

en: Her gaze grew distant; she closed her eyes. The child began to cry. He lifted the boy onto his knee, stroked his hair, and in a singing tone slowly recited a prayer learned in childhood. Those distant words came back, one by one. The child grew quiet, and sobbed himself to sleep.
zh: 她的目光渐渐迷茫，闭上了眼睛。孩子哭了起来。他把孩子抱上膝头，轻轻抚着他的头发，用歌唱般的调子，缓缓诵起一段童年学过的祷文。那些遥远的词句，一句一句回到他心里。孩子渐渐安静，抽噎着睡去了。

en: By the stove the ferryman was cooking rice, his head down. He looked up at the woman on the bed, then at his friend, and smiled a helpless smile—both knew the herbs could keep her only a little while.
zh: 炉边，摇船的老人正低头做米饭。他抬眼看看床上的妇人，又看看朋友，无奈地笑了笑——谁都明白，草药只能留住她一会儿。

en: She is dying.
zh: 她快要死了。

en: The ferryman nodded; the fire lit his kind face. The smell of rice mixed with the smell of medicine and spread through the hut.
zh: 摇船的老人点点头，炉火映着他慈祥的面容。米香混着药味，在小屋里散开。

en: When she woke again, her face was full of pain. He watched her quietly, intently, waiting, sharing her pain. She felt it, and her eyes found his.
zh: 她再度醒来时，脸上满是煎熬。他静静地、专注地看着她，等着，分担着她的痛。她感觉到了，眼睛找到了他的目光。

en: Your gaze is wholly different from before… tell me, have you found it—found peace in the heart?
zh: 你的目光，和从前完全不一样了……告诉我，你是不是已经找到了——找到了心里的安宁？

en: He smiled and gently stroked her hand.
zh: 他微笑着，轻轻抚摸她的手。

en: You have found it. I can see it. …I shall have peace too.
zh: 你找到了。我看得出。……我也会得到安宁的。

en: You have it already.
zh: 你已经得到了。

en: She had meant to go and see the dying {{e_qiaodamo|गौतम}}—that awakened saint—to look once upon his peace; yet in the end she had found only her old lover. She felt that this too was good, as good as seeing the other. She wanted to tell him so, but her lips would no longer obey; she only looked at him in silence.
zh: 她本想赶去朝觐病重的{{e_qiaodamo|世尊}}——那位觉悟的圣人，想瞻仰一眼他的安详；可她最终只找到了旧时的情人。她觉得，这也很好，和见到另一位，一样的好。她想把这话告诉他，嘴唇却已不听使唤，只是默默地望着他。

en: He watched life recede slowly from her eyes. When the last tremor passed over her body, he reached out and gently closed them.
zh: 他看见生命从她的眼睛里缓缓退去。最后的悸动掠过她的身体时，他伸出手指，轻轻合上了她的眼睛。

en: He gathered the white hair scattered on the pillow, and tucked in the quilt, as if she might take cold.
zh: 他替她拢了拢散在枕上的白发，又把被角掖好，像怕她着凉。

en: He sat a long time, looking at her old, weary face, at the shrunken lips. He remembered how, many years ago, he had compared her mouth to a newly picked fig. In the same instant he seemed to see two young faces—red mouths, eager eyes—as if all of them were alive in this moment.
zh: 他久久坐着，看她衰老而倦怠的脸，看那皱缩的双唇。他想起许多年前，自己曾把她的嘴唇比作一枚新摘的无花果。同一刻，他恍惚又看见两张年轻的脸——红润的嘴唇，热切的目光——仿佛全都活在此刻。

en: That night he did not eat. He sat alone outside the door and listened to the river all night. The river did not counsel him; it only flowed, as if to say: some come, some go.
zh: 夜里，他没有吃饭，独自坐在门外，听了一整夜的河。河水什么也不劝，它只是流，像在说：有人来，有人走。

en: Before sunrise the two old men built a pyre on the {{e_huozangqiu|श्मशान टीला}}—the ferryman's dead wife had been burned here many years before. The child still slept, his brow still furrowed. When the fire rose, he looked at the river and took the old man's hand.
zh: 清晨，太阳还没升起，两个老人在{{e_huozangqiu|临水的土丘}}上筑起柴堆——摇船老人的亡妻，许多年前也在这里火化。孩子仍在熟睡，眉头还皱着。火光升起来的时候，他望着河，握住了身旁老人的手。

en: She had meant to see the Buddha a last time, and met her old lover first.
zh: 她本想去看佛陀最后一眼，却先见到了旧情人。

en: Her lips had once been like a fresh fig.
zh: 她的嘴唇曾像新鲜的无花果。

en: old
zh: old

en: old
zh: old

en: Broken Bowls
zh: 碎碗

en: On the day of the funeral the child cried as if his heart would tear. After that he did not cry. For days he sat pale on the burial mound, staring into the distance, his heart locked, struggling before his fate. The man who called himself his father respected the grief and did not press him, left him be. He honoured the child's sorrow: the boy did not yet know him, and could not love him as a father.
zh: 葬礼那天，孩子哭得撕心裂肺。之后，他就不哭了。一连几天，他脸色苍白地坐在埋人的土丘上，望着远处，紧锁着心门，在自己的命运面前挣扎。那个自称是他父亲的人，体谅他的悲伤，不去逼他，随他自便。他尊重孩子的悲伤：这孩子还不认识他，自然不能像对父亲一样爱他。

en: The father knew well: this eight-year-old had been spoiled from infancy by {{e_jiamola|कमला}}. In the city house he had been used to fine food, soft beds, servants at a lifted hand. How could such a one settle at once in a poor hut? So the father did not hurry, did not scold; he only did many things for the child in silence: made the bed, mended clothes, kept the best portion of every meal for him.
zh: 父亲心里清楚：这个八岁的孩子，是被{{e_jiamola|他的母亲}}从小惯大的。在大城的宅子里，他吃惯了美食，睡惯了软床，一抬手就有仆人跑来。这样的人，怎么可能一下子在穷苦的草屋里安下心来？所以父亲不催，不骂，只是默默替孩子做了许多事：铺床，补衣，顿顿把最好的那份留给他。

en: But the child's heart did not soften at all. Coarse rice was set down; he tasted it and pushed it away, saying it was not food for a human being; asked to help with a little work, he turned his head aside; the fruit trees the other old man grew behind the hut he stripped bare, green and red fruit flung on the ground. He hated the water for being bitter, the bed for being hard, the night for its mosquitoes, and had 'home' on his lips all day. One evening, over a trifle, he seized the two rice-bowls on the table and smashed them on the floor.
zh: 可孩子的心，一点也没有软下来。粗米饭端上来，他尝一口就推开，说这不是人吃的东西；叫他帮忙做点活，他把头扭到一边；同住的那位老人种在屋后的果树，被他洗劫一空，青的红的扔了一地。他嫌水苦，嫌床硬，嫌夜里蚊子多，整天把「回家」挂在嘴上。一天傍晚，就为了一点小事，他抓起桌上的两只米饭碗，狠狠摔在地上。

en: I won't eat this! This is not food for people! I want to go home—back to my own house in the city! Even the water there is sweet!
zh: 我不吃这个！这根本不是人吃的东西！我要回家——回我自己在大城的家！那里连水都是甜的！

en: Very well. If you don't care for it, leave it. I have left you a mango, on the window-ledge.
zh: 好。不爱吃，就放着吧。我给你留了芒果，在窗台上。
