en: Who wants your mango! Stop pretending—I hate that good man's face of yours most of all!
zh: 谁稀罕你的芒果！你少假惺惺的——我最讨厌你这张好人的脸！

en: The bowls were broken. The father crouched, picked up the shards one by one, swept them clean, and as usual warmed the rice again, saying nothing. His heart was not without bitterness: for months he had waited for his son to understand him, to take his love, even a little in return. He came to see that this child brought him not joy but trouble. Yet he would rather have the trouble than the ease of having no child.
zh: 碗碎了。父亲蹲下身，一片一片，把碎片捡干净，扫净了，又像往常一样把饭热上，什么也没说。他心里不是不苦：几个月了，他等着儿子理解他，接受他的爱，哪怕回报一点点都好。可他渐渐明白，这个孩子带给他的不是快乐，是烦恼。只是他宁愿要这烦恼，也不要没有孩子的快活。

en: The child, for his part, hoped more that he would lose his temper. A scolding, a blow even? But this father answered every rudeness with a smile, every wilfulness with kindness—and in the child's eyes that was the most hateful cunning, the trick of an old fox.
zh: 孩子倒更盼着他发火。哪怕骂一句、打一下呢？可这位父亲对每一次无礼都报以微笑，对每一次任性都报以慈爱——在孩子眼里，这简直是最可恨的狡诈，是老狐狸的手段。

en: From then on the two old men divided the work: the {{e_weisudewa|वासुदेव}} took all the ferry's labour on himself, and the father kept the hut and the child. The child grew bolder. He had long noticed: the coppers and silver the passengers paid were kept in a bark {{e_shuangselan|द्विवर्णी टोकरी}} hung at the bow, and no one watched anyone. The child's gaze rested on that basket a long time; he said nothing.
zh: 从那以后，两个老人分了工：{{e_weisudewa|老船夫}}一个人担起渡口全部的活，父亲守着草舍和孩子。孩子却越发胆大。他早就留意到：渡客付的铜板和银币，都收在一只树皮编的{{e_shuangselan|双色小篮}}里，挂在船头，谁也没防着谁。孩子的目光在那只篮子上停了很久，什么也没说。

en: That night the old ferryman drew his friend outside. The smile was gone from his wrinkles.
zh: 这天夜里，老船夫把朋友拉到门外。他皱纹里的笑没有了。

en: Friend. Tonight we must talk.
zh: 朋友。今晚，我们必须谈一谈。

en: The father looked at the old man's face in the moonlight, and his heart sank. He half knew what would be said—the words he most feared to hear, and could least escape. The river ran at their feet, sound after sound, as if urging him to answer.
zh: 父亲望着老人被月光照亮的脸，心里咯噔一下。他隐约知道要谈什么——那是他最不敢听、也最躲不掉的话。河水在脚边流，一声，又一声，像在催他回答。

en: An eight-year-old spoiled by his mother.
zh: 被母亲惯坏的八岁孩子。

en: The child's father, when young, had once kept his own father sleepless a whole night.
zh: 孩子的父亲，年轻时也曾让他的父亲一夜难眠。

en: old
zh: old

en: Broken Oars
zh: 断桨

en: The evening before, the powder that had gathered for months in the hut at last went off. The father told the child to gather sticks in the woods for the evening fire. The boy stood still, stamped both feet, fists clenched, and roared out all his contempt in his father's face.
zh: 前一天傍晚，草屋里积压了几个月的火药，终于炸了。父亲叫孩子去林里拣些树枝，好烧晚上的饭。孩子站在原地不动，两脚跺地，双拳紧握，当着父亲的面，把一肚子的轻蔑全吼了出来。

en: Gather your own sticks! I am not your servant! I know you dare not beat me—you only punish me with your piety and your patience! You want me to be like you? Never! I hate you—I would rather be a thief, rather go to hell, than be like you!
zh: 去拣你自己的树枝！我不是你的奴仆！我知道你不敢打我——你只会拿你的虔诚和宽容来罚我！你想让我跟你一样？休想！我就是恨你——我宁愿当贼，宁愿下地狱，也不要像你！

en: The father stood as if struck on the head. He opened his mouth; nothing came.
zh: 父亲站在原地，像被当头打了一棍。他张了张嘴，什么也没说出来。

en: The child rushed out, and did not come back till late at night; he fell asleep without a word. The father sat in the dark half the night, those hard words still buzzing in his ears, like a blow in the face. Next morning the bed was empty. The boy was gone.
zh: 孩子夺门而出，到深夜才回来，倒头便睡，一句话也不说。父亲在黑暗里坐了半宿，那番狠话还在耳朵里嗡嗡作响，像被人迎面打了一棍。第二天清晨，床空了。人，不见了。

en: The {{e_shuangselan|द्विवर्णी टोकरी}} hung at the bow was gone too—bark-woven, holding the passengers' coppers and silver. The {{e_duchuan|नाव}} at the bank was gone as well. The quilt on the bed was folded neatly. The father ran to the river in one breath, and far off saw the empty boat moored on the far shore. He understood it all.
zh: 挂在船头的那只{{e_shuangselan|双色小篮}}也不见了——树皮编的，里面存着渡客付的铜板和银币。岸边的{{e_duchuan|渡船}}同样没了踪影。床上的被子叠得整整齐齐。父亲一口气跑到河边，远远看见空船泊在对岸。他全明白了。

en: I must follow him! A child cannot cross this forest alone; he will come to harm. We will bind a raft and cross at once!
zh: 我必须跟着他！一个孩子，独自穿不过这片林子，他会出事的。我们扎一条筏子，马上过河！

en: A raft we must bind—the boat has to be brought back. But friend, let him go. He is no longer a child; he knows how to look after himself. He is finding the road back to the city. He is right; do not forget that: he is walking his own road. The river will watch over him.
zh: 筏子是要扎的——船总得弄回来。可是朋友，你随他去吧。他已不再是孩子了，他知道怎么照顾自己。他在找回城的路。他是对的，别忘了这一点：他在走他自己的路。河水会看着他。

en: His own road? He is only eight! He will lose his way, go hungry, meet bad men—how can you ask me to let go?
zh: 自己的路？他才八岁！他会迷路，会挨饿，会遇上坏人——你叫我怎么放手？

en: And if you catch him, what then? Bind him and bring him back in the boat?
zh: 你追上了，又能怎样？把他捆在船上带回来？

en: At least he would be alive! At least he would not be among wolves!
zh: 至少他活着！至少他不在狼群里！

en: I can see you are suffering. Yet this suffering would make another man laugh. Before long you will laugh at it yourself.
zh: 我看得出你在受苦。可这份苦，换了旁人是要笑出声的。要不了多久，你自己也会笑它。

en: The father answered no more. He swung an axe at the bamboo; sweat ran down his temples; blisters rose on his palms and he did not stop. The old man helped him bind the poles tight with grass-rope. The raft went in, and the current drove it far downstream; they poled hard against the stream, and at last reached the other shore.
zh: 父亲不再答话。他抡起斧头砍竹，汗顺着鬓角往下淌，手掌磨出了血泡也不停。老人帮他用草绳把竹竿一道道扎紧。竹筏下了水，被激流冲向下游老远；两人奋力撑篙，逆流而上，总算到了对岸。

en: Why do you… carry an axe with you?
zh: 你为什么……随身带着斧子？

en: Perhaps our {{e_chuanjiang|चप्पू}} are already gone.
zh: 也许，我们的{{e_chuanjiang|船桨}}已经不在了。

en: So it was. The empty boat's bottom was clean; not an oar remained. Before he fled, the child had broken every oar and thrown them in the river—so the men could not row after him. A hard mind, and a thorough one. The old man pointed at the empty bottom and smiled, saying nothing—the smile said plainly: Do you still not see? Your son does not wish to be pursued. He crouched and began, in silence, to shape a new oar. The father looked into the depths of the woods, clenched his fists, and walked quickly in.
zh: 果然。空船的舱底干干净净，一根桨也没剩下。那孩子逃走之前，把船桨统统折断扔进了河里——他叫大人没法撑船追他。好狠的心思，也好周密的心思。老人指着空荡荡的船底笑了笑，什么也没说——那笑容分明在讲：你还不明白吗？你的儿子不愿被人追着。他蹲下身，默默削起一支新桨。父亲望着林子深处，攥紧拳头，快步走了进去。

en: There were small footprints in the woods, leading toward the great city. The old man looked at the prints, then at his friend's ashen face, and swallowed the words at his lips. The sun stood overhead, white and glaring; the two walked one behind the other, and neither spoke again.
zh: 林子里果然有小脚印，一路朝着大城的方向。老人望着脚印，又看看朋友铁青的脸，把到嘴边的话咽了回去。日头升到头顶，白花花的，两个人一前一后，谁也没有再说话。

en: Who stole the fares and broke the oars?
zh: 谁偷走了船费、折断了船桨？

en: The man who told the father to let go had no children of his own.
zh: 劝父亲放手的那个人，自己无儿无女。

en: old
zh: old

en: Ten Thousand Sounds Become Om
zh: 万音成唵

en: After the son left, the wound still ached. Seeing other travellers cross with their children, he felt, to his own surprise, a jealousy: even bad men have children with them—why not I? One day he could not bear it; he poled the {{e_duchuan|नाव}} to the other shore, meaning to search the city once more.
zh: 儿子走后，那道伤口一直隐隐作痛。看见别的行客带着儿女渡河，他心里竟然泛起嫉妒：连坏人都有孩子陪伴，为什么偏偏我没有？一天，他实在忍不住，撑{{e_duchuan|渡船}}到了对岸，想再去城里寻一次。

en: In the dry season the river was clear and shallow, yet strangely loud. The river was laughing—plainly, mocking this old man. He stopped, bent to look at the reflection, and suddenly knew the face: it was like his own father's. In those days he too had forced his father to let him leave home, and never returned. What his father had swallowed alone was what he now swallowed. This meaningless repetition was a circle drawn by fate.
zh: 旱季的河水又清又浅，声音却奇怪地响亮。河水在笑——明明白白地，嘲笑这个老人。他站住，俯身去看水里的倒影，忽然认出：那张脸，竟像他自己的父亲。当年，他也是这样逼着父亲放他离家，一去不返。父亲当年独自咽下的，正是他现在咽的。这无意义的重复，像命运画的一个圆。

en: He poled back, his heart bitter and confused; more than once he wanted to laugh aloud at himself. Yet he had one last road: to confess to the old man, to tell everything.
zh: 他撑船回来，心里又苦又乱，几次想放声嘲笑自己。可他还有最后一条路：向那位老人忏悔，把一切都讲出来。

en: In the hut the old man was weaving a basket. His eyes were dim, his hands slow, yet the peace on his face was as it had always been. He sat down beside him and slowly poured out all he had never told anyone: the search in the city, the river's mockery, the thoughts he was ashamed even to admit.
zh: 草舍里，老人在编篮子。他的眼睛花了，手也慢了，脸上的安详却一如既往。他在老人身旁坐下，缓缓地，把从未对人讲过的一切都和盘托出：进城的追寻，河水的嘲笑，那些连自己都羞于承认的念头。

en: The old man listened in silence. As he spoke he suddenly felt something was wrong: his trouble flowed into the old man's heart and came back cool and clear. Was this still a man? This motionless listener was plainly a great tree catching the rain, was plainly the river itself.
zh: 老人静静地听。讲着讲着，他忽然觉得不对：自己的烦恼流进老人心里，又清清凉凉地流回来。这哪里还是一个人？这端坐不动的倾听者，分明是一棵承接雨水的大树，分明就是这条河本身。

en: He had finished. The old man looked at him, worn, said nothing, took his hand, and led him to sit by the river.
zh: 讲完了。老人衰弱地望着他，没有说话，拉起他的手，领他到河边坐下。

en: You have heard its mockery. But you have not yet heard everything. Come, let us listen again.
zh: 你已经听见了它的嘲笑。可你还没有听见一切。来，让我们再听。

en: The two old men sat in silence, listening to the river sing.
zh: 两个老人默默坐着，听河水唱歌。

en: Do you hear?
zh: 你可听见？

en: He nodded.
zh: 他点点头。

en: Listen further!
zh: 再听！

en: He listened more deeply. Many images rose on the water: his father, alone in grief for a lost son; himself, alone in longing for the child who had fled; his son, alone on a road of burning desire. The three generations flowed into one river. Each clung to his goal, each was bound by his goal, each suffered. The water was full of thirst, sting, and pursuit. The river ran toward its goal; one goal reached, another rose, never ceasing.
zh: 他听得更深。水面浮起许多形象：他的父亲，孤独地为失去的儿子哀痛；他自己，孤独地思念着逃走的孩子；他的儿子，孤独地走在燃烧的欲望路上。三代人的形象汇进同一条河。每个人都执着于自己的目标，每个人都被自己的目标所困，每个人都在经受痛苦。水声里满是渴慕、刺痛和追逐。河水奔向自己的目标，一个目标达成，又有新的目标，永不停歇。

en: He no longer told which sound was weeping, which was laughter. Joy and sorrow, good and evil, a mother's song and a dying groan—ten thousand voices wound together into one great song. And when his heart no longer seized any one of them, only a single syllable remained in that song—{{e_om|ॐ}}. The syllable a Brahmin's child could chant from the first memory, meaning: perfection. Ten thousand sounds become one; the one is all.
zh: 他不再分辨哪一个声音是哭，哪一个是笑。喜与悲、善与恶、母亲的歌与临死者的呻吟，千万种声音缠绕在一起，合成一首大歌。而当他的心不再抓住其中任何一个，那首大歌里，只剩下一个字——{{e_om|唵}}。婆罗门的孩子记事起就会念的那个音节，意思是：圆满。万音归一，一就是一切。

en: The old man turned and smiled. The smile unfolded from every wrinkle, radiant. In the same moment the same smile rose on his own face. His wound began to close; the pain sank like a stone to the river-bed. From that moment he no longer fought his fate.
zh: 老人转过头来，笑了。那笑容从他脸上所有的皱纹里漾开，光辉夺目。同一时刻，同样的笑容，也浮现在他的脸上。他的伤口开始愈合，痛苦像一颗石子，沉进了河底。从这一刻起，他不再和自己的命运抗争了。

en: The one word into which ten thousand river-sounds flowed.
zh: 万千河声汇成的一个字。

en: The word a Brahmin's child could chant from childhood.
zh: 婆罗门的孩子从小会念的那个字。

en: old
zh: old

en: The Last Bow
zh: 最后一拜

en: At dawn the old monk was to go on. At the hut door, after much hesitation, he asked a last question. He was one of the strictest in {{e_sengtuan|गौतम का संघ}}—those who wore yellow robes, begged with bowls, wandered the four directions, and spent their lives preaching the teaching.
zh: 清晨，老僧要上路了。临别前，他站在草舍门口，犹豫再三，问出了最后一个问题。他是{{e_sengtuan|佛陀的僧团}}里守戒最严的僧人之一——那一群人披黄衣、托钵乞食、云游四方，一生宣讲佛法。

en: Friend, before I go on, tell me: have you some creed, some learning, that upholds your life?
zh: 朋友，在继续我的行程之前，请告诉我：你是否有某种信条、某种学问，在扶助你的生活？

en: You know well that from youth I have doubted every creed. Yet there is one thing I have found, and I can tell you: wisdom cannot be spoken. Knowledge can be taught; wisdom cannot. The wisdom a wise man tries to tell another always sounds foolish.
zh: 你很清楚，我年轻时就开始怀疑一切信条。不过有一种体会，我可以讲给你：智慧无法言传。知识可以传授，智慧不能。一个智者想要讲给别人听的智慧，听起来总是愚蠢的。

en: You are speaking strangely again… what does that mean?
zh: 你又在说怪话了……这是什么意思？

en: The opposite of every truth is also true. Words can say only half—like parting the river with a hand; in a moment it is one river again. I think only one thing truly matters: to love this world. Not to despise it, not to hate it, nor to hate ourselves; to look upon it and all life with love, with wonder, with reverence.
zh: 每一个真理的反面，也同样真实。话语只能讲出一半——像用手把河水划开，转眼它又合成一条。我以为真正重要的只有一件事：去爱这个世界。不鄙弃它，不憎恨它，也不憎恨我们自己；以爱、以赞叹、以敬意，看待它和一切生命。

en: The old monk was silent. The words were strange and hard. Yet this man's every gesture, his eyes, his brow, his smile, held a purity and a peace—a radiance he had seen in only one other: the Blessed One who had already entered Nirvana. Nirvana is the stillness beyond birth and death.
zh: 老僧默然。这些话又怪又难。可是，眼前这人的一举手一投足，他的眼睛、前额、微笑，都透着一种纯净与安详——这种神采，他只在一个人身上见过：那位已经涅槃的世尊。涅槃，就是超越生死的寂静。

en: A comparison even crossed his mind: the Blessed One's teaching was clear, definite, never so odd as this; yet this man's gaze and hands gave off a holiness he had not seen since the Blessed One's passing. The old monk's heart was in turmoil; already leaving, he turned back and bowed with deep feeling.
zh: 他心里甚至掠过一丝较量：世尊的教义清晰、明确，从不像这样怪诞；可这人的目光与手势，却散发着自世尊入灭以来他再未见过的圣洁。老僧心里翻江倒海，临走了，又回过身，深情地躬下身。

en: We are both old; we may not meet again in this life. I can see you have found peace; I have not. Tell me a little more—something I can carry in my breast upon the road. My road is often hard and dark.
zh: 我们都老了，今生恐怕再难相见。我看得出，你已经得到了安宁；而我，还没有。再给我讲一点吧——讲一点我能揣在怀里上路的东西。我的路，常常又难又黑。

en: He looked at the old monk in silence, with a calm, peaceful smile. Then he spoke softly.
zh: 他带着平静、安详的微笑，默默注视着老僧。然后，他轻声开了口。

en: Bend closer. Nearer still. Kiss my forehead.
zh: 俯身过来。再近一点。吻我的前额。

en: The old monk was greatly astonished, yet a strong love and obedience pushed him; he bent and touched the forehead lightly with his lips. In that instant a miracle occurred.
zh: 老僧惊愕万分，却被一股强大的爱与服从推着，俯下身去，用嘴唇轻轻碰了碰他的前额。就在这一瞬，奇迹发生了。

en: He no longer saw his friend's face. He saw a thousand forms arising and passing: a dying fish with its mouth wide, a newborn infant red in the face; a murderer raising a knife, a sinner on his knees; men and women in an embrace, the stiff dead; wild boar, crocodile, bull, birds… ten thousand forms turning, loving one another and destroying one another, endlessly changing, endlessly reborn. He seemed to hear again the great song by the river, ten thousand voices singing only one word: {{e_om|ॐ}}.
zh: 他看见的不再是朋友的脸。他看见千百种形象生生灭灭：垂死的鱼大张着嘴，新生的婴儿满脸通红；凶手举刀，罪人跪地；相拥的男女，僵冷的死者；野猪、鳄鱼、公牛、飞鸟……万相流转，彼此爱恋又彼此毁灭，不断变幻，不断重生。他仿佛又听见河边的那首大歌，万千声音只唱一个字：{{e_om|唵}}。

en: And over it all lay a thin, transparent smile—peaceful, subtle, hovering above ten thousand births and deaths. The old monk knew it: it was the smile of the Blessed One, which he had revered and gazed upon all his life.
zh: 而这一切之上，笼着一层薄薄的、透明的微笑——安详、微妙，盘旋在万千生死之上。老僧认出来了：那正是他毕生敬畏瞻仰的、世尊的微笑。

en: The old monk wept without restraint. Before the man who sat unmoving he bowed, deeply, deeply, to the ground. That peaceful smile called up all he had loved in his life, all that had been precious and holy.
zh: 老僧泪流满面，无法抑制。他在那端坐不动的人面前，深深地、深深地一躬到地。那安详的微笑，令他想起自己一生中所深爱的一切，想起生命中所有珍贵与神圣的一切。

en: Only the third time did he truly 'see' his friend.
zh: 他第三次才真正「看见」自己的朋友。

en: That smile he had seen on only one other face.
zh: 那个微笑，他只在一个人脸上见过。

en: old
zh: old

en: old
zh: old

en: Newborn Infant
zh: 新生婴儿

en: I woke. I lay under {{e_yezishu|ताड़ का तट}}, the river running before my eyes, sunlight broken on the water. A river-wind made me shiver, yet I wanted to laugh. I do not remember how long I slept—as if a lifetime, and as if only an instant.
zh: 我醒过来了。躺在{{e_yezishu|岸边那棵大树}}下，河水在眼前流，阳光碎在水面上。河风一吹，我打了个寒噤，却忍不住想笑。我不记得自己睡了多久——像睡了一辈子，又像只睡了一瞬。

en: Yesterday I had meant to feed myself to this river. The rich man's sickness had eaten me hollow: fine clothes, dice, wine-feasts; twenty years I had turned in {{e_lunhui|संसार}}—the cycle men call the turning of life between birth and death—and the longer I turned, the more numb the heart. I was sick of myself; even a glance at my reflection made me retch.
zh: 昨天的我，想把自己喂给这条河。富人的病把我蛀空了：华服、骰子、酒宴，二十年，我在{{e_lunhui|轮回}}里一圈一圈地转——人们管生命在生死之间的这种循环叫轮回，转得越久，心越麻木。我受够了自己，连看水里的倒影一眼都恶心。

en: Yet in the instant I let go, a syllable that had slept many years woke in the heart—{{e_om|ॐ}}. The first word a Brahmin's child can chant from memory, meaning 'perfection'. It sounded so lightly, as if someone under the water had called my name. I saw all at once how foolish I had been, sank down under the tree, and slept a deep sleep. That sleep had no dreams.
zh: 可就在松手的那一瞬，心里有个沉睡了许多年的音节醒了——{{e_om|唵}}。婆罗门的孩子记事起就会念的第一个字，意思是「圆满」。它就那么轻轻一响，像有人在水底唤我的名字。我忽然看清自己有多蠢，跌坐在树下，沉沉睡去。那一觉，没有梦。

en: Now I have nothing: no property, no fine clothes, no place that will wait for me. Yet my heart is light as a newborn infant's; all things look new. So a man must taste his own foolishness and sin with his own hands, let them rot, let them die, before he can become a child again. The songbird in my breast was not dead—it had only been mute many years.
zh: 现在我一无所有：没有家产，没有华服，没有一个肯等我的地方。可我心里轻快得像新生的婴儿，看什么都新鲜。原来人非得把那些愚蠢和罪孽都亲手尝过一遍，烂掉，死掉，才能重新变成孩子。原来我胸口那只歌鸟并没有死——它只是哑了许多年。

en: The river is singing. I will stay, stay beside it, and ask it to teach me. My old life has died on the other shore; the new life begins with this river.
zh: 河水在唱歌。我要留下来，留在它身旁，向它求教。我的旧生活已经死在对岸了；新的生活，就从这条河开始。

en: The man who had just died once by the river and come back to life.
zh: 刚在河边死过一回又活过来的人。

en: The one this story is about.
zh: 这个故事的主角。

en: Year upon Year
zh: 年复一年

en: Days on the river were like days, years like years. I rowed the {{e_duchuan|नाव}}, planted rice, wove baskets, and at dark ate with the old man. To others this white-haired ferryman had perhaps never lived any other way.
zh: 河上的日子一天像一天，一年像一年。我摇{{e_duchuan|渡船}}，插秧，编篮子，天黑了同老人一起吃饭。旁人看我，大约觉得这个白头发的船夫从来就没有过别的活法。

en: So it seemed. Yet in my heart a ledger still ran, year after year. I had counted: in the city I wasted twenty years. That number twenty I still cannot wipe away—when I wake at night, the first thing I do is take it out and reckon it again.
zh: 话是这么说。可我心里有一本账，还在一年一年往下记。我数过：在城里，我糟蹋掉了二十年。二十这个数，我至今抹不平——夜里醒来，第一件事仍旧是把它拿出来算一遍。

en: Some passengers make me uneasy. A merchant in good clothes steps aboard, and I remember how I once stepped onto another man's boat just so; a young couple with a child, and I have to turn my face to the water. The old man never asks; he only shifts the pole a little toward me.
zh: 有些客人上船，我会不自在。穿好衣裳的商人跨上来，我就想起自己当年也是这样跨上别人的船的；一对年轻夫妻抱着孩子过河，我要偏过头去看水。老人从不问，只是把篙子往我这边挪一挪。

en: The sharpest are another kind: a white-haired old man helped aboard by his son. I set a stool for them, take the fare, pole to the other shore, watch them walk slowly away. Only when they are far do I dare think of it—the year I left home I walked so sure of myself, and never went back once. In which year my father ceased to be, I have never even asked a soul.
zh: 最扎人的是另一种客人：白发的老人被儿子扶着上船。我替他们摆好板凳，收钱，撑到对岸，看他们慢慢走远。走远了我才敢想那件事——我离家那年走得那样理直气壮，此后再没有回去过一趟。父亲是哪一年不在的，我连问都没有问过一个人。

en: {{e_lunhui|संसार}}—I used to speak of it fluently: men trapped, turning between birth and death, circle after circle. I do not speak of it now. I lack no doctrine; I lack the hand that will close this ledger. I know only that some accounts the river cannot wipe out for me in a day. It runs past my feet each day, making no sound, as if to say: slowly.
zh: {{e_lunhui|轮回}}这个词，从前我讲得头头是道：人困在生死里打转，一圈又一圈。如今我不讲了。道理我一句不缺，缺的是把这本账合上的那只手。我只知道有些账，河水一时半刻替我抹不平。它每天从我脚下流过去，一声不响，像在说：慢慢来。

en: He no longer speaks doctrine aloud, yet the ledger in his heart still runs, year after year.
zh: 他嘴上不再讲道理，心里那本账还一年一年记着。

en: That white-haired apprentice by the river never went home again after he left.
zh: 河边那个白发的学徒，离家之后再没有回去过。

en: He Has Her Eyes
zh: 他有一双她的眼睛

en: Firelight falls on {{e_dukoucaoshe|घाट की कुटिया}}, and on the mother and child on the bed. The child has cried himself to sleep on my knee; his mother lies there, the poison still in her wound.
zh: 火光照着{{e_dukoucaoshe|这间河边的草舍}}，也照着床上的母子俩。孩子哭累了，在我膝头睡着了；他的母亲躺在那里，毒还留在她的伤里。

en: I look at that small face again and again. Eight years old, silk clothes, a spoiled look—yet the way he knits his brow is plainly {{e_jiamola|कमला}} when she was young. He has her eyes.
zh: 我一遍遍看那张小脸。八岁了，丝绸衣裳，被宠坏的眼神——可他皱起眉的样子，分明是{{e_jiamola|他的母亲}}年轻时的样子。他有一双她的眼睛。

en: When I left the great city I did not know she already carried my child. {{e_xiaoxiduo|सिद्धार्थ का पुत्र}} has grown till now in wealth: fine food, soft beds, servants at his call; and I, his father, was yesterday still rowing for a copper's fare.
zh: 当年我离开大城的时候，不知道她已经怀了我的孩子。{{e_xiaoxiduo|这孩子}}在富贵里长到今天：吃美食，睡软床，使唤仆人；而我，他的父亲，昨天还在为一个铜板的船费摇船。

en: I had thought myself different: the world was children, I was the one awake; I could not love, and need not. Now a son lies on my lap. So I too cannot escape—I too will worry, will fear, will want to press the world's best things on a child who loses his temper at me.
zh: 我曾以为自己与众不同：世人是孩童，我是醒着的人；我不会爱，也不必爱。现在，一个儿子躺在我腿上。原来我也逃不过——我也会牵挂，会害怕，会想把全世界最好的都塞给一个冲我发脾气的小孩。

en: Will she rest in peace? She will. Before she went she saw the peace in my eyes, and said she would have it too. Very well; the rest of the road is mine: to raise this motherless child, day by day, year by year.
zh: 她会安息吗？会的。她临走前看到了我眼里的安宁，她说她也会得到。那好，剩下的路我来走：把这个没了娘的孩子养大，一天一天，一年一年。

en: I owe her. When I was young I took her love as a lesson, learned it, and left, without looking back. Now she has given me a son—what have I to repay? Only to raise him, raise him upright, as she would have wished.
zh: 我欠她的。年轻时，我把她的情爱当作课业，学完就走，连头也没有回。如今她还给我一个儿子——我拿什么还？只有把他养大，养得堂堂正正，像她希望的那样。

en: He will not acknowledge me; he hates this poor hut; it does not matter. I have patience enough—I will warm his heart, day by day, with kindness.
zh: 他不认我，他恨这间破草舍，没关系。我有的是耐心——我要用善意，一天一天，把他的心焐热。

en: The man who has just learned he has a son.
zh: 刚知道自己有个儿子的人。

en: The child's father.
zh: 孩子的父亲。

en: old
zh: old

en: A Night Listening to the River
zh: 一夜听河

en: She is gone. Before dawn we must build a pyre for her on the {{e_huozangqiu|श्मशान टीला}}—the ferryman's dead wife was burned in the same place, many years ago. The child still sleeps, knowing nothing.
zh: 她走了。天没亮，我们还要在{{e_huozangqiu|临水的土丘}}上为她筑起柴堆——船夫的亡妻，许多年前也是在同一处火化的。孩子还睡着，什么都不知道。

en: I did not sleep this night. The ferryman lay down in the goat-stall; I sat alone outside the hut and listened to the river all night.
zh: 这一夜我没有睡。船夫在羊厩里睡下了，我一个人坐在草舍门外，听了一整夜的河。

en: Strange: fragments of my whole life rose tonight: the sacrificial fire in my father's house, hunger in the forest of austerities, the city's lamps and wine, the golden cage in her garden… they came without order, all at once, as the river does not divide source from sea, and all is only 'now'. Now I rose to hear the child's breathing at the door; now I sat and heard the water.
zh: 怪得很，我这一生的片段，今夜全都浮了上来：父亲宅邸里的祭火，苦修林里的饥渴，大城的灯红酒绿，她园子里的那只金笼……它们不分先后，一起涌到眼前，像河水不分源头和入海，全都只是「现在」。我一会儿起身，到门边听听孩子的呼吸；一会儿坐下，听水声。

en: I remember she once said she wished to give her garden to the order. She did it. In her life she could take, and she could let go; I have spent a whole lifetime on the lesson of 'letting go'.
zh: 我还记得，她从前说过，想把花园献给僧团。她真的做到了。她这一生，拿得起，也放得下；我却在「放下」这门课上，修了整整一辈子。

en: My friend said I had suffered, yet sorrow had not entered my heart. He asked why I did not grieve. Yes—why?
zh: 朋友说我受了苦，可悲伤并没有进到我心里。他问我为什么不悲伤。是啊，为什么呢？

en: I was once rich, once happy; now that she is gone I am not poorer but richer—my son has come back to me. This is what she left me with her last breath.
zh: 我曾经富有，曾经快乐；如今她不在了，我非但没有变穷，反而更富有了——我的儿子回到了我身边。这是她拼着最后一口气，留给我的。

en: The river sang all night. Near dawn I understood: it was not weeping for her; it was singing life itself—some come, some go, the river is still the river. I touched the child's hair and rose to carry the first bundle of wood.
zh: 河水唱了一夜。天快亮时我懂了：它不是在哭她，它是在唱生命本身——有人来，有人走，河还是河。我摸了摸孩子的头发，起身去搬第一捆柴。

en: The man who sat outside the hut all night.
zh: 在草舍外坐了一整夜的人。

en: He has just seen the child's mother away.
zh: 刚送走了孩子的母亲。

en: old
zh: old

en: The Listener
zh: 倾听者

en: The night was deep. In this hut by the {{e_linzhongdukou|वन की नाव-घाट}} the oil-lamp was nearly spent; the river's sound came in at the window. The guest had just told the half of his life, and suddenly felt that this night's telling had been more easing than twenty years of thought.
zh: 夜深了。这间{{e_linzhongdukou|渡口}}边的草舍里，油灯快要烧干，河声从窗外进来。客人刚讲完自己的半生，他忽然觉得，这一夜的讲述，比自己二十年的沉思还要痛快。

en: I thank you. And I have one more thing to thank you for—you know so well how to listen. Very few know the art of listening; I have walked most of my life and never met a listener like you. In this I would learn from you.
zh: 谢谢你。我还有一件事要谢你——你太懂得倾听了。极少有人懂得倾听的艺术，我走了大半辈子，没遇见过一个像你这样的听者。这方面，我要向你求教。

en: It is not hard. But you need not learn it from me.
zh: 这并不难。不过，你无须跟我学。

en: From whom, then?
zh: 跟谁学？

en: The river. The river taught me to listen. You will learn it from the river too. The river knows everything; a man can learn everything from it.
zh: 河水。是河水教会我倾听的。你也将从它那里学会。河水懂得一切，人可以从它那里学会一切。

en: The river… what can it teach?
zh: 河水……能教人什么？

en: You have already learned one thing: to go downward, to sink, to seek the deepest ground. You who were rich and honoured are now an oarsman on the {{e_duchuan|नाव}}—that is going downward. Later you will learn another thing.
zh: 你已经学会了一样：勉力走向低处，沉下去，去找那最深的底层。从前富有显贵的你，如今成了摇{{e_duchuan|渡船}}的桨手——这就是向低处去。往后，你还会学会另一件事。

en: What other thing?
zh: 另一件事是什么？

en: It is too late; we should sleep. I cannot tell you—you will find it yourself, perhaps you already know. I am not a learned man; I cannot speak, and I cannot think. I only know how to listen, how to honour. If I could speak, I should long ago have been a teacher. I am only a ferryman; my work is to take people across.
zh: 天太晚了，该睡了。我无法告诉你——你自己会发现的，或许你已经知道了。我不是有学问的人，不会讲，也不会想。我只懂得倾听，懂得敬重。要是我会讲，我早就去当先生了。可我只是个船夫，我的活计是渡人过河。

en: To take people across… thousands have gone over in your boat; do they all listen to the river as you do?
zh: 渡人过河……千万人从你船上过去，他们都像你一样听河吗？

en: No. To thousands of travellers this river is only an obstacle on the road. They hurry for trade, for money, to wedding-feasts, on long journeys, turning in {{e_lunhui|संसार}}—life circling between birth and death; men call it Samsara. The river blocks their way; the ferryman's work is to take them over quickly.
zh: 不。对千万过客来说，这条河只是路上的障碍。他们为生意奔忙，为金钱奔忙，赴婚宴，赶远路，在{{e_lunhui|轮回}}里一圈圈地转——生命在生死之间循环流转，人们管这叫轮回。河挡了他们的路，船夫的活儿，就是快快把他们渡过去。

en: Are there no exceptions?
zh: 就没有例外？

en: There are. Among thousands, a few dozen, perhaps only four or five—to them the river is not an obstacle. They can hear it speak, and will listen with the heart. To them the river becomes a holy thing, as it is to me.
zh: 有。千万人里，有那么几十个，也许只有四五个——河对他们不是障碍。他们听得见河水说话，肯用心去听。河对他们，就成了神圣的东西，就像对我一样。

en: I should like to be one of those four or five.
zh: 我也想成为那四五个。

en: You will. Sleep, my friend. The river is outside the window; it is not in haste to teach you, and you need not be in haste to learn.
zh: 你会的。睡吧，我的朋友。河在窗外，它不急着教你，你也别急着学。

en: The lamp went out. Listening to the water beyond the window, he felt for the first time that 'listening' too was a craft—a harder craft than rowing.
zh: 灯灭了。他听着窗外的水声，第一次觉得「倾听」也是一门手艺——比摇船更难的手艺。

en: The man who teaches 'listening' seldom speaks much himself.
zh: 教「倾听」的人，自己从不多话。

en: The ferryman.
zh: 船夫。

en: Before the Garden Gate
zh: 园门之前

en: I followed all the way to the city's edge. I did not find my son, yet I stopped before a garden gate—{{e_mingjihuayuan|गणिका का उद्यान}} I knew. Decades ago it had been the most beautiful place in the city, belonging to a {{e_mingji|गणिका}}—courtesans then were independent women of wealth and art, who chose their own lovers. Now the garden has been given to the order; yellow-robed monks come and go in the shade.
zh: 我一路追到了城郊。儿子没找到，我却在一座园子门前停住了脚——{{e_mingjihuayuan|这座园子}}，我认得。几十年前，它是大城最美的去处，属于一位{{e_mingji|名妓}}——那时候的名妓，是有财有艺、自己挑选情人的独立女子。如今园子已经献给了僧团，黄衣的僧人们在树荫下来来往往。

en: I stood a long time. The past rose scene by scene: a young Samana with long hair standing outside the garden, covered in dust, seeing her in the palanquin for the first time; the kiss under the pavilion; later the fine clothes, the counting-house, the dice, the songbird in the golden cage… my whole life, it seemed, was written on the road before me.
zh: 我站着，站了很久。往事一幕幕涌上来：长发的年轻沙门站在园外，满身尘土，第一次看见轿中的她；亭子下的那个吻；后来是华服、账房、骰子、金笼里的歌鸟……我的一生，原来都写在眼前这条路上。

en: Yet what have I come here to do? To pursue my son. And if I catch him? Drag him back to the hut he hates? Standing at the garden gate I suddenly saw how foolish the thought was: I cannot help him. I cannot force my own way of living upon his fate.
zh: 可我到这里来做什么？追我的儿子。追上了又怎么样？把他拽回那间他恨透了的草舍？站在园门前，我忽然看清这个念头有多蠢：我帮不了他。我不能把我自己的活法，强加到他的命上。

en: I love him; the love is like a wound, and it still hurts. But a wound should not rot in the heart; it should slowly close. He came into the world to walk his own road; I should go back to my river.
zh: 我爱他，这爱像一道伤口，此刻还在疼。可伤口不该在心里烂着，它应当慢慢愈合。他来这世上走他自己的路，我也该回我的河边去了。

en: At the garden gate a monk set two bananas before me. Only then did I feel the thick dust in my hair, and did not know how many hours I had stood there. I smiled at him, picked up the bananas, turned, and walked toward the ferry. The river was still waiting for me.
zh: 园门口，一位僧人在我面前放下了两只香蕉。我这才发觉，自己头发上的灰已经积了厚厚一层，也不知在这里站了几个时辰。我冲他笑笑，捡起香蕉，转过身，往渡口的方向走。河还在那里等我。

en: The man who stopped at the gate of his old lover's garden.
zh: 在旧情人的园子门口停下脚步的人。

en: The one he pursued was his son.
zh: 他追的人是他的儿子。

en: old
zh: old

en: Send Him Back to the City
zh: 送他回城

en: That night, when the shards of the bowls had been swept away and the child was asleep, the old man drew his friend outside and sat on the log by the river. He said more this evening than in the whole past year.
zh: 那天夜里，碗碟的碎片扫干净了，孩子睡下了。老人把朋友拉到门外，在河边的树干上坐下。他今晚的话，比过去一年都多。

en: Forgive me. As a friend I must speak with you. I know you are anxious, and much troubled. Truthfully, {{e_xiaoxiduo|सिद्धार्थ का पुत्र}} troubles you greatly—and me as well.
zh: 原谅我。作为朋友，我必须跟你谈一谈。我知道你很担忧，很苦恼。说实话，{{e_xiaoxiduo|你的儿子}}让你十分苦恼——也包括我。

en: He is still a child. He has just lost his mother.
zh: 他还是个孩子。他刚没了母亲。

en: That little bird is used to another life, another nest. He did not flee wealth in disgust, as you once did; he was dragged from that nest. I have asked the river many times; the river laughed, laughed at the foolishness you and I have done. Water returns to water; the young remain young. Your son will not be happy here.
zh: 那只小鸟，习惯了另一种生活、另一个巢。他不是像你当年那样，带着厌恶逃离财富的；他是被硬拖出那个窝的。我多次问过河水，河水笑了，笑你我做的蠢事。水终归于水，年轻人终归是年轻人。你的儿子在这里，不会快乐。

en: How can I part from him? Give me more time. I am fighting for him; I want to enter his heart. I will win him with love and patience. One day the river will speak to him too—the river is calling him as well.
zh: 我怎能与他分离？再给我些时间。我在为他而战，我要走进他的心里去。我要用爱和宽容赢得他。有朝一日，河水也会和他说话——河水也在召唤他。

en: Of course the river is calling him too. But do you and I know to which road he will be led? His heart is proud and hard; he will suffer much, and err much. Tell me: do you discipline him? Is he obedient to you? Have you beaten him, punished him?
zh: 当然，河水也在召唤他。可你我知不知道，他将被引到哪条路上去？他的心傲慢而冷酷，他会吃许多苦，犯许多错。告诉我：你管教他吗？他对你顺从吗？你打过他、罚过他吗？

en: No. I cannot do those things.
zh: 不。这些我做不到。

en: I know. You do not blame him, do not punish, do not command—you know gentleness is better than severity, kindness better than force. Yet friend, might this not be another error of yours? Are you not binding him with love? Day after day, with your goodness and patience, making him more ashamed? You keep him in this hut, to live with two old men of the woods—our very heartbeats are unlike his. Is that not a punishment for him?
zh: 我知道。你不苛责他，不罚他，不命令他——你懂得宽和胜过严苛，仁爱胜过暴力。可是朋友，这难道不会是你的另一种错吗？你不是在用爱捆住他吗？不是日复一日，用你的善意和耐心，叫他更加难堪吗？你把他硬留在这草屋里，跟两个山野老头过日子——我们的心跳都和他不一样。这对他，难道不是一种刑罚？

en: What do you think… I should do?
zh: 你觉得……我该怎么办？

en: Send him back to the city. Send him to his mother's house—{{e_mingjihuayuan|गणिका का उद्यान}} has been given away, but there are still servants in the house. Give him to the servants, to teachers; let him meet other boys and girls; let him live in the world that is his. Have you truly never thought this?
zh: 送他回城。送回他母亲的宅第——{{e_mingjihuayuan|那座园子}}虽然献了出去，宅子里还有仆从。把他交给仆从，交给先生，让他见到别的少男少女，让他活在他所属的那个世界里。你真的从没这么想过？

en: You can see through my heart. I think it often. And yet—how is a boy so hard of heart to stand in the world? He will surely think himself above others, lose himself in pleasure and power, and walk his father's road again.
zh: 你能看透我的心。我常这么想。可是——像他这样心肠刚硬的人，怎么在世上立足？他一定会自命不凡，在享乐和权势里丢掉自己，重蹈他父亲的覆辙。

en: Ask the river, my friend! Do you truly think keeping him at your side can protect him? What father, what teacher, can stop a man from living his own life? Who protected that young Samana in those days? His father's piety, his teachers' precepts—none of it could stop him. Even if you died ten times for your son, you could not alter his fate by a hair.
zh: 去问一问河水，我的朋友！你真以为，把他拴在身边就能护住他吗？哪位父亲、哪位导师，能拦住他去过自己的生活？当年谁来佑护那个年轻的沙门？他父亲的虔诚、导师的训诫，全都拦不住他。你就算替儿子死十次，也改动不了他命运的一分一毫。

en: The old man had never spoken so many words in one breath. His friend thanked him kindly, went back to the hut with his head down, and could not close his eyes all night. All those reasons he had thought, all he understood—but stronger than reason was love. He had never loved anyone so wholly, so blindly, so painfully.
zh: 老人从未一口气说过这么多的话。他的朋友友善地道了谢，垂着头走回草舍，一夜没能合眼。那些道理，他全都想过，全都懂——可比理智更强的，是爱。他从没这样彻底地、盲目地、痛苦地，爱过一个人。

en: Give me more time. I cannot.
zh: 再给我些时间吧。我做不到。

en: Outside, the old man looked at the river and sighed softly. From that day both began a silent endurance—one enduring a son, the other a friend.
zh: 门外，老人望着河，轻轻叹了口气。从那天起，两个人都开始了一场无声的忍耐——一个忍耐儿子，一个忍耐朋友。

en: The one who urged him to 'send him back to the city'.
zh: 劝他「送他回城」的人。

en: The childless old man saw more clearly than the father.
zh: 无儿无女的老人，看得比父亲更清。

en: old
zh: old

en: Farewell, River
zh: 再会，河流

en: After that dusk of listening to the river, the hurt on his face faded. Life at the ferry went on: rowing, taking fares, mending the raft. Only the old man more and more often laid down his work and gazed into the woods. A few days later he stood up on the bank and looked a long time into his friend's eyes—eyes that held the same peace as his own.
zh: 听河的那个黄昏之后，他脸上的伤淡了。渡口的日子照旧：摇船，收船费，补竹筏。只是老人越来越常放下手里的活，望着林子出神。几天后，他在岸边站起来，久久看着朋友的眼睛——那眼睛里，有和自己一样的安详。

en: I have been waiting for this moment, my friend. Now that it has come, I may go.
zh: 我一直在等待这一刻，我的朋友。既然这一刻已经来了，我可以走了。

en: You are going? Where?
zh: 你要走？去哪里？

en: Into the woods, into the unity of all things. For a long time I have been the ferryman of this crossing; now it is finished. The {{e_duchuan|नाव}} is yours, the ferry is yours.
zh: 步入林中，步入万物的圆融统一里去。很久以来，我一直是这个渡口的船夫；如今，结束了。{{e_duchuan|渡船}}是你的了，渡口是你的了。

en: If you go, what of the ferry? What of the travellers?
zh: 你走了，渡口怎么办？行客怎么办？

en: The ferry has you. You are already a ferryman—a better one than I. The hut I leave you too: rice in the jar, the net on the beam, the oars behind the door.
zh: 渡口有你。你已经是船夫了——比我更好的船夫。草舍也留给你：米在缸里，渔网在梁上，桨在门后。

en: I will look after them, and after every one who crosses.
zh: 我会照看好它们，照看好每一个过河的人。

en: But I have so much still unlearned—the river's ten thousand sounds becoming one, and I have only just heard that word…
zh: 可我还有许多没学会——河水万音归一，我才刚刚听见那个字……

en: You have already heard {{e_om|ॐ}}—the one into which ten thousand voices flow, the sound of perfection. He who has heard it needs no teacher. The river itself will teach you, as it once taught me, sentence by sentence, never weary.
zh: 你已经听见了{{e_om|唵}}——万千声音汇成的那一个，圆满之音。听见它的人，不需要老师了。河自己会教你，就像它当年教我，一句一句，从不厌烦。

en: In the days to come, whom shall I learn from?
zh: 往后的日子，我学谁去？

en: Learn from the river. All I have I learned from it. It has more patience than I, and more honesty.
zh: 学河。我这点东西，都是从它那里学来的。它比我有耐心，也比我诚实。

en: That year you ferried me across and took nothing. I have not yet repaid you.
zh: 当年你渡我过河，分文不取。我还没报答你。

en: You stayed and became my apprentice, and kept me company all these years. That is the repayment.
zh: 你留下作了我的徒弟，陪了我这么多年。这就是报答。

en: Then shall we… meet again?
zh: 那我们……还会再见吗？

en: Do not be sad. Look at the river—it bids farewell to every wavelet, and never turns back.
zh: 别难过。你看那河水——它告别每一朵浪花，从不回头。

en: I am not sad. I am… unwilling to let go.
zh: 我不是难过。我是……舍不得。

en: If you cannot let go, ferry it to the other shore. Ferry others, and ferry yourself. —Farewell, my hut. Farewell, my river. Farewell, my friend.
zh: 舍不得，就把它渡到对岸去。渡人，也渡自己。——再会，我的草屋。再会，我的河流。再会，我的朋友。

en: I understand. Go. Thank you—thank you for teaching me to listen.
zh: 我知道了。去吧。谢谢你——谢谢你教我倾听。

en: I will see you to the edge of the woods.
zh: 我送你到林边。

en: No need. A ferryman does not see a ferryman off. Keep your ferry well.
zh: 不必。船夫不送船夫。看好你的渡口。

en: He bowed deeply to the man about to leave. The old man turned into the woods, his step peaceful, his face as if it shone. That night he sat alone on the log and listened to the river the whole night through—among ten thousand sounds, what he heard was no longer farewell, but perfection.
zh: 他朝那即将离去的人深深鞠了一躬。老人转身走进林子，步态安详，面容像放着光。那天夜里，他独自坐在树干上听河，听了整整一夜——千万种声音里，他听见的不再是送别，是圆满。

en: The man who left the ferry to his apprentice.
zh: 把渡口留给徒弟的人。

en: The ferryman.
zh: 船夫。

en: old
zh: old

en: Seeking and Finding
zh: 追寻与寻见

en: The ferry was short one ferryman, yet the days went on. One day an old monk came to the crossing. He was of {{e_sengtuan|गौतम का संघ}}—those in yellow robes who begged with bowls and wandered the four directions preaching the teaching. He had heard that a saintly ferryman lived by this river, and came out of his way to see. He had kept the precepts all his life, yet his heart was never at peace—he felt he had not yet found.
zh: 渡口少了一个船夫，日子却照样过。一天，一位老僧来到渡口。他是{{e_sengtuan|佛陀的僧团}}里的人——那些披黄衣、托钵乞食、云游四方宣讲佛法的僧人。他听人传说这条河边住着一位船夫圣贤，便绕路来见。他守了一辈子戒律，心里却始终不安宁——他觉得自己还没有寻见。

en: Old man, please ferry me across.
zh: 老丈，请渡我过河。

en: At the other shore the old monk was in no haste to go; he only studied the old man who poled.
zh: 船到对岸，老僧却不急着走，只打量着撑船的老人。

en: You have ferried so many pilgrims and monks, and never tired. Are you—perhaps a seeker yourself?
zh: 您渡了那么多朝圣者和僧侣，从不厌烦。您莫非——也是一位求道者？

en: Venerable sir, you are already old, and you wear the robe of a disciple of {{e_qiaodamo|गौतम}}. Do you still call yourself a seeker?
zh: 尊贵的先生，您已经年迈，又身穿{{e_qiaodamo|世尊}}弟子的僧袍。您还把自己称作求道者吗？

en: I am old, it is true. But I have never ceased seeking, and I never shall—it seems to be my fate. You too, I think, have sought. Friend, can you give me some guidance?
zh: 我的确老了。但我从未停止追寻，我永远不会停止——这好像是我的命。我看您似乎也曾追寻过。朋友，您能指点我一二吗？

en: What I can say may be of little worth. And yet—perhaps you have sought too much, and so cannot find.
zh: 我能说的，未必有什么价值。不过——也许您追寻得太多，因而无从寻见。

en: What does that mean?
zh: 这是什么道理？

en: When a man is seeking, his eyes see only what he seeks. Bound to the goal, he discovers nothing, obtains nothing. Seeking means having a goal; finding means freedom, openness, the laying down of every goal. Venerable one, you may well be a seeker—you pursue so hard that you cannot see what is before you.
zh: 一个人有所追寻，眼里就只看得见他所追寻的东西。他执迷于目标，便无所发现、无所获得。追寻，意味着有目标；寻见，意味着自由、包容，摒弃一切目标。尊贵的人，您也许正是一位追寻者——您追得太急，反倒看不见眼前的事实了。

en: I still do not understand. You mean…?
zh: 我还是不明白。您的意思是……？

en: Venerable one, many years ago you came to this river and found a man asleep. You sat beside him and watched over his sleep—yet you did not know the sleeper, [[NPC2]].
zh: 尊贵的人，许多年前，您曾来到这条河边，发现一个酣睡的人。您在他身边坐下，守着他的睡眠——可您当时并没有认出那个酣睡的人，[[NPC2]]。

en: The old monk stood as if struck by lightning, staring hard at the ferryman.
zh: 老僧如遭雷击，呆住了，死死盯着船夫。

en: Is it you? …Is it you? This time, still, I did not know you. My old friend! You have changed—you are a ferryman now?
zh: 是您？……竟然是你？这一回，我还是没能认出你来。我的老朋友！你变了——你如今，是个船夫了？

en: Yes, I have become a ferryman. Men change, put on one garment and then another; so have I. You are welcome. Tonight, stay in my hut.
zh: 是的，我成了一名船夫。人都会变，换一件又一件衣裳，我也是。欢迎你。今晚，请你在我的草舍里住下。

en: Good! I have a bellyful of questions for you; tonight I shall not sleep, I fear.
zh: 好！我有一肚子的话要问你，今夜怕是不睡了。

en: Ask. The night is long, and the river does not sleep.
zh: 问吧。夜还长，河也睡不着。

en: Then tell me of yourself first—how did you come to be a ferryman?
zh: 那先说说你自己——你怎么就做了一个船夫？

en: That night the old monk slept in the bed the other ferryman had left empty. The heaviest question in his heart he kept for the next morning.
zh: 那一夜，老僧睡在另一位船夫空出的床上。他心里最重的那个问题，留到了第二天清晨。

en: The man who sought all his life, and the man who had long since 'found'.
zh: 追寻了一生的人，和早已「寻见」的人。

en: The old monk in all his life took refuge with only one teacher.
zh: 老僧这一生只皈依过一位导师。

en: old
zh: old

en: old
zh: old

en: The Seventeenth Boat on the Mound
zh: 土丘上的第十七条船

en: {{e_jiamola|कमला}} said we should be gone only a few days. She said a very great man outside the city was about to die; she wanted to see him once, and we should be back in time for the rains. She told me to wear my strongest shoes. I would not walk; I wanted a palanquin; she said we could not take a palanquin this time.
zh: {{e_jiamola|母亲}}说，我们只去几天。她说城外有一位很了不起的人快要不在了，她想赶去看他一眼，回来正好赶上雨季。她叫我穿最结实的那双鞋。我不肯走路，我要坐轿子；她说这一趟不能坐轿。

en: The thing in the grass I saw first. Grey, short, like a bit of broken rope. I opened my mouth and did not shout. When I did shout, she had already cried out and was sitting on the ground. I have told this to no one. I think it over and over: if I had been half a breath sooner?
zh: 草里那条东西，是我先看见的。灰的，短的，像一截断绳子。我张了张嘴，没有喊出来。等我喊的时候，她已经叫了一声，坐在地上了。这件事我谁也没有讲。我一遍一遍地想：要是我早半口气呢？

en: They carried her into a hut. It smelled of fish; the floor was earth, the bowls were coarse. Before dawn she did not speak any more. The next day they stacked wood on the {{e_huozangqiu|श्मशान टीला}}, stacked it very neatly, as if for one of their own.
zh: 他们把她抬进一间草屋。屋里有鱼腥味，地是土的，碗是粗的。天亮以前她就不说话了。第二天，他们在{{e_huozangqiu|临水的土丘}}上堆柴，堆得很整齐，像给自家人堆的。

en: I sat on the mound and counted the boats that passed on the river. Seventeen the first day, nine the second. They brought food; I would not eat; they brought it a second time, and I still would not. Hunger hurts, but if I eat it is as if I have given in. The wind blew ash onto my legs; I did not brush it off.
zh: 我坐在土丘上数河里过去的船。头一天十七条，第二天九条。他们端饭来，我不吃；端第二回，我还是不吃。饿是难受的，可我一吃，就好像认了。风把灰吹到我腿上，我也不拍。

en: Neither of them hurried me. One only sat far off braiding rope; the other came and went, setting a bowl of water where I could reach it. The more they did this, the more I understood: they did not mean to send me away.
zh: 他们两个都不催我。一个只是坐得远远的编绳子，一个走过来又走开，把水碗放在我够得着的地方。他们越是这样，我越是明白：他们不打算送我走。

en: The white-haired man says he is my father. I have no father. I had a house with walls around it, a gardener who picked fruit for me, a bird that could copy speech. Once I am sure of the road back to the city, I shall go at once.
zh: 那个白头发的人说他是我父亲。我没有父亲。我有过一座带院墙的宅子，有过一个替我摘果子的花匠，有过一只会学人说话的鸟。我只要弄清回城的路怎么走，我立刻就走。

en: He sat on the mound counting the boats that passed, and would not eat a mouthful.
zh: 他坐在土丘上数河里过去的船，一口饭也不肯吃。

en: Eight years old, his mother just dead at the ferry; he will not acknowledge the white-haired man.
zh: 八岁，母亲刚死在渡口，他不肯认那个白头发的人。

en: The River Would Not Carry Him
zh: 河不肯载他

en: In the afternoon no one crossed. [[NPC1]] untied the rope, jumped onto the {{e_duchuan|नाव}}, and rammed the pole into the water as the grown men did. The bow swung, and the boat drifted sideways downstream. The old man [[NPC2]] on the bank watched, neither shouting nor running.
zh: 午后无人过河。[[NPC1]]解开缆绳，跳上{{e_duchuan|渡船}}，学着大人的样子把篙子往水里一插。船头一偏，横着往下游漂去。岸上的老人[[NPC2]]看着，没有喊，也没有跑。

en: Stop staring! Come and give me a push!
zh: 别看了！过来推我一把！

en: I cannot. The water runs down; the more you fight, the farther it takes you. Take in the pole, and wait for it to come in of itself.
zh: 推不得。水往下走，你越挣，它带你走得越远。把篙子收起来，等它自己靠。

en: The boat turned twice in a bend and struck a stand of reeds and stopped. The old man rolled up his trousers, went in, held the boat with one hand and lifted the child ashore with the other. The child flung off his hand, shaking all over—whether from cold or from anger, he could not have said.
zh: 船在河湾里打了两个转，撞上一丛芦苇停住了。老人卷起裤脚下水，一手扶船，一手把孩子抱上岸。孩子甩开他的手，浑身发抖，说不清是冷还是气。

en: This boat is bad.
zh: 这船是坏的。

en: The boat is good. You were missing one thing in your hands—you used a pole, and the river is so deep the pole cannot reach the bottom.
zh: 船是好的。是你手里少了一样东西——你插的是篙，河这么深，篙子够不到底。

en: Then you take me. I will pay.
zh: 那你送我。我出钱。

en: Pay?
zh: 出钱？

en: That {{e_shuangselan|द्विवर्णी टोकरी}} hung at the bow is full of the coppers people give for the crossing. I have counted; it is enough. I will pay double—take me back to the city, to the street with the stone lions; I know my own door.
zh: 船头挂的那只{{e_shuangselan|双色小篮}}，里头全是过河人给的铜板。我数过，够了。我出双倍——你把我送回城里，送到有石狮子的那条街，我认得我家的门。

en: That is not my money.
zh: 那不是我的钱。

en: The basket hangs on your boat.
zh: 篮子挂在你的船上。

en: The basket hangs on my boat; the money is the river's. The river will give again tomorrow; I cannot spend it for the river today.
zh: 篮子挂在我的船上，钱是河给的。河明天还要给，我不能今天就替它花掉。

en: You two old things, one playing deaf, one playing stupid.
zh: 你们两个老东西，一个装聋，一个装傻。

en: The old man was not angry. He wrung out his wet trousers, crouched, fished a long wooden thing from the boat's bottom, laid it across his knees, and wiped it slowly with a cloth.
zh: 老人没有生气。他把湿裤脚拧干，蹲下来，从船底捞起一支长长的木器，横放在膝上，用布慢慢擦。

en: Why don't you beat me? He doesn't beat me because he dares not. And you?
zh: 你为什么不打我？他不打我，是因为他不敢。你呢？

en: If I beat you, you would have a ready reason to hate me. As it is, if you hate me you must invent a reason yourself—inventing reasons is tiring, and when you are tired you think of other things.
zh: 我打了你，你就有现成的理由恨我了。你如今恨我，还得自己去想理由——想理由是很累的，累了就会去想别的事。

en: I am not tired.
zh: 我不累。

en: Mm. When I was young I was not tired either.
zh: 嗯。我年轻的时候也不累。

en: If my mother were still here, one word would have bought your boat.
zh: 我母亲要是还在，一句话就买下你这条船。

en: If she were still here, there would be no need to buy. If she asked, I would ferry her just the same.
zh: 她要是还在，也不必买。她开口，我照样渡。

en: The child waited for the next sentence; the old man said no more. He held out the long thing in his hands and showed him how to grip with both hands, how to use the waist. The child turned his head, as if too lazy to learn. Yet he remembered every word: without this one thing, the boat goes nowhere.
zh: 孩子等着下一句，老人却不说了。他把手里那件长家伙递过来，教他两只手怎么握、腰怎么使力。孩子偏过头去，一副懒得学的样子。可他把每一句都记住了：这一样东西不在，船就哪儿也去不了。

en: One wanted to buy a passage home with other people's money; the other said it was the river's money.
zh: 一个想用别人的钱买一趟回城的船，一个说那是河的钱。

en: The small one is eight; the old one has poled all his life, and never loses his temper.
zh: 小的那个八岁；老的那个撑了一辈子船，从不生气。

en: The Thing Thrown into the Water
zh: 扔进水里的那一样

en: Yesterday at dusk I roared out all the words I had saved for months. Then I ran, and sat in the woods till midnight. When I came back a lamp was still left in the house, and a mango on the window-ledge. I did not touch it.
zh: 昨天傍晚我把攒了几个月的话全吼了出来。吼完我就跑了，在林子里坐到半夜。回来的时候屋里还留着灯，窗台上放着一只芒果。我没有碰它。

en: I waited till they slept. The two old men slept deeply, their breathing long and short, like two ropes wrongly tied. I felt my way to the bow, took down the {{e_shuangselan|द्विवर्णी टोकरी}}, crouched in the moonlight and counted the coppers one by one into my pocket—enough to last ten days in the city, find my own door, and need no one.
zh: 我等他们睡熟。两个老人睡得很沉，呼吸一长一短，像两条搭错了的绳子。我摸到船头，取下那只{{e_shuangselan|双色小篮}}，蹲在月亮底下把铜板一枚一枚数进衣兜——够我在城里撑上十天，找到我家的门，那就用不着谁了。

en: Crossing was easier than I had thought. Hands low, waist turning: the old man who would not take me had taught me that himself. In the middle the water pushed hard; I clenched my teeth and poled through, shoes wet to the ankles. On the other shore I tied the boat, then untied it; thought, and tied it again.
zh: 过河比我想的容易。手要低，腰要转，这是那个不肯送我的老人自己教我的。水在中间那一段推得很凶，我咬着牙撑过去，鞋子湿到脚踝。到了对岸，我把船拴好，又解开；想了想，还是拴回去。

en: Then I did one thing: I broke the {{e_chuanjiang|चप्पू}} one by one and threw them all into the water. Not because I feared he would follow—if he meant to, he could bind a raft and still catch me. I wanted him to spend himself for me once, to sweat, to curse an ugly word. In all my life I have never heard him curse anyone, not once.
zh: 然后我做了一件事：我把船上的{{e_chuanjiang|船桨}}一根根折断，全扔进了水里。不是怕他追——他要追，扎个筏子也能追得上。我是要他为我费一次力，出一次汗，骂一句难听的话。我这辈子还没听他骂过人，一次也没有。

en: A little white was just showing in the sky when I took the road to the great city. Far on I looked back once: a point of lamp still burned by the hut. He will come looking for me. He will keep looking. But he will not beat me—that I have always known.
zh: 天边刚有一点白，我上了那条通往大城的路。走出很远我回过一次头：草屋那边有一点灯，还亮着。他会来找我。他会一直找我。可他不会打我——这一点，我早就知道了。

en: He counted the coppers, crossed the river, and before he left broke one thing on the boat and threw it in.
zh: 他数着铜板过了河，走之前把船上的一样东西折断扔了。

en: He wanted to force that father who never lost his temper to lose it once.
zh: 他想逼那个从不发火的父亲发一次火。

en: A Farewell Stood Through the Night
zh: 一夜站成的告别

en: In ancient India twenty-five hundred years ago, a man's station was fixed at birth; the highest rank was called Brahmin—hereditary priest-nobles. Siddhartha, raised in this house of mango trees, could recite all the scriptures, perform the whole rite of bathing and sacrifice, and argue with a sharp tongue. Everyone in the town loved him; his friend Govinda honoured him above all others, and was content to be his shadow.
zh: 两千五百年前的古印度，人一出生就定下终身，最高的一等叫作婆罗门——世代相传的祭司贵族。在这座种满芒果树的宅第里长大的悉达多，会背诵所有经文，会做整套沐浴与献祭，辩论起来言辞锋利。城里人人都爱他，好友侨文达敬他胜过任何人，甘愿做他的影子。

en: Yet he was not happy. Father and teachers poured wisdom into his vessel, and the vessel was never full; bathing could wash the dust from the body, not the trouble from the heart; the sacrificial fire, however beautiful, could not reach the source he sought. The scriptures said there was an eternal, undying Atman in the depths of the heart—and that road his father could not walk for him, nor his teachers, nor the sacred verses.
zh: 可是他并不快乐。父亲与师长把智慧灌进他的容器，容器却总也盛不满；沐浴洗得掉身上的尘土，洗不掉心里的烦恼；献祭的烟火再美，也到不了他要找的那个源泉。经典说人心深处有一个永恒不灭的真我，而这条路，父亲不能替他走，师长不能，神圣的诗篇也不能。

en: So in the deep of night he went into his father's room and asked leave to go and become a Samana—an ascetic who leaves the family and walks naked in austerity. The father was displeased and went back to sleep; the son stood where he was, hands folded, unmoving. Three times in the night the old man rose, and from a small window saw that still figure in the moonlight; anger, anxiety, and fear turned little by little into understanding: this son could no longer be kept.
zh: 于是深夜，他走进父亲的房间，请求离家去做沙门——离弃家庭、赤身苦行的修道者。父亲不悦，回房睡下；他却叉手立在原地，一动不动。老人一夜三次起身，从小窗里看见月光下那个纹丝不动的身影，怒气、焦虑与恐惧，一点点变成了明白：这个儿子，已经留不住了。

en: At first light the father put out his hand and gently touched his shoulder: Go, into the forest; if you find the bliss of heaven, come back and teach me. The young man tried to step; his body swayed—he had stood in that place a whole night. The legs might tremble; the heart must not.
zh: 天光初亮，父亲伸出手，轻轻抚上他的肩：去吧，到林中去；若寻得天堂之乐，回来教给我。年轻人试图迈步，身体摇晃了一下——他已经在原地站了整整一夜。腿可以战栗，心不许。

en: I will stand till dawn, till noon, till night—until he himself gives me leave to go.
zh: 我会站到天明，站到中午，站到夜晚——站到他亲口放行为止。

en: At the next daybreak he left the still-sleeping town alone. At the last hut on the town's edge a crouched figure slipped from the shadows and followed in silence: Govinda had not slept; he had already decided—wherever you go, I will go, as your companion, your servant, your shadow.
zh: 第二天破晓，他独自离开还在沉睡的城邑。走到城边最后一间小屋，阴影里闪出一个蜷曲的身影默默跟上：侨文达一夜没睡，早想好了——你走到哪里，我就跟到哪里，做你的伙伴，做你的仆人，做你的影子。

en: The Narcotic, and Rumours of the Awakened One
zh: 麻醉剂与觉醒者的传闻

en: The years in the forest were counted in hunger. One meal a day, a fast of fourteen days, then of twenty-eight; standing in the heat, standing in the rain, lying in thorns. In meditation his soul left the body, became a hawk over the bamboo, a rotting jackal on the sand—yet each time he woke again in sun and moonlight, and was himself again. The elders praised him as the fiercest in practice, the quickest to learn; in his heart he quietly doubted what it all meant.
zh: 林中的岁月，是用饥饿计算的。一天一餐，禁食十四天，又禁食二十八天；烈日下站，雨中站，荆棘丛里卧。冥想中，他的灵魂飞出躯壳，化作掠过竹林的苍鹰，化作沙滩上腐烂的死豺——可每一次，他都在日光与月华中再度清醒，再度成为自己。长老夸他修得最狠、学得最快，他心里却在暗暗怀疑这一切的意义。

en: After three years he admitted to himself: meditation, breath, fasting, were only narcotics for fleeing the self. A herdsman drinking a few bowls of rice-wine in a tavern, sinking into sleep, was fleeing in the same way; drown the self a hundred times, and on waking it still sat waiting in its place.
zh: 三年后，他对自己承认：冥想、调息、斋戒，说穿了不过是逃离自我的麻醉剂。牧牛人坐在小酒馆里喝几碗米酒，昏然睡去，做的是同样的逃离；把自我灌醉一百次，醒来时它还是坐在原地等他。

en: The place he reaches with one bowl of wine, we need a month of hunger and a month of sitting to reach.
zh: 他一碗酒就到得了的地方，我们要饿上一个月、打坐一个月。

en: On the alms-road he said heavier words to Govinda: the eldest is sixty and has not attained Nirvana; you and I will grow old the same way, and fall equally short—we are only going in circles; perhaps learning itself is Atman's greatest enemy. Govinda still believed the path was a rising spiral; yet watching that back that was always half a step ahead, he felt panic for the first time: this man, he would soon not be able to follow.
zh: 乞食的路上，他对侨文达说出更重的话：长老六十岁了仍未证得涅槃，你我也将一样老去，一样够不着——我们不过是在兜圈子，也许学识正是真我最大的敌人。侨文达还信这条路是一个上升的螺旋，可他望着前方那个总快半步的背影，第一次生出恐慌：这个人，他快跟不住了。

en: Just then rumours poured into the jungle: a sage of the Sakya clan had appeared, had conquered the world's sufferings, stilled the wheel of rebirth; people called him the Awakened One. Some praised, some mocked. And the subject of the rumours was at that moment silently begging in the lanes of Savathi—in his view, rumours themselves grow old and lose their teeth; what mattered was that those who slept under the trees this year were twice last year's number.
zh: 恰在这时，传闻涌进丛林：一位释迦族的智者出现了，征服了世间众苦，止息了再生之轮，人们称他为觉者。有人赞美，有人嘲讽。而传闻的主角此刻正在舍卫城的巷子里默默托钵——在他看来，传闻自己会老、会掉牙；真正要紧的是，今年在树下过夜的人，比去年多了一倍。

en: The two young men asked leave to quit the jungle and hear the teaching with their own ears; the eldest flew into a rage. Siddhartha came near the old man and gazed into his eyes with complete attention—the very art the old man had taught, year by year, with his own hands—and the old man suddenly fell silent, bowed, and stammered a blessing. The morning mist broke; the two set out empty-handed toward the rumoured city.
zh: 两个年轻人请求离开丛林去亲耳听法，长老暴怒。悉达多走近老人，专注一意地凝视他的眼睛——那门老人亲手一年年教出的本事，叫老人忽然沉默，鞠躬，结结巴巴地祝福。晨雾散开，两人空着双手上路，走向那座传闻中的大城。

en: After the Teaching, Each His Own Road
zh: 听法之后，各走各的路

en: Asking along the way, the two young Samanas entered Savathi and spent the night in a garden monastery a rich elder had given to the Buddha. At dawn, among hundreds of monks in the same dress, Siddhartha knew that man at a glance: yellow robe, alms-bowl, no pride in him; face, gait, even every finger showed perfection, and his smile was no different from an infant's. He spoke not a word; merely walking so quietly, he was known.
zh: 一路打听，两个年轻沙门走进舍卫城，在一位富长者献给佛陀的园林精舍里歇脚过夜。清晨，几百个装束相同的僧侣中间，悉达多一眼认出了那个人：黄衣托钵，毫无骄慢之态，面容、步态乃至每一根手指都显示着圆满，微笑与婴孩并无不同。他不讲一句话，光是这样安安静静地走路，就叫人认出了他。

en: Before the evening teaching, the Buddha told an old monk to prepare one more robe: the shy come earliest and stand last; when I entered the garden I saw one who had already stood a long while. Indeed, when the teaching ended, Govinda, always shy, pressed forward, his voice tight but without hesitation, and asked to take refuge. He was received.
zh: 说法的黄昏之前，佛陀吩咐老比丘多备一件衣：羞怯的人来得最早，站得最后，我进园时看见一个，已经在那儿站了很久。果然，讲法结束时，那个一向羞怯的侨文达挤上前去，声音发紧却没有犹豫，请求皈依。他被接纳了。

en: That night the two friends walked long in the woods, lay down, and long could not sleep. One wept; the other only blessed him again and again: you have always followed me a step behind; now at last you have taken a step of your own; may you go on by this road, may you find salvation. At the next dawn the old monks gave out yellow robes; Govinda put one on and embraced the friend of his youth—from then he stayed, and was no one's shadow.
zh: 当夜，两个朋友在林中长久地漫步，躺下，又久久无法入眠。一个哭了；一个只是再三祝福：你一直落后一步跟从我，如今终于独立走出了一步，愿你沿这条路走下去，愿你得到救赎。第二天清晨，老僧分发黄衣，侨文达披上它，拥抱了青年时代的朋友——从此他留了下来，不再是谁的影子。

en: Siddhartha, the next day, spoke plainly to the Buddha's face: Your teaching is unified, crystal-clear, yet there is a small crack—the experience you yourself attained cannot be given in words, and so no one can be saved by doctrine; I will leave all creeds and teachers, and go on by my own road. The Buddha listened in silence, eyes lowered, with a faint smile.
zh: 悉达多却在第二天向佛陀当面直言：您的教义圆融统一，水晶般明晰，可有一个小小的裂缝——您亲自证悟的体验，无法以言辞传授，所以任何人也无法通过教义得到救赎；我要离开一切教条与导师，继续走自己的路。佛陀静静听完，眼光低垂，带着一丝微笑。

en: You are clever, Samana from afar; you know how to argue with skill. My friend—beware your own excess of cleverness.
zh: 你很聪明，远方来的沙门，你懂得如何巧妙地论说。我的朋友——提防你自己过分的聪明。

en: Leaving the garden, Siddhartha woke as from a long dream: he had meant to destroy the self and find Atman in the ruins, and had for that very reason lost himself all along the way. From today everything was reversed—learn from the self, take the self as teacher. He looked about: the world was gold, deep blue, green, strangely beautiful; meaning was not behind things, but in the things themselves.
zh: 走出园林，悉达多大梦初醒：他一心想摧毁自我、在废墟上寻找真我，却恰恰因此一路丢失了自己。从今天起，一切颠倒过来——向自我学习，以自我为师。举目四望，世界金黄、湛蓝、碧绿，美得出奇；意义不在事物的背后，就在事物自身。

en: The Buddha watched that light-footed figure go out the garden gate. The missing corner, perhaps, was a door left for such a man.
zh: 佛陀目送那个脚步很轻的背影走出园门。缺的那一角，说不定正是给他这样的人留的门。

en: Across the River, a First Sight Outside the Garden
zh: 渡河入城，园外一见

en: Leaving the Buddha's garden, Siddhartha travelled alone several days, his heart light and bright: the world had suddenly become so beautiful—gold, deep blue, green—it had been there all along. At evening he came to a great river and lodged in the hut at the ferry; the ferryman shared bread, water, and mangoes, and at dawn poled him across. On the far shore he could not find a copper; the ferryman only smiled.
zh: 离开佛陀的园林，悉达多独自赶了几天路，心里又轻又亮：世界忽然变得这么美，金黄、湛蓝、碧绿，原来一直都在。傍晚他走到一条大河边，在渡口草舍借宿；船夫分给他面包、水和芒果，清晨撑筏渡他过河。到岸时他摸不出一个铜板，船夫只是笑。

en: I take no money from you. One day you will come and repay me. Water flows out and flows back; it always turns.
zh: 我不收你的钱。将来有一天，你自会来报答我。水流来流去，终会回转。

en: He took it for a joke, and entered the great city. By a beautiful unwalled garden outside the city he met a train of servants with gift-boxes, crowding round a fine palanquin; in it sat Kamala, the city's most famous courtesan, her small red mouth like a newly picked fig. As the palanquin passed he bowed deeply, and rising met those intelligent eyes—she nodded and smiled, then vanished into the garden.
zh: 他只当那是句玩笑，走进了大城。城外一座没有围墙的美丽园林旁，他遇见一队手捧礼盒的仆从，簇拥着一顶华轿；轿中端坐着这座城最有名的名妓伽摩拉，嫣红的小嘴像一枚新摘的无花果。轿子经过时，他深深躬身，起身正迎上那双聪慧的眼睛——她向他颔首微笑，随即消失在园林深处。

en: The servants' eyes came like needles. For the first time he looked at himself in earnest: tangled long hair full of dust, a ragged loincloth barely covering him. In the forest he had been proud of poverty; at this garden gate he suddenly felt himself only a beggar. So he changed his skin: shaved, combed, put on hair-oil, bathed in the river; the rice-cake he had begged he threw to a dog—from today he was no longer a beggar.
zh: 仆人的目光像针一样扎过来。他第一次认真打量自己：纠结的长发沾满尘土，一条破腰布勉强蔽体。在林中，他以贫穷为荣；在这座园子门前，他忽然觉得自己只是个乞丐。于是他给自己换了一张皮：剃须、梳发、抹上发膏，到河里沐浴；伸手乞来的米糕，他抛给了一条狗——从今天起，他不再是乞丐。

en: In this city where everyone had money and everyone loved money, a man who had thrown everything away felt, for the first time in his life, a clear wanting: fine clothes, costly shoes, a bag full of coin—so that he might walk into that garden with dignity, and see those eyes again.
zh: 这座人人有钱、也人人爱钱的大城，一个抛弃了一切的人，生平第一次有了清清楚楚的想要：华美的衣服、名贵的鞋子、满袋的钱财——想要堂堂正正地走进那座园林，再见到那双眼睛。

en: A Poem for a Kiss, Letters for a Living
zh: 以诗换吻，以字立足

en: The next day he waited, made new, at the garden entrance. In the pavilion Kamala named her terms: the young men who come to me all wear splendid clothes, costly shoes, scented hair, and bags full of money. What he offered in return were three arts she did not understand.
zh: 第二天，他焕然一新地候在园林入口。凉亭里，伽摩拉开出她的条件：到我这里来的年轻人，个个穿着华丽的衣服、名贵的鞋子，头发飘香，袋中装满金钱。他还的价，是三样她听不懂的技艺。

en: I can think, I can wait, I can fast.
zh: 我会思想，我会等待，我会斋戒。

en: He added an impromptu poem, and received a kiss—and in that kiss such rich learning: conquest, refusal, and temptation. She gave him a white robe and had a servant lead him out by winding paths. Only two days in the city, and he had already kissed the most beautiful woman in it.
zh: 他又补上一首即兴的诗，换了一个吻——那吻里竟藏着如此丰富的学问：征服、推拒，又是诱惑。她赠他一件白袍，让仆人领他沿迂回的小径离开。进城才两天，他已经吻过了全城最美的女人。

en: She opened the next door for him as well: Kamaswami, the city's richest merchant, was expecting his visit. Her only charge—be friendly to him, but do not be a cringing servant; I want you as his equal, or I shall be displeased.
zh: 她又替他推开下一扇门：城中最富有的商人湿瓦弥正期待他去拜访。她的叮嘱只有一条——对他友善，但不要作奴态十足的仆从，我要你作与他平等的对手，不然我会不高兴的。

en: In the great house the merchant fired questions: You are in some difficulty, are you not? You have nothing; what can you give? He answered without hurry, the same answer: I can think, I can wait, I can fast; a man who can fast is not driven by hunger, and so can wait in peace. Given a contract to read, he missed not a word; asked to write, he took up the pen: Writing is beautiful, yet not so as thought; wit is beautiful, yet not so as patience. The merchant read it twice and at once kept him as a guest. The one being tested was unhurried; the one testing was the first to be moved.
zh: 豪宅里，商人连珠发问：你是陷入窘境了吧？你一无所有，拿什么付出？他答得不慌不忙，还是那个答案：我会思想，我会等待，我会斋戒；会斋戒的人不被饥饿驱赶，才能安安静静地等待。让他读契约，他一字不差；请他写字，他提笔写下：写作虽美，莫如沉思；机智虽美，莫如能忍。商人读了两遍，当即留他作客。应试的人不慌不忙，考校的人倒先动了心。

en: From then servants brought clothes and shoes, and important letters and papers were put in his hands. He treated trade as a game: the rules he learned in earnest; winning and losing he did not take to heart. Kamaswami sighed to an old friend: When he gains, he smiles; when he loses, he smiles, and sleeps like a child just the same. Someone suggested giving him a third of the profit, to let money stick to him—yet he turned and gave the share to the labourers at the harbour; if he lost, he made it up himself without a word, and went off to someone else's wedding-feast.
zh: 从此仆从送来衣服鞋子，重要的信件与文书都交到他手上。他把生意当游戏：规则认真学，输赢不入心。湿瓦弥对老友叹气：赚了，他笑一笑；蚀了，他也笑一笑，照样睡得像个孩子。有人出主意把赢利的三分之一分给他，让钱沾上他的身——可他转头把分红散给码头上的苦力，赔了则一声不吭自己补上，掉头又去赴人家的喜宴。

en: The merchant rose at midnight to count the books; he slept like a child. There are such men in the world: everything in their hands, and nothing taken in earnest.
zh: 商人半夜爬起来数账，他睡得像个孩子。这世上竟有这样的人：什么都握在手里，又什么都不当真。

en: The Fall, and the Death of a Songbird
zh: 沉沦，与一只歌鸟的死

en: Those years Siddhartha lived a double life. At the appointed hour he went to Kamala in fine clothes and costly shoes, and from a child who knew nothing of love became her proudest pupil; in trade he remained an outsider—his master careful and anxious, sleepless three nights over a cargo, while he treated it as a game. Sent to a village for rice, he found the rice already bought; he was not angry, simply stayed, feasted the farmers, went to a wedding, and came back content.
zh: 那几年，悉达多过着一种双重的生活。约定的时刻，他穿华服名鞋去拜访伽摩拉，从对情爱一无所知的孩子，学成了她最得意的弟子；生意场上他却始终是个局外人——东家谨小慎微，为一批货三夜合不上眼，他只当游戏。派他去村落收稻米，稻子早被买走，他不恼，索性住下款待农夫、赴了一场婚宴，满意而归。

en: One dusk after the lessons were done, Kamala named what they shared: You are the finest of all my lovers; one day I should like a child with you; yet you are still a Samana—you do not truly love me, you love no one. He admitted it: I am much like you; you too have no power to love. Ordinary people can love, like leaves rolling in the wind; they themselves are like stars, which the wind cannot reach, and which cannot reach the leaves' joy.
zh: 课业学完后的黄昏，伽摩拉说破了两人共同的底细：你是我所有情人中最优秀的一个，将来我愿意与你要一个孩子；可你仍旧是一个沙门——你不真正爱我，你不爱任何人。他承认：我很像你，你也没有爱的能力。平凡的人们能够爱，像落叶在风中翻滚；他们像星辰，风吹不到，也够不着落叶的快乐。

en: You do not truly love me—you love no one, is that not so?
zh: 你不真正爱我——你不爱任何人，难道不是吗？

en: Year by year the world seeped in like damp into a dying trunk. The wheel of abstinence, the wheel of thought, turned slower and slower; he learned to give orders, fine clothes and wine, and learned to gamble: thousands on a throw, and only when a great stake hung did he feel a little fear, sweet and terrible, and know he was still alive. Kamaswami was at first glad he would at last fret over money; later he could not smile—he did not love money, he hated it. The man in the mirror grew older and uglier by the day; the smiles grew fewer.
zh: 一年一年，尘俗像湿气钻进垂死的树干。禁欲之轮、思维之轮越转越慢，他学会了发号施令、华服美酒，也学会了赌钱：一掷成千上万，只有大笔赌金悬着时，才感到一点可怕又甜美的焦虑，感到自己还活着。湿瓦弥起初高兴他终于肯为钱着急，后来笑不出来——他不是爱钱，他是恨钱。镜子里的人一天比一天衰老、丑陋，笑容越来越少。

en: The height of the fall was a dream. On the last night Kamala asked him to tell the Buddha's story again, and said she wished to give her garden to the order; she held him, tears in her eyes, as if to wring a last drop of sweetness from this passing joy. That night he came home drunk, and at dawn dreamed the songbird in the golden cage stiff at the cage's floor—he started in terror, his heart wrung hard: as if all that was good and of worth in him had been thrown away with that dead bird.
zh: 沉沦的顶点是一个梦。最后一夜，伽摩拉请他再讲佛陀的故事，说想把花园献给僧团；她眼中含泪抱紧他，仿佛要从这无常的快乐中榨取最后一滴甜蜜。当夜他醉酒归家，破晓时梦见金笼里那只歌鸟僵死在笼底——他大惊失色，心像被狠狠绞住：仿佛身上所有善良和有价值的东西，都随这只死鸟一起抛弃了。

en: He sat under the mango tree a whole day, reviewing his life from the start: had he left all those people only to become such a rich man as this? Night fell; he rose and said farewell to the tree, the garden, the city, and did not return. She was not surprised at the news; she only went to the golden cage, opened the little door, and let the bird go.
zh: 他在芒果树下坐了整整一天，从头回顾一生：难道他离开所有那些人，就是为了成为今天这样一个富人吗？夜幕降临，他起身与树、与花园、与这座城市道别，一去不返。她得知消息并不惊讶，只走近金笼打开小门，放走了那只鸟。

en: A Word That Sounded by the Water
zh: 水边响起的一个字

en: Leaving the city, Siddhartha wandered into the woods and came to that same great river. That life he had tasted to the point of nausea; nothing in the world could comfort him. He held the great tree on the bank and looked down at the water; the cold in it mirrored the emptiness in his soul. He spat at his own reflection, let go, and gave himself to death—and in that instant a syllable that had slept twenty years sounded from the depths of the soul.
zh: 离开城市，悉达多彷徨入林，来到当年那条大河边。那种生活，他已经品味到了恶心的程度；世上再没有任何东西能给他安慰。他搂住岸边的大树俯视水波，水里的冰冷正映着他灵魂中的空虚。他向自己的倒影唾了一口，松开手，投向死亡——就在这一瞬，灵魂深处传来一个沉睡了二十年的音节。

en: Om—the first word a Brahmin's child can chant from memory, meaning perfection.
zh: 唵——婆罗门的孩子记事起就会念的第一个字，意思是圆满。

en: The word sounded lightly; he saw all at once how foolish he had been, sank down under the tree, and fell into a deep, dreamless sleep. He had meant to drown in this river; and in truth that old, weary, despairing self had already drowned in it.
zh: 那个字轻轻一响，他猛然看清自己有多愚蠢，跌坐在大树下，沉入深沉无梦的酣睡。他想自溺于这条河；而实际上，那个衰老、疲惫、绝望的他，已经溺在了河里。

en: When he woke, a yellow-robed old monk was sitting before him, watching—a monk of the order, travelling, who had seen him sleep so deeply and stayed. Thanks, farewell—yet he smiled and spoke the other's name: Govinda. The old monk started: the most beloved friend of his youth, and he himself had twice failed to know him. He looked at this seeker in rich clothes, scented with perfume, bowed, and went on his way.
zh: 醒来时，一位黄衣老僧正坐在面前守护——僧团的僧人外出游化，见他睡得深沉，便留了下来。道谢、道别，他却微笑着唤出了对方的名字：侨文达。老僧大吃一惊：青年时代最敬爱的朋友，自己竟两次没有认出。他打量着这个衣着华贵、洒着香水的求道者，躬身行礼，重新踏上了旅程。

en: And in the city Kamaswami turned the ledger: not a coin touched, not a discrepancy. He would never accept the other explanation—that a man would lay down house, clothes, and trade, and for what? That room he left empty a whole year.
zh: 而在城里，湿瓦弥翻着那本账：钱一文没动，分毫不差。他始终不肯认另一种说法——一个人把宅子、衣裳、生意全撂下，凭什么？那间屋子，他空了整整一年。

en: Meeting Again at the Ferry, Year upon Year
zh: 渡口重逢，年复一年

en: Many years later a white-haired old man in rich clothes came on foot, alone, to the ferry. The ferryman knew him: more than twenty years before he had ferried a young Samana across for nothing—today that word, you will come and repay me, was fulfilled. The old man would give his fine robes as fare, only asking to stay: a helper first, then an apprentice; I must learn to row. A smile rose from the depths of the ferryman's wrinkles: You are welcome; my name is Vasudeva.
zh: 许多年后，一位衣着华贵的白发老人独自步行来到渡口。摇船的船夫认出了他：二十多年前，他曾免费渡过一个年轻的沙门过河——今天，那句你自会来报答我，应验了。老人愿把华服送给船夫抵船费，只求留下：先作帮手，再作学徒，我一定要学会摇船。船夫皱纹深处漾开了笑：欢迎你，我叫维稣德瓦。

en: That night the oil-lamp in the hut was nearly spent; the guest told his whole life the whole night through: birth, study, wealth, the fall, down to despair by the river and the waking. The ferryman only listened—did not interrupt, did not press, did not blame, did not praise; this night's telling was more easing than twenty years of thought. He asked to learn the art of listening; the ferryman said: You need not learn it from me—the river taught me to listen.
zh: 当夜，草舍里的油灯快要烧干，客人把自己的一生讲了整整一夜：出身、求学、富贵、沉沦，一直讲到河边的绝望与醒来。船夫只是听——不打断，不追问，不责备，也不称赞；这一夜的讲述，比二十年的沉思还要痛快。他求教倾听的艺术，船夫说：你无须跟我学——是河水教会我倾听的。

en: And waking from that sleep by the river, he was light as a newborn infant: so a man must taste his own foolishness and sin with his own hands, let them rot, let them die, before he can become a child again; the songbird in the breast was not dead, it had only been mute many years.
zh: 而河边的这一觉醒来，他轻快得像新生的婴儿：原来人非得把那些愚蠢和罪孽都亲手尝过一遍，烂掉，死掉，才能重新变成孩子；胸口那只歌鸟并没有死，它只是哑了许多年。

en: Life settled at the ferry: mending boats, shaping oars, planting rice, weaving baskets; he liked whatever he did, and learned quickly. At dusk after work the apprentice asked the master: Have you also learned this secret from the river—that time does not exist at all? The river is everywhere at once, and each place is only now; life too is a river; boy, man in his prime, old man, are only three stretches drawn by illusion.
zh: 日子在渡口定了下来：补船、削桨、插秧、编篮，他做什么都喜欢，学什么都快。收工的黄昏，徒弟问师父：你是否也从河水学到了这个秘密——世上根本不存在时间？河水在同一时刻无处不在，每一处都只有现在；生命也是一条河，少年、壮年、老年，只是幻象划出来的三段。

en: What is spoken is leftover rice; what one tastes for oneself is the meal. So I do not speak. I only sit and listen with you.
zh: 讲出来的，都是剩饭；自己尝到的，才是饭。所以我不讲，我只陪你听。

en: The doctrine he understood; the ledger in his heart still ran, year after year: the twenty years wasted in the city, still reckoned when he woke at night. A white-haired old man helped aboard by his son; he set a stool for them—after leaving home he had never gone back; in which year his father ceased to be, he had never even asked.
zh: 只是道理懂了，心里那本账还在一年一年地记：城里糟蹋的二十年，夜里醒来仍要算一遍。白发的老人被儿子扶着上船，他替他们摆好板凳——他离家后再没有回去过；父亲是哪一年不在的，他连问都没有问过。

en: Years ran past like the river. Travellers slowly noticed a strange thing: the smiles of the two ferrymen, old and younger, grew more and more alike—the same unfolding from a thousand fine lines, the same peace. Many, boarding, asked: Are you brothers? The two only looked at each other and smiled.
zh: 岁月像河水一样流过去。行客们渐渐看出怪事：这一老一少两个船夫，笑容越来越像——同样从千百条细纹里漾开，同样的安详。许多人上了船就问：你们是亲兄弟吧？两人只是相视一笑。

en: Pilgrimage, Snakebite, Death at the Ferry
zh: 朝圣蛇咬，渡口死别

en: Many more years passed; news that the Awakened One was dying ran like wildfire, and the ferry did not rest from dawn to dusk. In the stream of people walked a mother and child: the mother had once given her garden to the monks, and this time brought the child to see the saint on his last journey. Resting in the woods, a small snake darted from the grass—the child saw it first; he opened his mouth and did not shout.
zh: 又过了许多年，那位觉者病重的消息像野火一样传开，渡船从早到晚没有停过。人流里有一对步行的母子：母亲从前把自家的园子赠给了僧人，这次带着孩子，要送圣人最后一程。林间歇息时，草丛里窜出一条小蛇——那条东西，是孩子先看见的，他张了张嘴，没有喊出来。

en: The cry reached the ferry; the old ferryman lifted the fainting woman and went toward the hut. The other old man lighting the fire by the stove raised his head, knew her at a glance, and in that instant knew who the child was. He looked at that small face again and again: eight years old, the knitted brow plainly hers when she was young—he has her eyes. Only one road remained: to raise this motherless child, day by day.
zh: 呼声传到渡口，摇船的老人抱起昏迷的妇人往草舍走。炉边生火的另一个老人抬起头，一眼认出了她，也就在那一瞬，明白了那孩子是谁。他一遍遍看那张小脸：八岁了，皱起眉的样子分明是她年轻时的样子——他有一双她的眼睛。剩下的路只有一条：把这个没了娘的孩子，一天一天养大。

en: The wound was washed, yet the herbs could keep her only a little while. Kamala woke and knew the man bending over her: You have grown old, your hair is white, yet you are more like that young Samana who once stood outside my garden than you were when you left the city. She had meant to see the Buddha a last time, and met her old lover first; she felt that this too was good, as good as seeing the other. When life receded slowly from her eyes, he reached out and gently closed them.
zh: 伤口洗净了，草药却只能留住她一会儿。伽摩拉醒来，认出俯身望着她的人：你老了，头发白了，可你比离开大城时，更像当年站在我园外的那个年轻沙门。她本想去看佛陀最后一眼，却先见到了旧时的情人；她觉得，这也很好，和见到另一位，一样的好。生命从她眼睛里缓缓退去时，他伸出手指，轻轻合上了她的眼睛。

en: That night he did not eat; he sat alone outside the door and listened to the river all night: fragments of a whole life rose without order, as the river does not divide source from sea. At dawn the two old men built a pyre on the mound by the water—the ferryman's dead wife had been burned in the same place, many years before.
zh: 夜里他没有吃饭，独自坐在门外，听了一整夜的河：一生的片段不分先后全浮了上来，像河水不分源头和入海。清晨，两个老人在临水的土丘上筑起柴堆——摇船老人的亡妻，许多年前也在同一处火化。

en: For days the child sat pale on the mound, counting the boats that passed: seventeen the first day, nine the second. The food they brought he would not eat—if he ate, it was as if he had given in. He had seen the snake first; this he told no one. The more they sat with him at a distance, the more he understood: they did not mean to send me away. The white-haired man says he is my father—I have no father.
zh: 孩子一连几天脸色苍白地坐在土丘上，数河里过去的船：头一天十七条，第二天九条。端来的饭他不吃——一吃，就好像认了。那条蛇是他先看见的；这件事，他谁也没有讲。他们越是远远地陪着，他越是明白：他们不打算送我走。那个白头发的人说他是我父亲——我没有父亲。

en: Two Broken Bowls, Flight with Broken Oars
zh: 两只碎碗，断桨而逃

en: The funeral gave way to days, yet the days would not soften. Coarse rice he tasted and pushed away; the fruit trees the old man grew behind the hut he stripped bare; one evening, over a trifle, two rice-bowls smashed hard on the floor. The father crouched, picked up the shards one by one, swept them clean, and as usual warmed the rice again, saying nothing. The child hoped more that he would lose his temper—answering every rudeness with a smile was, in the child's eyes, the most hateful cunning. And the father would rather have the trouble than the ease of having no child.
zh: 葬礼让位给日子，日子却不肯软下来。粗米饭尝一口就推开，屋后老人种的果树被洗劫一空；一天傍晚，就为一点小事，两只米饭碗狠狠摔在地上。父亲蹲下身，一片一片把碎片捡干净，扫净了，又像往常一样把饭热上，什么也没说。孩子倒更盼着他发火——对每一次无礼都报以微笑，在孩子眼里简直是最可恨的狡诈。而父亲宁愿要这烦恼，也不要没有孩子的快活。

en: The child again asked the old ferryman to take him back to the city, offering double fare—the coppers in the two-coloured basket at the bow he had already counted. The old man said, That is not my money; it is the river's; then laid an oar across his knees and showed him how to grip with both hands, how to use the waist. The child turned his head, pretending laziness, yet remembered every word: without this one thing, the boat goes nowhere.
zh: 孩子又去求老船夫送他回城，愿出双倍船钱——船头那只双色小篮里的铜板，他早数过了。老人说，那不是我的钱，是河给的；又顺手把一支船桨横在膝上，教他两只手怎么握、腰怎么使力。孩子偏过头去装懒，却把每一句都记住了：这一样东西不在，船就哪儿也去不了。

en: Water returns to water; the young remain young. Are you not binding him with love? Send him back to the city.
zh: 水终归于水，年轻人终归是年轻人。你不是在用爱捆住他吗？送他回城吧。

en: That night the old ferryman drew his friend outside and said more than in the whole past year. The friend thanked him kindly, went back to the hut with his head down, and could not close his eyes all night. All those reasons he had thought, all he understood—but stronger than reason was love: he had never loved anyone so wholly, so blindly, so painfully.
zh: 那天夜里，老船夫把朋友拉到门外，说了比过去一年都多的话。朋友友善地道了谢，垂着头走回草舍，一夜没能合眼。那些道理他全都想过，全都懂——可比理智更强的，是爱：他从没这样彻底地、盲目地、痛苦地，爱过一个人。

en: The powder that had gathered for months at last went off one evening: the child roared out a bellyful of contempt in his father's face and rushed out; next morning the bed was empty, the two-coloured basket at the bow was gone, the ferry-boat was gone. The empty boat lay on the far shore; every oar had been broken and thrown into the river.
zh: 积压了几个月的火药，终于在一个傍晚炸了：孩子当着父亲的面吼出一肚子轻蔑，夺门而出；第二天清晨，床空了，船头那只双色小篮不见了，渡船也不见了。空船泊在对岸，船桨全被折断扔进了河里。

en: Not because I feared he would follow. I wanted him to spend himself for me once, to sweat, to curse an ugly word—in all my life I have never heard him curse anyone.
zh: 不是怕他追。我是要他为我费一次力，出一次汗，骂一句难听的话——我这辈子还没听他骂过人。

en: The two old men bound a raft and crossed; the father followed all the way to the city's edge, yet stopped at an old garden gate—decades ago he, long-haired, covered in dust, had stood here and seen her in the palanquin for the first time. He suddenly saw how foolish the thought was: he could not help his son, could not force his own way of living upon his son's fate. He picked up the two bananas a monk had set down, and turned back to the ferry.
zh: 两个老人扎竹筏过河，父亲一路追到城郊，却在一座旧园门前停住了脚——几十年前，长发的他曾满身尘土站在这里，第一次看见轿中的她。他忽然看清这念头有多蠢：他帮不了儿子，不能把自己的活法强加到儿子的命上。他捡起僧人放下的两只香蕉，转身回渡口。

en: Ten Thousand Sounds Become Om, the Last Bow
zh: 万音成唵，最后一拜

en: The wound still ached. One day he poled to the other shore again; the dry-season river was strangely loud—the river was laughing, mocking this old man; the reflection in the water was like his own father: in those days he too had forced his father to let go. He came back and confessed to the old man, pouring out all he had never told anyone; as he spoke he felt that the listener was plainly the river itself.
zh: 伤口还在隐隐作痛。一天他又撑船到对岸，旱季的河水响亮得奇怪——河水在笑，嘲笑这个老人；水里的倒影竟像他自己的父亲：当年他也是这样逼着父亲放手。他回来向老人忏悔，把从未对人讲过的一切和盘托出；讲着讲着，他觉得那倾听者，分明就是这条河本身。

en: The old man took his hand and led him to sit by the river: You have heard its mockery, but you have not yet heard everything—listen further! On the water rose the images of father, himself, the son; three generations flowed into one river; joy and sorrow, good and evil, ten thousand voices became one great song. And when his heart no longer seized any one of them, only a single word remained in the song: Om. The wound began to close; he no longer fought his fate.
zh: 老人拉起他的手，领他到河边坐下：你已经听见了它的嘲笑，可你还没有听见一切——再听！水面上浮起父亲、他自己、儿子的形象，三代人汇进同一条河；喜与悲、善与恶，千万种声音合成一首大歌。而当他的心不再抓住其中任何一个，大歌里只剩下一个字：唵。伤口开始愈合，他不再和自己的命运抗争了。

en: A few days later the old man looked a long time into his eyes: I have been waiting for this moment. Now that it has come, I may go. He turned into the woods, his step peaceful, his face as if it shone. That night he listened to the river alone the whole night through; among ten thousand sounds, what he heard was no longer farewell, but perfection.
zh: 几天后，老人久久看着他的眼睛：我一直在等待这一刻。既然它来了，我可以走了。他转身走进林子，步态安详，面容像放着光。那天夜里，他独自听了一整夜的河，千万种声音里，听见的不再是送别，是圆满。

en: Farewell, my hut; farewell, my river; farewell, my friend.
zh: 再会，我的草屋；再会，我的河流；再会，我的朋友。

en: Many years later an old monk came out of his way to the ferry—he had heard that a saintly ferryman lived by this river. The ferryman said: Perhaps you have sought too much, and so cannot find; seeking means having a goal, finding means freedom. In the moment they knew each other the old monk stood as if struck by lightning: this time, still, he had not known his friend. On the morning of parting the old monk asked a last question: Have you some creed that upholds your life?
zh: 许多年后，一位老僧绕路来到渡口——他听人传说这条河边住着一位船夫圣贤。船夫说：也许您追寻得太多，因而无从寻见；追寻意味着有目标，寻见意味着自由。认出彼此的那一刻，老僧如遭雷击：这一回，他仍没认出自己的朋友。临别清晨，老僧问出最后一个问题：你可有某种信条，扶助你的生活？

en: Wisdom cannot be spoken. Knowledge can be taught; wisdom cannot.
zh: 智慧无法言传。知识可以传授，智慧不能。

en: Already leaving, he turned back: Tell me a little more; my road is often hard and dark. The ferryman smiled and said softly: Bend closer; kiss my forehead. In the instant the old monk bent, he saw a thousand forms arising and passing; and over it all lay a transparent smile—the very smile of the Blessed One, which he had gazed upon all his life. He wept, and bowed deeply to the ground.
zh: 临走了他又回过身：再讲一点吧，我的路常常又难又黑。船夫微笑着，轻声说：俯身过来，吻我的前额。老僧俯下身的那一瞬，看见千百种形象生生灭灭；而这一切之上，笼着一层透明的微笑——那正是他毕生瞻仰的、世尊的微笑。他泪流满面，深深一躬到地。
